title: Leverage Church History for Ministry
summary: Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan discuss how pastors can use church history to strengthen their preaching, encourage their congregations, understand historic Christian beliefs, and learn from believers who have gone before us.
summary_zh: 马特·斯梅瑟斯特（Matt Smethurst）和利根·邓肯（Ligon Duncan）讨论了牧师如何利用教会历史来强化讲道、激励会众、理解历史上的基督教信仰，并向先辈信徒学习。
title_zh: 利用教会历史开展事工
content: Why should pastors care about church history, and how can they use it in everyday ministry? Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan discuss why church history is more than a subject for scholars. They share practical ways pastors can draw from Christian biographies, historical events, and the early church to strengthen their preaching and help their congregations grow in faith. title: How to Preach to Workers
summary: The New Testament offers two paradigms for how preachers can consider workers in their teaching.
summary_zh: 新约提供了两种范式，说明传道人如何在教导中考虑到工人。
title_zh: 如何向工人传福音
content: I still remember the first time I heard a sermon on God’s design for work. Pastor Colin Smith was in a series working through the Ten Commandments, and he’d come to the fourth command about the Sabbath. I was expecting to hear challenging words about rest. So I was surprised when he spent the first half of his sermon talking about work. Because he’s a good exegetical preacher, Smith reminded us to pay attention to the part of the passage we might overlook: “Six days you shall labor, and do all your work . . .” (Ex. 20:9). For 16 minutes, Smith preached about God’s design for work. He explained how God modeled work in creation, crafting and making our world like a builder, engineer, and artist. And since humans were created in the likeness of this God, our labors are a significant part of what it means to represent him in the world. Then he started naming regular kinds of work—such as the school crossing guard who creates a zone of safety and protection for children. He shared example after example, even naming those who are were unemployed and looking for work as engaging in a form of dignified labor. They can please God as they trust him to provide and remain diligent to seek out what’s next. At the time, I was working a summer landscaping job between semesters at seminary. I took the job because it was necessary, not because I found it personally fulfilling or spiritually significant. I’d been subconsciously wanting to be done with mowing lawns and picking weeds so I could get back to the important work of studying Scripture. But God used Smith’s sermon to reorient my ordinary labor. Preaching with workers in mind is vital to shepherding a congregation. It reminds church members that work is a primary context for discipleship and helps them work out the implications of God’s Word where they spend a large portion of their time. The New Testament gives two paradigms for how preachers can consider workers in their teaching. Work as an Illustration of the Kingdom As the eternal, perfect Son of God, Jesus isn’t only Savior and Lord but also the most brilliant teacher the world has ever heard. Therefore, as preachers, we take his pedagogy seriously even as we learn his precepts and mimic his practices. Jesus often proclaims the good news by igniting people’s imaginations and explaining eternal truths in concrete realities, including the body (Matt. 6:22; 7:3–5; 24:7–8), nature (Matt. 6:28–29; Mark 11:23; Luke 17:6), and food (Matt. 13:33; John 6:35, 53–56). But Jesus’s most consistent metaphor for the truths of the kingdom is work and workers. Klaus Issler’s survey reveals that of the 37 parables in the Synoptic Gospels, 32 reference work or workers, representing 22 different work roles. In 25 of the parables, work is a main part of the storyline. Here are examples: The farmer sows the seed (Matt. 13). The faithful manager gives the servants of the household food at the proper time (Luke 12:42). Even an unjust judge will give a persistent widow justice (18:1–8). The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). A king going into battle should take counsel to see if he’s strong enough before he a ttacks (Luke 14:31). When Jesus describes what it meant to follow him and live in his kingdom, why does he use the ordinary language of work and workers? First, God’s self-disclosure is often wrapped in the language of work. For instance, he’s portrayed as a composer and performer (Deut. 31:19), a tentmaker (Job 9:8), a garment maker and dresser (29:14), a shepherd (Ps. 23:1–4), a builder (Prov. 8:27–31), a metalworker (Isa. 1:24–26), a potter (31:9), and a farmer (Hos. 10:11). If God is the original worker, it makes sense that the whole realm of work can teach us his ways. If God is the original worker, it makes sense that the whole realm of work can teach us his ways. 我还记得我第一次听到关于上帝设计工作的布道。 科林·史密斯牧师在"十诫"系列中工作, 我希望听到关于休息的富有挑战性的话。 他上半场讲道工作时 我感到惊讶

由于他是一个优秀的传教士,史密斯提醒我们注意我们可能忽略的那段话:"六天你必须努力,并做你所有的工作."(前20:9). 16分钟,史密斯宣扬上帝的工作设计. 他解释了上帝如何塑造我们的世界 像一个建筑师、工程师和艺术家

由于人类是在这个上帝的相似之处创造的, 我们的劳动是世界中代表他的意义的重要部分. 然后,他开始点名从事常规工作,例如学校越野警卫,为儿童创造一个安全和保护的地区。

他举了个例子,甚至将那些失业和寻找工作的人命名为从事一种有尊严的劳动。 他们可以取悦上帝, 因为他们相信上帝提供, 当时我在神学院的暑期园林设计工作

我接受这份工作是因为有必要,而不是因为我发现这份工作是个人的满足或精神意义。 我潜意识地想要完成割草和摘草, 但上帝用史密斯的布道来调整我的普通劳动。 向工人宣讲对牧羊人至关重要。

它提醒教会成员,工作是门徒活动的主要背景,帮助他们解决神话的影响,在那里他们花费了大量的时间. "新约"为传教士如何在教学中考虑工人给出了两种范式.

发挥王国的作用 耶稣不仅是救世主, 因此,作为传教士,我们在学习他的戒律和模仿他的做法时,也认真对待他的教学方法.

耶稣经常通过点燃人们的想象力和在具体现实中解释永恒的真理来宣告好消息,包括身体(Matt 6:22;7:3–5;24:7–8),自然(Matt 6:28–29;Mark 11:23;Luke 17:6)和食物(Matt 13:33;John 6:35,53–56). 但耶稣对王国真理最一致的比喻是工作和工人.

Klaus Issler的调查表明,在Synoptic福音书中的37个比喻中,有32个参考工作或工人,代表着22个不同的工作角色. 在25个比喻中,作品是故事情节的主要部分. 以下是例子:农民播种(Matt.13). 忠诚的经理在适当的时候给家庭食物的仆人(公爵12:42).

即使是不公正的法官也会给守寡者一个持久的公正(18:1-8)。 善牧者为羊舍命(约翰10:11). 一个参战的国王应该接受建议, 当耶稣描述追随他并生活在他的王国的意义时,他为什么使用普通的劳动和工人语言?

首先,上帝的自我披露常常用工作语言包扎。 例如,他被描绘成作曲家和表演者(德国31:19)、帐篷匠(约旦9:8)、制衣和梳妆师(29:14)、牧羊人(Ps.23:1-4)、建筑师(Prov.8:27-31)、金属工人(Isa:1:24-26)、锅工(31:9)和农民(Hos:10:11)。

如果上帝是最初的工人,那么整个工作领域可以教我们他的方法是有道理的. 如果上帝是最初的工人,那么整个工作领域可以教我们他的方法是有道理的. 第二,耶稣作为一名普通工人可能花费了近6倍于他在公共部委中花费的年头,可能是石匠,或者经营一个S.

title: In the Darkness, Christmas Shines a Light
summary: The general revelation of God’s created order—darkness and light, night and day—primes every created thing to know they need light, a salvation from outside themselves.
summary_zh: 神所创造的秩序——黑暗与光明、黑夜与白昼——的普遍启示，使每一受造物都认识到自己需要光明，需要来自自身之外的拯救。
title_zh: 在黑暗中，圣诞节照亮光明
content: Read For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but the LORD will arise upon you, and his glory will be seen upon you. And nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising. (Isa. 60:2–3) Reflect There’s something about a sunrise. It wakes the world. Unlike the jarring blare of an alarm clock, a sunrise quietly whispers “Wake, O sleeper” with the graceful love of a parent rubbing a sleeping child’s back. When the sun rises, the slumbering stir to life. We’ve just spent seven or eight hours dead to the world. Then the sunrise triggers in us what looks like a resurrection. We rise. Certain flowers—daisies, poppies, and the aptly named morning glories—open their blossoms at the sun’s rising. Little by little, empty streets fill and quiet houses stir. Drawn to the warmth and energy of the just-unveiled sun, we transition from rest to work, stillness to activity. Drawn to the warmth and energy of the just-unveiled sun, we transition from rest to work, stillness to activity. It’s not surprising that the sun is an oft-used metaphor for God. For he, too, resurrects the dead. He, too, is the Giver of life and growth. He, too, draws all things to himself—such as the trees, which by nature grow upward, toward the sun, their branches like arms raised in perpetual worship. This is the created order. All things were made to be drawn to and sustained by the sun. We were made to be alive insofar as we live, grow, and flourish by solar energy. So too with God. We’re in darkness and death without him. As he bestows his grace on us, we rise to new life. We’re able to grow. Like the sunflower blossom, which turns to follow the sun wherever it’s positioned in the sky, we’re created to look to the Lord, who “will arise upon [us], and his glory will be seen upon [us]” (Isa. 60:2). In a world of darkness, we ache for the light. We wait for the sunrise. All nations, all kings, all people share this in common. The horizon each of us looks to—the nature of the “new day” we await—may be different: A new job. A remodeled home. A regime change. But only the sunrise of Christ will eternally satisfy. His is “the true light, which gives light to everyone” (John 1:9). Isaiah’s prophecy was fulfilled in him. Only the sunrise of Christ will eternally satisfy. The general revelation of God’s created order—darkness and light, night and day—primes every created thing to know they need light, a salvation from outside themselves. The special revelation of Christ reveals a truer light than even the sun: the light that is our eternal life, the light the darkness will never overcome (v. 5), the light that will one day end night as we know it (Rev. 22:5). Respond How is God’s glory seen in your life? How are you reflecting his beauty? In contrast to those who dwell in darkness, how does your life reflect 1 Thessalonians 5:5: “You are all children of light, children of the day. We are not of the night or of the darkness”?

我们每个人期待的地平线——我们等待的 " 新日 " 的性质——可能不同:新的工作。 一座重修的故乡. 政权更迭. 但只有基督的日出才能永远满足. 他的作品是“真正的光,它为每个人带来光明”(约翰1:9)。 以赛亚的预言在他身上得到了实现. 只有基督的日出才能永远满足

真主所创造的秩序——黑暗和光明,昼夜——的启示,使每一个被创造的事物都明白,他们需要光明,这是外部的拯救。 基督的特别启示揭示出比太阳更真实的光芒:即我们永恒生命的光芒,黑暗永远不会战胜的光芒(v. 5),即我们所知道的一天末夜的光芒(Rev.22: 5).

响应 上帝的荣耀在你的生活中是如何显现的? 你怎么反映他的美丽? 与那些生活在黑暗中的人不同,你的生活如何反映一个塞萨洛尼亚人5:5:“你们都是光明的孩子,是白天的孩子。 我们不是在黑夜中,也不是在黑暗中。”

title: How to Fire Someone at a Christian Organization
summary: If managers do their jobs well, believe that God is sovereign, and bring the love of Christ even into hard conversations, everyone will be better off.
summary_zh: 如果管理者能做好自己的工作，相信神掌管一切，即使在艰难的谈话中也能流露出基督的爱，那么每个人都会受益。
title_zh: 如何在基督教组织中解雇某人
content: Over the course of my career, I’ve participated in more than 190 exits of employees, whether I was coaching a manager, planning upstream, sitting in on calls, or orchestrating layoffs. Each time was tough. Parting ways with an employee is one of the heaviest things a manager does. Doing it both clearly and kindly takes a lot of preparation and emotional regulation. In a faith-based workplace, these decisions can be even more surprising and hurtful, because managers try to spare the discomfort of a conversation about performance under any number of banners of being “kind.” How should we think about this as Christians who manage other Christians? Why Good Work Is Important A church’s mission is to spread the good news of Jesus, create ways for people to know him more deeply, and love our neighbors. A Christian nonprofit’s purpose is adjacent—to provide mercy, justice, evangelism, or discipleship while pointing people to Christ and their local church. This work happens through ministry and outreach staff, but also through effective operations. Doing this work takes all types of roles: pastors, administrators, and ministry coordinators; managers, accountants, and musicians; executive admins, facilities operators, and IT teams. Much of what it takes to run a church or Christian organization happens outside the hours of direct ministry. To do any of this well, churches and nonprofits must hire capable people who can effectively perform their duties and steward the mission. When managers in a secular workplace don’t hire wisely, I’ve seen the result in poor functional performance, departmental infighting, disengagement, acrimonious exits, and abuse of company resources. In a faith-based organization or church, you may get a mix of this and something worse: the spread of the gospel can be compromised too. Upstream Work for Managers As a manager, if you notice someone isn’t performing well, the best time to start talking about it isn’t at the exit conversation. It’s way upstream from that. Your core job is to ensure your people have what they need to be successful. That includes clear expectations, communication of what success looks like, feedback on performance, and accountability for meeting those standards. Ideally, you’re doing these on a regular basis in one-on-one meetings  and in performance check-ins throughout the year. Churches and nonprofits must hire capable people who can effectively perform their duties and steward the mission. This is a manager’s job, and faith-based organizations don’t have a softer standard. Where I’ve seen termination decisions and conversations go south—in Christian organizations or elsewhere—is when a manager doesn’t understand this. (Or, worse, they understand it but think that somehow it doesn’t apply to them.) Speaking to an employee about parting ways because you’ve consistently documented underperformance is a rough conversation. It’s far worse when your failure to give regular feedback leaves an employee blindsided, confused, and hurt when you need to broach termination. Often, that failure is rooted in a desire to avoid conflict or hurt feelings. The manager would rather spare himself the discomfort of a direct conversation. In a Christian organization, this impulse pulls hard. The employees under your care all love Jesus. They’re there to promote the church’s mission and spread the gospel. You may even sit shoulder to shoulder in the pews with them on Sundays. But James 4:17 has a word for managers who fail to do the difficult work: “Whoever knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, for him it is sin.” Colossians 4:1 underlines this: “Masters, treat your bondservants justly and fairly, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.” I’ve watched managers avoid the perceived sin of commission (telling someone he’s doing a poor job in his role) and step right into the sin of omission (letting the problem fester until the employee is struggling and a termination conversation seems inevit
content_zh:
无论是辅导经理、上游计划、接听电话、还是安排裁员。 每次都是艰难的。 与员工分离是经理最重的事情之一。 这样做既清楚又友好,需要大量的准备和情绪调节.

在基于信仰的工作场所,这些决定可能更加令人惊讶和痛苦,因为管理人员试图避免在任何“善良”的旗帜下谈论业绩的不愉快。 作为管理其他基督徒的基督徒,我们该怎么考虑?

为什么好工作是教会的重要使命 是传播耶稣的好消息, 创造方法让人们更深入地了解他, 基督教非盈利组织的目的相邻——在指向基督及其当地教会的同时提供慈悲、正义、福音或门徒。

这项工作通过部委和外联人员以及有效的行动进行。 从事这项工作需要发挥各种作用:牧师、行政人员和部委协调员;管理人员、会计师和音乐家;行政主管、设施运营商和信息技术团队。 管理教会或基督教组织所需的大部分是在直接部委时间之外。

title: Why Christianity Explains Our Deepest Longings
summary: ‘Why Christianity Makes Sense’ offers a compelling argument that Christianity explains the condition of both the world and the human heart.
summary_zh: 《基督教为何有道理》提出一个令人信服的论点，即基督教解释了世界和人心两种状态。
title_zh: 为什么基督教能够解释我们最深切的渴望
content: Throughout church history, God has raised up faithful voices to speak the gospel to each generation. The apostle Paul traveled through much of the known world, preaching in synagogues and public settings. In Athens, he used the questions the culture was asking as a platform from which to proclaim the gospel. Similarly, Augustine, Anselm, Blaise Pascal, C. S. Lewis, Tim Keller, and many others helped readers see Christianity’s coherence amid the questions and assumptions of their times. Through his online ministry, Truth Unites , Gavin Ortlund fills that sort of role in our cultural moment. In Why Christianity Makes Sense: A Book About Jesus, the Mysteries of the World, and the Longings in Your Heart , Ortlund offers an accessible defense of the faith for readers unsure whether Christianity can withstand serious examination. It’s also a useful tool for discipling believers bombarded with hard questions about Christianity on the internet. Ortlund’s goal is to show “why it makes sense to be a Christian” (xiii). Ortlund’s particular strength is that he recognizes our questions aren’t merely intellectual. They arise from deeper longings for meaning, purpose, and transcendence. Unknown God In Athens, Paul thoughtfully noticed an altar established “to the unknown god” (Acts 17:23). He didn’t mock them for it. Every generation builds an altar of its own. Augustine called it the restless heart; Lewis called it Sehnsucht , the longing that joy itself cannot satisfy. Keller called the traces it leaves behind clues . Ortlund has a name for it: “the ache.” Ortlund doesn’t begin with a technical exposition of the ache but by showing it’s the desire behind every altar to every unknown god. He asks, “Are you genuinely curious about what life means—why you’re here, and what it’s all for?” (xi). The ache is the restless longing for the transcendent that we can’t put into words. Just as hunger implies we live in a world where food is meant to fuel our bodies, so the desire for meaning points to the existence of something that will satisfy that desire. So many counterfeits promise to satisfy our desire for God. Many people have learned to deny any sense of longing for the divine or simply scroll past the question before it finishes loading in their minds. Just as hunger implies we live in a world where food is meant to fuel our bodies, so the desire for meaning points to the existence of something that will satisfy that desire. In a culture where the most shocking content on social media becomes boring, it’s worth drawing attention to Jesus’s radical claims. “He claimed to be the way, the truth, and the life,” notes Ortlund. “Muhammad taught the five pillars, Buddha spoke of enlightenment, Confucius pointed to the Way, but Jesus pointed to himself as the answer. In fact, Jesus claimed to be God” (104). The claim is preposterous, unless it’s true. So Ortlund asks his readers to put on their thinking caps: “What if God is real, and Jesus is this God, showing up in history to reveal himself to us? Why not? Is it really all that much crazier than the alternatives?” (104). It’s not. And more importantly, the solution Jesus offers is the most complete answer to the ache. This message deserves to be proclaimed in public. In the Marketplace When Paul was in Athens, he “reasoned . . . in the marketplace” (Acts 17:17), the agora, which is where ideas were exchanged. Our modern agora is increasingly virtual, less of a town square and more like the comment section of a microvlog. Ortlund has excelled in this space, making hard things plain in his videos without making them small. His talent for public communication comes through in this book. For example, Ortlund tackles divine hiddenness: Have you ever wondered why, if God is indeed real, his existence isn’t completely obvious? Why are religious matters so ambiguous ? Wouldn’t a loving God want to make things clear to us? (176) It’s an intuitive argument that undermines the sense that the ache is a longing

title_zh: 印度一个有8口人的基督徒家庭被驱逐，无家可归
content: A Christian family of eight in the Sukma district of Chhattisgarh, India, was left homeless after Hindu nationalists ransacked and demolished their home on the morning of Nov. 16. During the eviction, the family’s essential household items — including food, clothing, bedding, kitchen utensils, and vital personal documents — were thrown out of their home. The house, belonging to Manglu Sodi and his wife, Hirmibai, was reportedly ransacked and demolished because of their Christian faith. Amid the destruction, 4,000 rupees (roughly $43), about five grams of gold, and a bicycle were stolen before the house was destroyed. Relief in Safe House Fleeing for their safety, the family traveled roughly 40 miles to reach the district headquarters of Sukma, where they were placed in a Safe House constructed with the help of International Christian Concern (ICC). Representatives of the Progressive Christian Alliance (PCA), a rights advocacy group working for the welfare of Christian minorities, coordinated with local pastor Harendra Madiya in Sukma to provide relief for the persecuted family. PCA State Coordinator Patras Balti visited the family to encourage and pray with them, urging them to remain steadfast in their faith despite the severe hardship. Although formal complaints have been submitted to the local police station, the Superintendent of Police (SP), and the district collector of Sukma, no formal inquiry or legal action has been initiated to date. Without their identification documents or savings, the family faces steep hurdles in rehabilitation and rebuilding their lives. Historic Church Building Razed Down In another development, up north of Sukma district, about 300 miles away, a historic church estimated by locals to be roughly 130 years old was demolished in Rajnandgaon district of Chhattisgarh in the past week. The structure was part of the campus of the Missionary Bands of the World Leprosy Hospital (also known as the Rajnandgaon Leprosy Hospital and Clinics), which stood on about 23 acres of government-leased land originally allotted for treating and rehabilitating leprosy patients. The Clearance Operation The demolition followed a lease-cancellation order issued on Nov. 6 by the Rajnandgaon district collector. The demolition drive razed not only the church, but also the old hospital wards, administrative offices, and residential quarters of the leprosy hospital. The administration said the reclaimed land will be used for public amenities, including a sports ground. However, Christian watchdogs are skeptical about the district collector’s action. Christian community leaders urged a clear distinction between the government’s right to recover land over alleged lease violations and the decision to destroy a heritage religious structure. To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . summary_zh: 这可能令人感到意外，但圣诞节是伊拉克的国定假日——自2018年12月政府正式宣布以来一直如此。“这感觉像是为了显得不歧视而采取的象征性举措。”“彼得罗斯”说道。他是一名亚述基督徒，与一个伊拉克侨民家庭一起居住在美国。他补充说，这种“象征性”的庆祝……   这篇题为《圣诞节在伊拉克是一个喜忧参半的节日》的文章最初发表在“国际基督徒关注”网站上。
title_zh: 圣诞节是伊拉克一个喜忧参半的节日
content: This may come as a surprise, but Christmas is a national holiday in Iraq — ever since the government formally declared it so in December 2018. “It feels like a token move to appear non-discriminatory,” said “Petros,” an Assyrian Christian living in the U.S. with an Iraqi expat family. He added that this “token” celebration of Christmas “ignores the native traditions” of the region’s Christians and “instead opts for a European-style Christmas” with Santa Claus and various types of Christmas trees that don’t naturally grow in the area. Iraq, which was already celebrating the birth of Christ when most of Europe was still pagan, has among the world’s oldest Christian communities, with the faith arriving in the first century A.D. Petros feels that the Iraqi government’s acknowledgment of Christmas is more of a public relations strategy to deflect from the recent horrors faced by Iraq’s Christians. “Yonita,” an Assyrian woman who is Chaldean Catholic and lives in the U.S., believes the recent recognition of Christmas is financially motivated. “Iraq is trying to rebuild itself,” she said, adding that it might be “taking notes” from more successful countries in the region that have comparatively more religious freedom. Yonita suspects that celebrating Christmas could be an attempt at showing camaraderie with the West. It could also be a way to make the homeland seem more congenial to the many Iraqi Christians abroad. As she pointed out, the Christian Iraqi diaspora tends to be quite well-off financially. “There was a formal call inviting us back to Iraq [to] invest in the rebuilding of the cradle of civilization,” Yonita said. A Sad Reality Whatever the Iraqi government’s true motivation, one painful aspect is hard to deny: By the time Christmas became a national holiday, most Iraqi Christians had already been driven out of their homeland. Conditions were so difficult during the previous 15 years that the country had lost up to 90% of its Christian community. Iraq’s remaining Christians, most of whom belong either to the Chaldean Catholic Church or the Assyrian Church of the East, now comprise less than half of 1% of the country’s overall population. The Christian population had already seen considerable decline during the 24-year reign of former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein, a man of immense sadism. But, for all his homicidal flaws, Hussein — though Muslim by background — was no Islamic extremist. In fact, his longtime right-hand man, Deputy Prime Minister Tariq Aziz, was a Christian, at least technically. It would likely be an exaggeration to say that Hussein cared about the welfare of Iraqi Christians, but the bone-crushing force of his reputation rendered most Iraqis, regardless of their faith, too intimidated to indulge in sectarian hostilities. Petros said that his fellow Assyrian Christians “either liked Hussein for providing stability and jobs, or hated him for killing their family members.” Many of Iraq’s Christians wanted him to stay in power only because they had an acute sense of the mayhem that would erupt after their secular tyrant was deposed. “It’s like the saying goes,” Petros said. “Better to deal with the devil you know than the devil you don’t.” At this point, though, both “devils” have fully acquainted themselves with Iraq. The Rise of Extremism The ousting of Hussein from power in 2003 brought in an era of rising Islamic extremism, most notably with the Islamic State group (ISIS), formerly known as “al-Qaida in Iraq.” Some Iraqi Christians were even accused of collaborating with the U.S. military. As the atmosphere grew increasingly precarious in post-Hussein Iraq, most Christians fled the country, having decided the other options — violent death, forced conversion, or paying a religious tax — were unpalatable. Those who remained were often hunted. In June 2007, in the northern Iraqi city of Mosul, a priest and his assistants were killed right in front of his church. 这也许是个惊喜, 但圣诞节是伊拉克的国庆节, “Petros”是一位居住在美国的亚述基督教徒,

他补充说,这种对该地区基督教徒的圣诞节 " 玷污当地传统 " 的 " 庆祝 " , " 而不是选择一个欧洲式的圣诞节 " ,圣诞老人和该地区自然不会生长的各类圣诞树。

伊拉克在庆祝基督诞生时,欧洲大部分地区仍然是异教徒,伊拉克是世界上最古老的基督教社区之一,公元一世纪时,信仰就已经降临。 彼得罗斯认为伊拉克政府承认圣诞节更是一种公共关系策略,旨在转移伊拉克基督徒最近面临的恐怖。

“Yonita”是一位信奉迦勒底天主教、居住在美国的亚述妇女, 她说,“伊拉克正在努力重建自己”,她补充说,它可能“注意到”该区域比较成功的宗教自由的国家。

Yonita怀疑庆祝圣诞节可能是试图与西方展示友情. 这也可以成为使祖国看起来对海外许多伊拉克基督徒更加融洽的方法. 正如她指出的那样,伊拉克的基督教散居国外者往往在财政上相当富裕。

Yonita说,“有人正式邀请我们回到伊拉克,投资重建文明的摇篮。” 一个悲哀的现实 无论伊拉克政府的真正动机如何,一个痛苦的方面很难否认: 到圣诞节成为国家节日时,大多数伊拉克基督徒已经被驱逐出家园.

在过去15年里,情况十分困难,以至于该国丧失了90%的基督教徒。 伊拉克其余的基督教徒,大多属于迦勒底天主教会或东方亚述教会,现在占该国总人口的不到1%。

伊拉克前总统萨达姆·侯赛因24年的统治期间,基督教徒人数已经大幅度减少,他是一位极度虐待的人。 但是,侯赛因尽管有穆斯林背景,但他的杀人缺陷并非伊斯兰极端主义分子。 事实上,他长期担任右手的副总理塔里克·阿齐兹是基督徒,至少在技术上是这样.

如果说侯赛因关心伊拉克基督徒的福利,那很可能是一种夸张的说法,但他的名声的骨折力量使大多数伊拉克人,无论其信仰如何,都过于恐吓,不敢陷入教派敌对行动。

Petros说,他的亚述基督徒同胞“要么喜欢侯赛因提供稳定和工作,要么恨他杀害家人”。 许多伊拉克基督徒希望他继续掌权,只是因为他们对世俗暴君被废黜后爆发的混乱有强烈的感受。 Petros说,

“最好对付你认识的恶魔, 然而,此时,这两个“恶魔”已完全熟悉伊拉克。

极端主义的兴起 2003年侯赛因被赶下台,带来了伊斯兰极端主义抬头的时代,其中最突出的是伊斯兰国集团(ISIS),它以前被称为“伊拉克基地组织”。 一些伊拉克基督徒甚至被指控与美国军方勾结.

由于后侯赛因的伊拉克气氛越来越不稳定,大多数基督徒逃离该国,决定了其他选择——暴力死亡、强迫皈依或缴纳宗教税——是令人不快的。 留下来的人经常遭到追捕。 2007年6月,在伊拉克北部城市摩苏尔,一名牧师及其助手在他教堂前被杀死。

title_zh: 为巴基斯坦基督徒的释放而进行的呼吁工作变得更加紧迫
content: Shahzad Masih has been praying for justice since 2017. He was just 16 years old when he was arrested on false charges, and has been waiting to be hanged since 2022. Nine years later, the American Center for Law and Justice (ACLJ), through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), is continuing to advocate for his release, Christian Daily International reported. In 2017, Masih was working as a janitor at a hospital when a Muslim coworker asked him about his belief in Jesus. As he explained his faith, he mentioned a comment made by a family friend that was spoken against the Prophet Muhammad, which offended the coworker and ended the conversation. The coworker belonged to Tehreek-e-Tahfuz-e-Islam, a conservative Islamic group in Pakistan. Members of the group heard about their conversation and confronted the Masih. Though he tried to clarify the situation, he was handed over to the police on July 13, 2017, and was questioned without legal representation before being imprisoned. In November 2022, according to Section 295C of the Pakistan Penal Code, he was sentenced to death for the “use of derogatory remarks, etc. in respect of the Holy Prophet.” Since then, he has been waiting to be hanged for his unjust sentence. The United Nations has called for his immediate release, stating that these decisions deny his right to “freedom of expression.” OLA has supported him and filed an appeal for his freedom four times, but the Lahore High Court has yet to hear his case. “Shahzad Masih was just 16 years old when he was arrested, and nine years later, he remains on death row for allegedly reporting someone else’s words,” said CeCe Heil, senior counsel and international legal director for the ACLJ. “We urge Pakistani authorities to uphold fundamental human rights, overturn this unjust conviction, and bring Shahzad Masih home to his family.” One of Many As more stories of Christians being imprisoned for false blasphemy accusations arise this year — including Amir Peter , who was tried before by a Lahore court in 2024 and died in custody in July — ACLJ is committed more than ever to fighting for the life of this young Christian. “This is the ultimate abominable human rights violation, and we’ll take this case all the way to Pakistan’s Supreme Court,” the advocacy group wrote . Open Doors ranks Pakistan as the eighth most dangerous place to be a Christian in the world. They are constantly subjected to persecution through discrimination, death threats, mob violence, imprisonment, and death, through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), continues. Story by Bella Agnello To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . title_zh: 越南在教会土地纠纷中拆除历史悠久的天主教建筑
content: Vietnamese authorities demolished a historic building belonging to the Redemptorist Catholic community in the central city of Huế on Tuesday, escalating a decades-long dispute over church property and raising renewed concerns about religious freedom in the communist-governed country. The demolition of the L’Accueil building followed the deployment of police by local authorities to block roads surrounding the Redemptorist monastery and Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church. Electricity to the area was also cut, preventing some parishioners from reaching the church to attend Mass or express solidarity with the religious community. According to the Redemptorists, heavy machinery began demolishing the structure while priests, religious brothers, and parishioners gathered nearby in prayer. The demolition continued through Nov. 18, leaving the property leveled and fenced off. The Redemptorist Provincial Chapter of Vietnam condemned the operation, arguing that authorities proceeded despite unresolved legal questions and repeated requests to review the property’s ownership. “Justice cannot be established through force, and the truth cannot be erased along with the structures that have been demolished,” the congregation said in a Nov. 17 statement as the demolition was proceeding. Communist Land Takeover The dispute centers on land that the Redemptorists purchased in 1930. According to historical documentation cited by the religious order, Huế municipal authorities formally recognized the congregation’s ownership in 1971. The L’Accueil complex was subsequently developed on the property between 1938 and 1943. It served as a center for educational, cultural, and community activities, housing a library, auditorium, and reading room. A sawmill was also established on the grounds in the 1950s, providing local employment. Following the communist takeover of South Vietnam in 1975, the government’s relationship with religious institutions changed significantly. Church properties throughout the country came under increasing state control, with religious communities frequently losing access to land and buildings they had previously owned. The Redemptorists maintain that they never voluntarily surrendered their rights to the L’Accueil property. They acknowledge that the congregation transferred assets associated with a sawmill to the state in 1978, but argue that the transfer did not include the land itself. Authorities subsequently assigned the property to government-controlled institutions. The remaining parcel, measuring about 2,550 square meters, is currently managed by a local sports vocational school. Recent Efforts The congregation has sought the property’s return since 1994. Its most recent formal complaint, submitted to the Huế People’s Committee on Oct. 24, requested recognition of its land-use rights and clarification of the property’s legal status. Authorities reportedly rejected the complaint in a Nov. 8 response, stating that it had no basis for consideration. A notice posted at the property in October announced plans to develop a public park and parking lot on the site. Local authorities have defended the project as serving public interests, including improving traffic conditions and providing additional green space in a densely populated area. Vietnamese law establishes that land is collectively owned by the people and administered by the state. Government authorities have also invoked a 2003 National Assembly resolution that generally prevents reconsideration of certain land and housing arrangements established before July 1, 1991. The Redemptorists, however, dispute the government’s interpretation of the property’s history and say authorities have not adequately explained the legal grounds for demolishing the building. They have asked officials to publicly disclose the documentation supporting their decision and review the historical records presented by the congregation. 在L ' Accueil大楼被拆除之前,地方当局部署了警察,封锁救赎会修道院和永生圣母助教周围的道路。 该地区的电力也被切断,使一些教区人士无法前往教堂参加弥撒或表示对宗教界的声援.

据救赎派说,重型机械开始拆除该建筑,而祭司,宗教兄弟,以及教区教徒聚集在附近祈祷. 拆除工作一直持续到11月18日,财产被夷为平地和围起来。

越南救赎主义省分会谴责了这次行动,认为当局不顾尚未解决的法律问题和一再要求审查该财产的所有权而继续行动. “正义不能通过武力建立,真理不能与被拆除的建筑物一起抹去。”

17份在拆除过程中的声明。 共产党夺地 争端集中在救赎者在1930年购买的土地上。 根据宗教秩序所引用的历史文献,胡瓦克市当局于1971年正式承认该教会的所有权. L ' Accueil建筑群后来于1938年至1943年间在地产上发展.

它作为教育、文化和社区活动中心、图书馆、礼堂和阅览室。 1950年代还在当地建立了锯木厂,提供当地就业。 1975年共产党接管南越后,政府与宗教机构的关系发生了重大变化.

全国各地的教会财产受到越来越多的国家控制,宗教社区往往失去获得其以前拥有的土地和建筑物的机会。 救赎者坚持认为,他们从未自愿放弃对L ' Accueil财产的权利。

他们承认教会在1978年将与锯木厂有关的资产转移到了国家,但辩称转让不包括土地本身. 当局随后将财产分配给政府控制的机构。 其余部分占地约2,550平方米,目前由当地体育职业学校管理.

最近的努力 自1994年以来,教会一直要求归还财产。 它最近于10月24日向胡瓦克人民委员会提出正式申诉,要求承认其土地使用权并澄清财产的法律地位。 据报告,当局在11月8日的答复中驳回了申诉,称申诉没有审议依据。

10月在该地产张贴了一份通知,宣布计划在该地开发一个公共公园和停车场. 地方当局捍卫该项目是为了公共利益,包括在人口稠密地区改善交通条件和提供更多的绿色空间。 越南法律规定,土地属于人民集体所有,由国家管理。

政府当局还援引了2003年国民议会的一项决议,该决议一般禁止重新审议1991年7月1日之前确定的某些土地和住房安排。 但救赎者质疑政府对该地产历史的解释,

他们要求官员公开公布支持其决定的文件,并审查教会提出的历史记录。 争议说明了宗教共产主义的困难

summary_zh:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普,中国国家主席习近平,俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京星期四在中国深圳举行前所未有的三边峰会,展现出世界三大强国之间合作的形象,但对面临的冲突和国际问题却很少提出具体协议.

title_zh: 特朗普、习近平和普京在宗教自由状况恶化之际会晤
content: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin met Thursday in Shenzhen, China, for an unprecedented trilateral summit, projecting an image of cooperation among three of the world’s most powerful nations but offering few concrete agreements on the conflicts and international issues facing them. The roughly 80-minute meeting produced a joint statement addressing United Nations reform, energy production, international legal authority, and nuclear risks. However, the statement offered no clear breakthroughs on the wars in Ukraine or Iran and made no public reference to religious freedom or the persecution of religious communities in China and Russia. The gathering underscored the importance of direct engagement among world leaders as they seek to manage competing interests, global conflicts, and questions about the future of international order. The summit also offered an opportunity to address concerns affecting millions of people who face persecution for their faith, particularly in countries governed by authoritarian regimes. A Summit Focused on Global Stability The three leaders presented themselves as sharing responsibility for maintaining international peace and security. Their joint statement called for United Nations reform, increased production and supply of petroleum products, and further dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The leaders also emphasized state sovereignty and the immunity of government officials, declaring that the International Criminal Court and similar bodies should not abuse their authority. The language reflects a shared interest among the three governments in limiting the reach of international institutions, although their respective political, economic, and security priorities remain distinct. Concerningly, this language is similar to that used by China in pushing back on American calls to respect human rights and ensure citizens can freely practice religion. Claiming that these are internal affairs, China rejects what it considers to be overly zealous policing by the U.S. and continues on its path of persecution. Putin described the summit as a new chapter in diplomatic history and praised the opportunity for direct engagement with Trump and Xi. The Russian president also invoked the 1945 Yalta Conference, which helped shape the postwar European order, arguing that international conflicts eventually require countries to recognize realities on the ground. While the leaders expressed interest in dialogue and international stability, their meeting did not produce publicly announced agreements to resolve major conflicts or address underlying tensions between their governments. Religious Freedom Remains a Global Concern For religious freedom advocates, high-level diplomatic meetings represent an important opportunity to raise the plight of prisoners of conscience and religious communities facing government persecution. China, in particular, continues to impose severe restrictions on religious practice. Christians in unregistered churches face surveillance, detention, church closures, and pressure to submit to government oversight. The Chinese Communist Party’s campaign to bring religious institutions under its control has affected Protestant house churches, Catholic communities, Tibetan Buddhists, Uyghur Muslims, and other religious minorities. In recent months, international advocates have urged the Trump administration to raise the cases of imprisoned religious leaders with Xi. Earlier this year, Trump raised the case of Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri, founder of Beijing’s Zion Church, during a meeting with Xi. Chinese authorities subsequently released Jin, who later relocated to the United States. However, other Zion Church leaders arrested during the same crackdown remain detained, and no such direct advocacy seems to have occurred at this most recent meeting. The case demonstrated how direct presidential engagement can potentially influence the circumstances
content_zh:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普,中国国家主席习近平,俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京星期四在中国深圳举行前所未有的三边峰会,展现出世界三大强国之间合作的形象,但很少就它们面临的冲突和国际问题达成具体协议.

大约80分钟的会议产生了关于联合国改革、能源生产、国际法律权威和核风险的联合声明。 然而,该声明对于乌克兰或伊朗的战争没有提出明确的突破,也没有公开提及中国和俄罗斯的宗教自由或对宗教团体的迫害.

会议强调了世界领导人直接参与的重要性,因为他们寻求管理相互竞争的利益、全球冲突和有关国际秩序未来的问题。 首脑会议还提供了一个机会,解决影响到数百万因信仰而面临迫害的人的关切,特别是在专制政权统治的国家。

以全球稳定为重点的首脑会议 三位领导人自称分担维护国际和平与安全的责任。 他们的联合声明呼吁联合国改革、增加石油产品的生产和供应,以及就减少核风险进一步进行对话。

各国领导人还强调国家主权和政府官员的豁免权,宣布国际刑事法院和类似机构不应滥用其权力。 其措辞反映了三国政府对限制国际机构的影响力的共同利益,尽管它们各自的政治、经济和安全优先事项仍然不同。

关于这一点,这种语言类似于中国在抵制美国尊重人权和确保公民可以自由信奉宗教的呼声时所使用的语言。 中国声称这是内政,反对美国过于狂热地维持治安,继续走迫害的道路。

普京将峰会描述为外交史上的新篇章,并称赞与特朗普和习近平直接接触的机会. 俄罗斯总统还援引了1945年雅尔塔会议,会议帮助塑造了战后的欧洲秩序,认为国际冲突最终需要各国承认当地的实际情况.

虽然领导人对对话和国际稳定表示兴趣,但他们的会议没有达成公开宣布的协议,以解决重大冲突或解决政府之间的紧张关系。

宗教自由仍然是全球关注的问题 对于宗教自由倡导者来说,高级别外交会议是一个重要的机会,可以提高良心犯和宗教界面临政府迫害的困境。 特别是中国继续严格限制宗教活动.

在未登记的教堂的基督徒面临监视,拘留,教堂关闭,以及服从政府监督的压力. 中国共产党将宗教机构置于其控制之下的运动影响了新教住宅教堂,天主教社区,藏传佛教,维吾尔穆斯林等宗教少数派.

最近几个月,国际倡导者敦促特朗普政府向习近平提出被囚禁宗教领袖的案件. 今年早些时候,特朗普在北京锡安教会创始人伊兹拉·金明里牧师会见习近平时提出这个案例. 中国当局随后释放了后来移居美国的金.

然而,在同一次镇压中被捕的其他锡安教会领导人仍然被拘留,在最近的这次会议上似乎没有进行这种直接的宣传。 该案表明,总统直接参与会如何影响局势

title_zh: 在持续冲突的背景下，东盟继续将缅甸军政府排除在外
content: Southeast Asian leaders reaffirmed their opposition to Myanmar’s military government at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila on Nov. 15, extending restrictions on the country’s political representation after concluding that its military leadership had made insufficient progress toward ending the country’s civil war. The decision came as leaders from the 11-member regional bloc gathered in the Philippines for three days of discussions on international conflicts, regional security, and economic stability. Myanmar’s continuing violence and humanitarian crisis featured prominently, alongside disputes in the South China Sea and the broader consequences of conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine. In a statement following their review of Myanmar’s implementation of a five-point peace plan adopted in 2021, ASEAN leaders expressed deep concern over the continuing conflict. They denounced attacks against civilians and public infrastructure. They called on all parties to halt indiscriminate violence, protect civilian populations, and allow humanitarian assistance to reach those in need. The leaders also agreed to maintain the restriction preventing Myanmar’s military leader and foreign minister from attending ASEAN summits and foreign ministers’ meetings until meaningful progress is made toward implementing the peace plan. Myanmar will continue to be represented at those meetings by lower-level diplomatic officials. The decision represents a positive continuation of ASEAN’s effort to pressure Myanmar’s military leadership while preserving diplomatic channels with the country. A Peace Plan with Little Progress Myanmar has been embroiled in a nationwide civil war since February 2021, when the military overthrew the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi. The coup prompted widespread protests and a violent crackdown by security forces. Armed resistance subsequently emerged across the country, with longstanding ethnic armed organizations also intensifying their campaigns against the military. In April 2021, ASEAN developed a five-point consensus intended to address the crisis. The agreement called for an immediate cessation of violence, constructive dialogue among all parties, mediation by an ASEAN special envoy, humanitarian assistance, and engagement between the envoy and relevant stakeholders. Despite repeated diplomatic efforts, the plan has produced little meaningful progress toward ending the conflict. ASEAN has struggled to balance its traditional policy of noninterference in member states’ domestic affairs with the need to respond to the increasingly severe humanitarian and political crisis in Myanmar. The bloc has maintained contact with the military government while withholding full political recognition at its highest-level meetings. In May 2025, ASEAN attempted to strengthen its approach by making the special envoy position permanent rather than replacing the representative annually. The change was intended to provide greater continuity in diplomatic engagement and improve the prospects for negotiations. However, continued military operations and widespread abuses have undermined those efforts. According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent monitoring organization, more than 8,600 people had been killed and 32,406 arrested by Myanmar’s security forces as of this week. The figures reflect the extensive human cost of the conflict and the government’s continued repression of opposition. Myanmar’s military leadership has also attempted to restore its international standing. Military chief Min Aung Hlaing became president in April following elections conducted in phases in December and January. Opposition groups and international observers criticized the elections as an effort to consolidate military control rather than restore genuine civilian government. Despite visits to several ASEAN member states, Min Aung Hlaing remains excluded from the bloc’s highest-level politi
content_zh:
东南亚领导人在11月15日于马尼拉举行的东南亚国家联盟(东盟)首脑会议上重申反对缅甸军政府,认为缅甸的军事领导在结束该国内战方面进展不足后,延长了对该国政治代表权的限制.

这项决定是11个成员的区域集团领导人在菲律宾聚集一堂,讨论国际冲突、区域安全和经济稳定问题,为期三天。 缅甸的持续暴力和人道主义危机与南中国海的争端以及中东和乌克兰冲突的更广泛后果一道,占据了显著地位。

东盟领导人在审查缅甸执行2021年通过的五点和平计划后发表声明,对持续冲突深表关切. 他们谴责对平民和公共基础设施的袭击。 他们呼吁所有各方停止不分青红皂白的暴力,保护平民,允许人道主义援助送达需要援助的人。

领导人还同意继续限制缅甸的军事领导人和外交部长出席东盟首脑会议和外交部长会议,直到在执行和平计划方面取得有意义的进展。 缅甸将继续派低级外交官员出席这些会议。

这一决定是东盟在保持与缅甸的外交渠道的同时向缅甸军事领导人施压的努力的积极继续。 自2021年2月军方推翻昂山素季当选政府以来,与小进步缅甸的和平计划卷入全国内战.

政变引发了广泛的抗议和安全部队的暴力镇压. 武装抵抗随后在全国各地出现,长期存在的族裔武装组织也加强了对军队的进攻。 2021年4月,东盟达成了旨在应对危机的五点共识.

协定要求立即停止暴力,所有各方进行建设性对话,由东盟特使进行调解,提供人道主义援助,特使与相关利益攸关方进行接触。 尽管一再作出外交努力,但该计划在结束冲突方面没有取得什么有意义的进展。

东盟努力在不干涉成员国内政的传统政策与应对缅甸日益严重的人道主义和政治危机的必要性之间取得平衡。 该集团与军政府保持联系,同时拒绝在最高级别会议上给予充分的政治承认。

2025年5月,东盟试图加强其做法,使特使的职位永久化,而不是每年更换代表。 这一变化旨在增加外交接触的连续性,改善谈判前景。 然而,持续的军事行动和普遍的侵权行为破坏了这些努力。

据独立监督组织政治犯援助协会称,截至本周,缅甸安全部队已杀害8 600多人,逮捕32 406人。 这些数字反映了冲突给人带来的巨大代价以及政府继续镇压反对派。

缅甸的军事领导人也试图恢复其国际地位。 在12月和1月分阶段举行选举之后,军事长官敏昂·赫莱于4月成为总统。 反对派团体和国际观察员批评选举是为了巩固军事控制而不是恢复真正的文职政府。

尽管访问了东盟的几个成员国,敏昂莱仍然被排除在集团最高领导层之外。

title: Fulani Militants Kill 14 Christians in Plateau State, Nigeria
summary: At least 14 Christians have been killed in fresh attacks across four local government areas of Plateau state, Nigeria, days after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu appealed for forgiveness over his failure
summary_zh: 在尼日利亚博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统就其未能保护人民免受袭击一事呼吁原谅的几天后，在高原州的四个地方政府辖区内发生的最新袭击中，至少有14名基督徒被杀害。
title_zh: 富拉尼武装分子在尼日利亚高原州杀害14名基督徒
content: At least 14 Christians have been killed in fresh attacks across four local government areas of Plateau state, Nigeria, days after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu appealed for forgiveness over his failure to visit violence-affected communities during an earlier trip to the state and promised to rebuild destroyed communities and return internally displaced persons (IDPs) to their ancestral homes. The killings occurred between Sunday, Nov. 15, and Monday, Nov. 16, in Mangu, Riyom, Barkin Ladi and Bokkos local government areas, according to community sources and local security groups. Armed attackers reportedly targeted rural settlements and ambushed residents traveling between communities. The latest violence followed Tinubu’s visit to Jos on Saturday, Nov. 14, for an All Progressives Congress (APC) political rally at Zaria Road Stadium, where he acknowledged the suffering of communities affected by recurring attacks and displacement. Addressing residents and party supporters, Tinubu asked Plateau residents to forgive him for not visiting affected communities during his previous trip to the state in April. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport,” he said. “Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland, but I saw the devastation. I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people.” The president promised to rebuild communities destroyed by violence and facilitate the return of displaced residents. “We will rebuild your communities, and we will bring you back to your communities,” Tinbu added. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau.” He also commended the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr. Bernard Doro, for identifying vulnerable populations and coordinating humanitarian assistance. Tinubu announced that 1,000 forest guards were undergoing training and that surveillance cameras promised to Plateau state had been procured to strengthen security monitoring and early warning operations. However, fresh attacks were reported within hours of the president’s departure from the state. In Mangu Local Government Area, armed attackers invaded Zwagal community in Jipal District at about 9 p.m. on Sunday, killing nine people. Other residents were reportedly missing following the attack. Silas Nanfwang, a resident who confirmed the incident to journalists, called on security agencies to intensify efforts to locate the attackers and bring those responsible to justice. In Barkin Ladi, 79-year-old Da Ishaku Pam Vwos was killed when armed men invaded Sho village at about 5:20 p.m. on Sunday, according to the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM). The association’s National Publicity Secretary, Rwang Tengwong, also reported the killing of 42-year-old Dauda John Davou during an attack on the Sambak community in Hoss District, Riyom LGA, at about 2 a.m. on Sunday. Another attack was reported in the Jol community around 12:10 a.m. on Sunday. According to BYM, local vigilantes responded to the attackers, preventing further casualties. The association said the incidents followed the shooting of Joshua Doro Dafwel in Jol on Wednesday. He is currently receiving medical attention. BYM also reported that Ina Arin was killed when armed men ambushed him and his friend, Abok Gyang, as they returned to Dorong village in Foron District. Gyang survived the attack. In Bokkos Local Government Area, two people, including a unit commander of the Plateau state-owned security outfit, Operation Rainbow, were killed in an ambush on Monday afternoon. The victims, identified as Gambo and his companion, were traveling on a motorcycle from Hurti village to Tadai in Manguna District when armed men attacked them at about 1:30 p.m. They had reportedly visited Hurti for a condolence visit and died at the scene. Gambo had recently completed a refresher training program for Operation Rainbow unit commanders in Jos and was known amon
content_zh:
在博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统呼吁原谅他在早些时候访问受暴力影响的社区,并承诺重建被摧毁的社区并让境内流离失所者返回其祖传家园几天后,在尼日利亚高原州四个地方政府地区,至少有14名基督徒被杀死。

据社区人士和地方安全团体称,这些杀戮发生在11月15日星期日至16日星期一的Mangu、Riyom、Barkin Ladi和Bokkos地方政府地区。 据报告,武装袭击者以农村定居点为目标,并伏击社区之间的居民。 在Tinubu于11月星期六访问Jos后,

14,在Zaria Road体育场举行全体进步人士大会(APC)政治集会,他承认一再受攻击和流离失所影响的社区遭受苦难。 蒂努布针对居民和政党支持者,要求高原居民原谅他4月前去该州旅行期间没有访问受影响的社区.

他说,“上次访问时,我仅限于机场。” “对不起,如果你没有在内地看到我,但我看到了灾难。 我收到州长的报告了 我在我国人民的脸上看到了恐怖。” 总统承诺重建被暴力摧毁的社区并便利流离失所居民回返。

Tinbu补充说,“我们将重建你们的社区,并将你们带回你们的社区。” “我已指示所有安全机构采取果断行动,并维持高原的和平与稳定。” 他还赞扬人道主义事务和减贫部长贝尔纳·多罗博士确定弱势人口和协调人道主义援助。

蒂努布宣布有1000名森林警卫正在接受训练,并且已经采购了向高原州承诺的监视相机,以加强安全监测和预警行动. 然而,据报道,总统离开国家后的数小时内又有新的袭击.

在Mangu地方政府地区,武装袭击者于星期日下午9时左右入侵Jipal区的Zwagal社区,造成9人死亡。 据报告,其他居民在袭击后失踪。 向记者证实此事的居民Silas Nanfwang呼吁安全机构加紧努力找到袭击者,并将责任人绳之以法。

在Barkin Ladi,79岁的Da Ishaku Pam Vwos被武装分子于星期日下午5:20左右入侵Sho村而死,据Berom青年穆尔德斯协会(BYM)称. 该协会的全国宣传秘书Rwang Tengwong还报道了42岁的Dauda John Davou星期天凌晨2时左右在Riyom LGA的Hoss区被Sambak社区袭击时被杀死的事件。

据报道,乔尔社区在星期日12:10左右又发生了一起袭击事件. 据BYM称,当地民团对袭击者作出反应,防止了进一步的伤亡. 该协会说,事件发生在周三Joshua Doro Dafwel被枪击后。 他目前正在接受治疗。

BYM还报告说,Ina Arin被武装分子伏击并被其朋友Abok Gyang杀死,当时他们返回了Foron区的多龙村。 克阳幸免于袭. 在博克科斯地方政府地区,包括高原国有保安装备"彩虹行动"的一名分队指挥官在内的两人于星期一下午被伏击而身亡.

受害者被确认为Gambo和他的同伴,他们乘坐摩托车从Hurti村前往Manguna区的Tadai,武装人员于下午1时30分左右袭击他们。 据报告,他们前往Hurti慰问,并在现场死亡。 甘博最近完成了 " 彩虹行动 " 部队指挥官在乔斯的进修培训方案,并被称作 " 阿蒙 "

title_zh: 印度西孟加拉邦的印度教民族主义者将矛头对准基督徒
content: At least 48 to 65 incidents of targeted harassment, church vandalism, and physical violence against Christian communities in West Bengal, India, have been recorded between May and November. The Bangiya Christiya Pariseba, a Christian organization working for the welfare of the state’s Christian community, compiled this data. The right-wing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in West Bengal following the April 2026 Legislative Assembly elections. Independent tracking by the research group India Hate Lab verified 60 hate crime incidents explicitly targeting Christian individuals, domestic fellowships, and institutional properties within West Bengal during the same period, confirming the widespread geographic footprint of the escalation of attacks on Christians. According to reports, the latest attack occurred on Nov. 9, when vandals desecrated a sacred shrine and Marian grotto of a church in an overnight attack in Khari Bamuner Chak, located within the Raidighi and Baruipur pastoral region of West Bengal’s South Parganas. A week earlier, a heavily organized contingent of about 40 men attacked a house prayer fellowship in Rayan village of the Bardhaman area. The assailants stormed the private residence during a morning service, violently assaulting the officiating pastor and worshippers. Surge of Attacks The surge in targeted violence, intimidation, and vandalism against Christian communities, churches, and home prayer fellowships in West Bengal is proving that Hindu nationalists have found West Bengal to be the new hunting ground with tacit support of the authorities. The state is currently experiencing a rapid breakdown in local law enforcement deterrence. This erosion directly threatens the constitutional guarantees enshrined in Article 25 of the Indian Constitution, which ensures freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion. The emergence of organized Hindutva networks operating with near-total impunity represents not merely localized social friction, but a systemic challenge to the rule of law and civil stability across the state. Faith Space Shrinking Across rural and semi-urban districts of West Bengal, Hindu nationalists increasingly employ physical blockades, structural desecration, and coordinated mob actions to shrink the space for religious minority assemblies. By weaponizing social intimidation and exploiting police inertia, these actors seek to criminalize ordinary acts of devotion, transforming private exercise of faith into contested public security triggers. Detailed documentation by human rights organizations and community defense networks attributes the vast majority of these incursions to organized Hindutva-affiliated groups. Investigations specifically point to operational coordination by local cadres associated with the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) and the Bajrang Dal, the RSS’s militant arm. Assailants consistently deploy dual narratives of illegal “unlawful religious conversions” and fabricated “honey traps.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . content_zh:
5月至11月期间,印度西孟加拉邦至少有48至65起针对基督教社区的有针对性骚扰、破坏教堂和人身暴力事件。 Bangiya Christiya Pariseba是一个致力于国家基督教团体福利的基督教组织,

右翼印度民族主义者Bharatiya Janata党(BJP)于2026年4月立法议会选举后在西孟加拉邦上台.

研究小组印度仇恨实验室的独立跟踪核实了同期60起仇恨犯罪事件,明确针对西孟加拉邦的基督教个人、家庭奖学金和机构财产,证实了对基督教徒袭击升级造成的广泛地域影响。 据报道,最近一次袭击发生在11月.

9日,在位于西孟加拉邦南帕尔干纳斯的Raigighi和Baruipur牧区Khari Bamuner Chak的一起夜间袭击中,被破坏者亵渎了一座圣地和一座教堂的Marian地道。 一周前,一支由约40名男子组成的组织严密的特遣队袭击了Bardhaman地区Rayan村的一个家庭祈祷研究金。

袭击者在上午礼拜时冲入了私人住宅,暴力袭击了牧师和礼拜者。

袭击的激增 西孟加拉邦针对基督教社区、教堂和家庭祈祷研究金的有针对性暴力、恐吓和破坏行为激增,证明印度教民族主义者在当局的默许下发现西孟加拉邦是新的狩猎地。 目前,该国地方执法威慑迅速崩溃。

这种削弱直接威胁到《印度宪法》第25条所载的宪法保障,该条确保良心自由和自由信奉、实践和传播宗教的权利。

有组织的印度人网络的出现几乎完全不受惩罚,这不仅是局部性的社会摩擦,而且是对全国法治和国内稳定的系统性挑战。

印度民族主义者在西孟加拉邦的农村和半城市地区越来越多地采取实际封锁、结构性亵渎、协调暴徒行动来缩小宗教少数群体集会的空间。

通过将社会恐吓武器化和利用警察惯性,这些行为者试图将普通的献身行为定为刑事犯罪,将个人信仰的行使转变为有争议的公共安全触发因素。 人权组织和社区防卫网络的详细文件将绝大多数入侵归因于有组织的印度教附属团体。

调查特别指向与印度印度人理事会(VHP)和RSS好战武装Bajrang Dal有关的当地干部的业务协调。 仆从们一贯使用非法的“非法宗教皈依”和捏造的“甜蜜陷阱”的双重说法。 更多新闻报导, 采访,请通过电子邮件。

The Kuala Lumpur High Court has ordered that a lawsuit filed by a…   The post  Malaysian Court Sends Christian Convert’s Religious Freedom Suit to Regional Bench  first appeared on  International Christian Conc
summary_zh:
一个34岁的法学毕业生的多年战斗暴露了宗教控制的严重现实和想要离开伊斯兰教的公民所面临的法律陷阱. 马来西亚宗教自由受到侵蚀,

吉隆坡高等法院下令... 马来西亚法院将基督教皈依者 的宗教自由申请提交地区法官,
title_zh: 马来西亚法院将一名皈依基督教者的宗教自由诉讼移交地区法庭
content: A 34-year-old law graduate’s multi-year battle exposes the severe reality of religious control and the legal trap facing citizens who want to leave Islam. A high-stakes constitutional challenge highlighting the erosion of religious freedom in Malaysia has taken a procedural step backward. The Kuala Lumpur High Court has ordered that a lawsuit filed by a 34-year-old legal researcher seeking legal recognition as a Christian be transferred to the Shah Alam High Court. The case lays bare the rigid and intrusive control exercised by state apparatuses and Islamic religious authorities over personal faith, showcasing a system where basic human rights — such as choosing one’s own religion — are tightly policed by the government. A Life Labeled Without Consent The plaintiff, Shameer PV, identifies as a Christian and has lived as one since he was 18. However, under strict Malaysian administrative regulations, the word “Islam” was stamped on his compulsory national identity card (MyKad) when he was just 12, following a bureaucratic policy introduced under the National Registration Act. Despite decades of personal conviction and his marriage to a Christian wife, the state continues to legally treat him as a Muslim, directly violating his parental and marital status and refusing to recognize his family. Shameer’s legal challenge names the federal government, the Selangor state government, and the Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) as defendants. He argues that labeling citizens by religion on state identity cards violates Article 11(1) of the Federal Constitution, which ostensibly guarantees every person the right to profess and practice their religion. Trapped in Shariah Bureaucracy Shameer’s ordeal underscores the labyrinthine and punishing hurdles forced upon religious minorities and converts in Malaysia’s dual-justice system, which runs a parallel set of Islamic (Shariah) courts alongside the civil judiciary. In 2018, Shameer initiated proceedings in a Selangor Shariah court seeking official recognition of his Christian faith. After an exhausting 72 court sessions spanning over seven years, the Shariah court dismissed his application in January. Rather than allowing him to move on with his life, the religious court went a step further, ordering state departments and Islamic authorities to “guide and control” his practice of Islam — effectively treating his desire to leave the faith as a disciplinary or correctional matter. Having exhausted the religious tribunal system, Shameer turned to the civil high court in July, filing an originating summons to ask the highest judicial authorities whether state-mandated religious labeling on identity cards is unconstitutional, and whether Shariah courts have any lawful jurisdiction over individuals who do not practice Islam. A Wider Crisis for Freedom of Conscience International human rights observers and religious freedom advocates have long criticized Malaysia’s legal framework regarding apostasy and conversion. While the Malaysian Constitution theoretically protects freedom of religion, civil courts have repeatedly ruled that only Islamic Shariah courts have the authority to permit someone to leave Islam — creating an effective judicial catch-22, as Shariah courts rarely grant permission to renounce the religion. For international human rights advocates and supporters of religious liberty, Shameer’s case is a stark reminder of the state-enforced religious controls facing millions in Southeast Asia. As his case moves to the Shah Alam court, the legal battle continues to test whether Malaysia’s secular constitutional framework can protect an individual’s fundamental right of conscience against a totalizing state religious bureaucracy. 一个34岁的法学毕业生的多年战斗暴露了宗教控制的严重现实和想要离开伊斯兰教的公民所面临的法律陷阱. 马来西亚宗教自由受到侵蚀,

吉隆坡高等法院下令将34岁法律研究者提出的寻求法律承认为基督徒的诉讼移交沙阿拉姆高等法院.

这一案件暴露了国家机构和伊斯兰宗教当局对个人信仰的严格和侵扰性控制,表明政府严格控制基本人权(如选择自己的宗教)的制度。 未经同意的生活标签 原告Shameer PV确认为基督教徒,自18岁起就一直作为一个教徒生活在一起。

然而,根据严格的马来西亚行政条例,他12岁时的强制性国民身份证(MyKad)上印有“伊斯兰”一词,这是根据《国家登记法》实行的官僚政策。

尽管几十年的个人信念和他与基督教妻子的婚姻,但国家继续在法律上将他视为穆斯林,直接侵犯了他的父母和婚姻状况,并拒绝承认他的家人. 沙门的法律质疑将联邦政府,雪兰莪州政府,雪兰莪伊斯兰宗教委员会(MAIS)列为被告.

他辩称,以宗教方式将公民贴在州身份证上违反了《联邦宪法》第11(1)条,该条表面上保障每个人信奉和奉行其宗教的权利。

伊斯兰教法官僚沙姆耶的折磨凸显了Labyrinthine和惩罚强加给宗教少数派和皈依马来西亚双重司法制度的障碍,马来西亚的双重司法制度与民事司法平行设有一套伊斯兰(伊斯兰教法)法院。 2018年,沙姆耶在塞兰哥教法法院提起诉讼,寻求官方承认他的基督教信仰.

经过历时七年的72次开庭,教法法院于1月驳回了他的申请。

宗教法庭没有让他继续自己的生活,而是更进一步,命令国家部门和伊斯兰当局“指导和控制”他的伊斯兰教习俗——实际上将他放弃信仰的愿望视为纪律或惩戒事项。

在用尽了宗教法庭制度之后,Shameer于7月向民事高等法院提交了原传票,询问最高司法当局在身份证上贴上国家规定的宗教标签是否违宪,伊斯兰教法法院是否对不信奉伊斯兰教的个人拥有任何合法管辖权。

国际人权观察员和宗教自由倡导者长期批评马来西亚关于叛教和皈依的法律框架。

虽然马来西亚宪法理论上保护宗教自由,但民事法院一再裁定只有伊斯兰教法法院有权允许某人离开伊斯兰教——这创造了有效的司法抓捕-22,因为伊斯兰教法法院很少允许放弃该宗教.

对国际人权倡导者和宗教自由支持者来说,Shameer一案明确提醒人们注意东南亚数百万人所面临的国家强制宗教控制。

title: Teenage Girl Dies After Six Months in Captivity
summary: On Nov. 1, six people took their first steps of freedom after being held by Fulani extremists for more than six months. One of them died only two days later. Hasana Bulus, 13, died in the hospital where she was taken in critical condition. Bulus was one of the 11 people who were kidnapped by a Fulani militia in…   The post  Teenage Girl Dies After Six Months in Captivity  first appeared on  International Christian Concern .
summary_zh: 11月1日，六人在被富拉尼族极端分子关押超过六个月后，迈出了重获自由的第一步。其中一人仅两天后就去世了。13岁的哈萨娜·布卢斯（Hasana Bulus）在被送往医院时已处于危急状态，后在医院去世。布卢斯是富拉尼民兵绑架的11人之一……   这篇题为《少女被囚禁六个月后死亡》的文章最初发表在“国际基督徒关注”网站上。
title_zh: 少女被囚禁六个月后死亡
content: On Nov. 1, six people took their first steps of freedom after being held by Fulani extremists for more than six months. One of them died only two days later. Hasana Bulus, 13, died in the hospital where she was taken in critical condition. Bulus was one of the 11 people who were kidnapped by a Fulani militia in April. One had escaped, but five died at the camp, and the rest were released with Bulus — including the 4-year-old daughter of a woman who had died in captivity. Bulus’ village, Awon, is predominantly Christian and has been the target of Fulani attacks, just like Ariko, a neighboring village in Kaduna state. According to a six-year study conducted by the Observatory for Religious Freedom in Africa (ORFA), Islamic Fulani militias are by far the deadliest persecutors of Christians in Nigeria. Ariko is home to the 37 Christians who were kidnapped during the Easter services earlier this year in a neighboring village. Of these, 17 people have died in captivity, 12 have escaped, and eight have since been released. The abductees from both these villages were held in the same forest hideout, where they were kept in inhumane conditions. “They [the villagers] told us how they would stay for two weeks without food,” one woman, whose father died in the camp, told Open Doors . “They only boil water to drink. That’s how they struggled before the bandits gave them corn flour, and they started making swallow (a porridge). The men are restrained, chained in groups; they are not free to move around.” All of the male abductees in these groups had died in the camp. Christian Solidarity Worldwide (CSW) is calling for Nigerian authorities to protect these communities and fight to free more people left in bondage. “We continue to urge the Nigerian government at state and federal levels to prioritize the protection of vulnerable communities throughout the nation, to combat the threat posed by the litany of terrorist groups that are active in the country far more effectively, and to secure the release of all abductees,” CSW CEO Scot Bower said. “Nigeria’s Christians do not need another statement of sympathy,” ICC’s president, Shawn Wright, said. “They need protection , justice , and accountability . When those who murder innocent Christians face no meaningful consequences, impunity becomes an invitation to the next attack. The Nigerian government must protect vulnerable communities, pursue the perpetrators, and make clear that these crimes will not go unanswered.” Story by Bella Agnello To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . 根据非洲宗教自由观察站(ORFA)进行的一项为期六年的研究,伊斯兰富拉尼民兵是尼日利亚基督教徒最致命的迫害者。 阿里科是37名基督徒的家,他们在今年早些时候在复活节礼拜期间在一个邻近村庄被绑架。

其中,17人在囚禁中死亡,12人逃脱,8人自此获释. 这两个村庄的被绑架者被关在同一个森林藏身处,他们被关在不人道的条件下。 “他们[村民]告诉我们,他们将如何在没有食物的情况下呆两周,”一位父亲死于营地的妇女告诉Open Doors。 “他们只煮水饮用。

在土匪给他们面粉之前, 这些人被捆绑起来,被捆绑在一起;他们不能自由移动。” 这些团伙中的所有男性被绑架者都死于营地。

世界基督教团结会呼吁尼日利亚当局保护这些社区,并努力释放更多受奴役的人。

“我们继续敦促尼日利亚州和联邦政府优先保护全国的弱势社区,更有效地打击在该国活动的众多恐怖主义团体构成的威胁,并确保释放所有被绑架者。”

“尼日利亚的基督徒不需要再次表示同情, “他们需要保护、正义和问责制。 当杀害无辜基督徒的人没有面临有意义的后果时,有罪不罚就成为下一次袭击的诱因。

尼日利亚政府必须保护弱势社区,追捕肇事者,并表明这些罪行不会得不到答复。” Bella Agnello的故事 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

title_zh: 如果家庭游戏之夜能让您的孩子谈论圣经，会怎么样？
content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Doxa Games . This post is written by Marco Bartholomae, founder of Doxa Games and creator of the Bible-based board and card games Trials & Triumphs , Bible Clash , and Hurry! Fleeing Disciples . A couple of years ago, I was playing cards with my kids when a question hit me. What would it take to make a Bible game they’d ask to play again? I grew up in Germany with four brothers. We played cards on long car rides and spent hours on our bedroom floor with a board game spread out between us. I still remember how easy it was to lose track of time when we played together. Now I live in California with my wife and our four children, and we still love a good game night. The screens go away, somebody wants a rematch, and we get to enjoy being together. That question from the card table stayed with me. I started imagining games that could give other families that same experience and get them talking about Scripture along the way, games a child could sit down to, learn the rules, and enjoy right away, even if they were new to the Bible. Then maybe a name on a card or something that happened on the board would make them curious enough to ask a question. That’s how Doxa Games started. The Conversations That Start Around the Table In Deuteronomy 6, God tells his people to speak about his commandments with their children as they go about ordinary life, including when they sit at home. A game night gives us another chance to do that. Our games don’t replace family devotions, but they do open conversations about God’s Word. Your child might pick up a card and ask who Thaddaeus was. A race to a house church might get them wondering why the early Christians gathered in homes. Those are questions you can follow right back to Scripture. That’s also why I chose the name Doxa . It’s the Greek word for glory . In 1 Corinthians 10:31, Paul reminds us to do everything to the glory of God, even in ordinary things like eating and drinking. That conviction shapes what we make and how we think about time around the table. Three Games to Play With Your Family Bible Clash: Gospels (ages 8+) is a fast-paced, head-to-head card game. Play characters from the four Gospels and try to outscore your opponent. Trials & Triumphs (ages 5+) sends players down a winding path where one turn can move you forward, and the next can set you back. It gives younger kids a way to talk about trusting Christ through trials. Hurry! Fleeing Disciples (ages 8+) takes you into the world of Acts. Choose your route, evade Roman guards, and race to reach a house church. From Our Family Table to the Mission Field As Doxa grows, we hope to translate these games and put them in the hands of missionaries, church planters, and ministry training centers in places like Colombia, the Philippines, and East Africa. I’d love for a family in Malawi to pull out one of these games, play it in their own language, and have the same kinds of conversations we have around our table. If your family is getting together this Christmas, pick a game, clear a spot at the table, and let the kids make the first move. See all three games at DoxaGames.com . content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Dakota Fiebranz says that since it’s the easiest and most expected thing in the world to criticize Grand Theft Auto , he takes a different tack and writes about what its popularity says about its users. “For those unfamiliar with the Grand Theft Auto series, the premise is relatively simple. You’re placed in a fictional American city, usually in the character of a criminal, and given a staggering amount of freedom to carry out your most dubious ambitions. What I am, however, is the father of a very classically autistic teenage boy.” Stephen Kneale explains what we can learn about evangelism from people with autism. How to Fire Someone at a Christian Organization. Unfortunately, even Christian people working for Christian organizations sometimes need to be let go. This article offers wisdom for those times. “When we hold back the hard call, we tell ourselves a story about mercy: I don’t want to be the one who upends this person’s life, so I won’t go there. That’s a heavy burden to put on your shoulders. To believe you’re ruining someone’s life by ending his employment is to believe you hold his future in your hands. But here’s the thing: You don’t. You aren’t sovereign over this person’s story. You cannot see his next chapter. The assumption that you can, that keeping him in a role where he’s failing is protecting him from some fate only you can foresee, isn’t humility. It’s pride.” America Needs a New Temperance Agenda. Brad Littlejohn writes about the recent political earthquake in the U.S. and explains why America needs a new temperance agenda. “Our markets, rather than serving American families, are tearing them apart, and American voters are primed for leaders willing to rein in an economy that caters to appetite and impulse rather than genuine human needs. Rather than narrowing our moral message, it’s time to broaden it—and with it, our coalition.” Praise God From Whom All Sparrows Flow. Kevin Burrell explains how a bird told him that the season of gratitude has begun. “The mid-fall arrivals of fall colors and flannel and pumpkin spice lattes can trigger our hearts to a sort of Thanksgiving nostalgia; they announce, like my backyard sparrows, ‘Remember, ‘tis the season to give thanks!’ But if we let them, these annual bellwethers can slingshot us well past an afternoon of turkey and football and reciting a couple of blessings around the table.” The Housing Crisis and the Biblical Duty of Stewardship. This is a thoughtful piece about the housing crisis. The context is the U.S., but much of it applies to Canada as well. “If we want young Americans to have a genuine opportunity to build stable lives, it’s not enough to implement another temporary affordability program. We need to recover a vision of economic life rooted in stewardship and responsibility, with the goal of flourishing families.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. What books, products, videos, sites, or oth

summary_zh: 能够与Missionary合作，创作面向儿童的图画传记系列《Goers》，我深感荣幸。每本传记都向年轻的读者和听众讲述那些被教会派出去将耶稣基督的福音传到地极的男男女女的故事。另请参阅今日出版：埃里克最伟大的比赛6本适合儿童的优秀新书约翰·加尔文（适合青少年读者的基督教人物传记）
title_zh: 教导子女了解那些被差遣的人
content: It was a great honor to be able to partner with Missionary to create Goers , a series of illustrated biographies for children. Each biography introduces young readers and listeners to the stories of men and women who were sent by churches to spread the good news about Jesus Christ to the ends of the earth. Each is illustrated by the ultra-talented Rommel Ruiz. The books can be purchased as a set of three or as individual volumes. The Plowboy’s Bible: The Story of William Tyndale’s English Translation . Hunted by spies, William Tyndale fled across Europe with a bounty on his head, his Bible translation labeled as contraband. Young John, on the other hand, has a long day of farm work ahead of him. Although their lives seem worlds apart, John’s father knows a story that binds John and William together—their love for God’s word. The scripture John relies on for encouragement cost William everything, but they gave John’s family everything! Rescued from Darkness: Amy Carmichael and the Girls of Dohnavur . Kumari is scared, helpless, and alone in a dark temple until Amma, a mysterious woman from a faraway land, carries her away to a beautiful garden. This is not a fairy tale. It’s the true story of missionary Amy Carmichael and the children she rescued and raised at Dohnavur Fellowship in India. Into the Unknown: David Livingstone’s Heart for Africa . Before David Livingstone was the most famous man in the world, he was a boy who dreamed of being free to explore God’s creation. But when David reached the mission field, he found that freedom taken from the people he tried to teach about the Creator. This is the story of a goer’s dangerous journey to the ends of the earth, of his courageous stand for justice, and of his patient endurance for the sake of Christ. The Goers series is written for children ages 4–10, and is ideal for parents to read to their children or for young readers to read on their own. Each book includes discussion questions and prayer points to get your family thinking and praying about the Great Commission. Each hardcover volume has 40 full-color pages and is sized 10″ x 10″. The Goers series is currently available exclusively through Westminster Books . Look for three more volumes to be added to the series around this time next year. See Also Releasing Today: Eric’s Greatest Race 6 Great New Books for Kids John Calvin (Christian Biographies for Young Readers)
content_zh:
能够和传教士合作创作Goers, 每部传记都向年轻的读者和听众介绍被教会派去向世界末端传播耶稣基督的好消息的男女的故事. 每个都由超能的隆美尔·鲁伊斯(英语:Rommel Ruiz)来说明.

书籍可作为一套三卷或单卷购买. 《犁男孩的圣经:威廉·廷达勒英文译本的故事》。 在间谍的追捕下,威廉·廷达勒带着头上的赏金逃过欧洲,他的圣经译本标注为违禁品. 而年轻的约翰则有很长的一天的农场工作在他前面.

虽然他们的生活似乎有些不同,但约翰的父亲却知道一个把约翰和威廉联系在一起的故事——他们对上帝之言的爱。 圣经中约翰依靠的鼓励让威廉付出了一切,但他们给了约翰的家人一切! 从黑暗中拯救:艾米·卡迈克尔和多赫纳武尔的少女.

库马里害怕,无助,独自在黑暗的神庙中,直到远方的神秘女子阿玛把她带到美丽的花园. 这不是童话 这是传教士Amy Carmichael和在印度Dohnavur联谊会救起和抚养的孩子的真实故事。 David Livingstone的非洲之心。

在大卫·利文斯通(David Livingstone)是世界上最有名的人之前,他是一个梦想自由探索上帝创造的男孩. 但是当大卫到达任务领域时,他发现自由从那些他试图教导造物主的人身上夺走.

这是一位行者前往地球尽头的危险旅程,他勇敢地站在正义面前,以及他为基督而耐心忍耐的故事。 Goers系列为4–10岁的儿童写作,是父母向子女阅读或年轻读者自己阅读的理想.

每本书都包含讨论问题和祈祷点,以让你的家人思考和祈祷大委员会. 每个硬盖卷有40页全色,大小为10′′×10′′. Goers系列目前完全通过Westminster Books提供。 明年的这个时候再找三卷

content: Good morning. If you have read this site for any length of time, you will know that I am not the kind of person who does hot takes, since I just don’t trust myself to do them well. However, with the Wesley Huff situation developing, I did want to link to what I consider an especially helpful assessment of the matter. You can find that beneath today’s recommended reads. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several volumes in the excellent New Studies in Dogmatics series. You’ll also find books by Jinger Duggar Vuolo, David Mathis, John Piper, and others. I continue to find and highlight hardcover and softcover book deals as part of Amazon’s Pre-Black Friday Book Deals . There are around 80 of them now, many of which are half off or more. Recommended Reading Hot Water and Holy Wonder: Giving Thanks for Ordinary Luxuries. “Every now and then, as I sit in my home library, a sense of awe settles over me—a spirit of wonder at the everyday comforts that surround me.” Trevin Wax celebrates the joy of the ordinary luxuries that God so graciously grants us. Are My Prayers Selfish? Responding to a question from a listener, John Piper explains the difference between prayers that are selfish and those that simply ask for things. “James is saying there is a kind of prayer that treats God like a cuckold. It refers to a husband whose wife is cheating on him. That’s a cuckold. Christians are making God into a cuckold. How? When it says they are praying just to spend it on their passions. The picture is of an unfaithful wife who asked her husband for $50 so she can go down the hall and pay another man to have sex with her. That’s the picture. She’s using prayer to cheat on her husband, God.” When the Heavens Declare: What a Solar Halo Says to a Secular City. Johannesburg was recently the site of a solar halo ( see here for images ). Tim Cantrell writes about what the skies were declaring in that moment. Gospel-Pilling the Looksmaxxers: Hope for Despairing Men. “What do dating apps, the 1999 film The Matrix, rhinoplasty, crystal meth, and smashing your face with a hammer all have in common? Welcome to the world of looksmaxxers. Let’s start at the beginning.” Mark Sanders introduces a concerning trend for young men and offers a much more satisfying hope. Here Are the Lessons I’ve Learned About Single Missionaries (From a Lifetime of Being One). I’m neither single nor a missionary, but still very much appreciate Andy Smith’s thoughts on the matter. “I always assumed that I would get married. I never thought I would enter full-time ministry. Yet, here I am, a contented single missionary since 1989.” Don’t Be Afraid to Provoke Your Brothers. Michael Kelley says why it’s important that we provoke one another. “I grew up in a house with two brothers. By the time we were all in school, ‘provoking’ was down to an art form. For each of my brothers, I knew the right buttons to push to get a rise out of them. I knew the words, the facial expressions, or even the subtle hint to drop that would flush their anger. What’s more, I knew how to do it to one of them to get at the other one. Like I said, an art form.” On Wesley Huff All those who have heard the recent news about Wesley Huff’s plagiarism have been shocked by it, myself no less than anyone else. I think Glen Scrivener is especially helpful, firm, and compassionate in this video . Even if you don’t watch it all, consider watching the final 10 minutes for the brief “sermon” he preaches there. Huff released a statement yesterday, which you can read on X or Facebook . Flashback The Blessing of a Higher Purpose in Our Pain. The chief end of affliction is to glorify God and enjoy him. The purpose of our lives is the purpose of our times of struggle, loss, grief, illness, and bereavement. The local church enables the world to look upon the canvas of God’s people and see an authentic painting of Christ’s love and holiness, not a forgery. —Jonathan Leeman Download Share See Also A La Carte (April 1) A L
content_zh:
早报. 如果你读过这个网站有一段时间, 你会知道,我不是那种热心的人, 因为我不相信自己能做得很好。 然而,随着Wesley Huff局势的发展,我确实想把我认为对此事特别有益的评估联系起来。 在今天推荐的读物中,

推荐阅读热水与神圣神奇:为普通的Luxuries致谢. “每当我坐在家里的图书馆里时, 一种敬畏感会安顿在我身上, 特雷文·瓦克斯(Trevin Wax)庆祝上帝如此慷慨赐予我们的普通豪华的喜悦. 我的祷告是自私的吗?

约翰·皮珀(John Piper)在回答一个听众的提问时,解释了自私的祷告和单纯要求事物的祈祷之间的区别. “詹姆斯说,有一种祷告将上帝当作一个笑柄。 它指的是妻子在欺骗他的丈夫。 那是个骗局。 基督徒正在让上帝变成傻瓜 怎么会?

当它说他们祈祷 仅仅把它花在他们的激情。 照片是一位不忠的妻子,她向丈夫索要50美元,这样她就可以下堂,付钱给另一个男人和她做爱. 这张照片就是这样。 她利用祈祷欺骗她的丈夫上帝。 当天堂宣布:太阳光环对世俗城市说些什么.

约翰内斯堡是太阳光环的所在地(图片请参见这里)。 蒂姆·坎特雷尔写了 那一刻天空在宣布什么 (原始内容存档于2018-09-22). Glass-Pilling the Looksmaxxers:希望绝望的人. “约会应用,1999年的电影《母体》,犀角成形术,水晶冰毒,用锤子砸你的脸,有什么共同点? 欢迎来到美容师的世界

让我们从头开始。 马克·桑德斯介绍了青年男子的趋势,并带来了更令人满意的希望。 我所学到的关于单一传教士的教训, 我既不是单身,也不是传教士,但仍非常欣赏安迪·史密斯对此问题的想法. “我一直认为我会结婚。

我从未想过我会进入全职部门 然而,我在这里,是一个自1989年以来满足的单一传教士。” 不要害怕为你的兄弟们辩护。 Michael Kelley指出, “我与两个兄弟在一个房子里长大。 到我们全校时, " 挑衅 " 已沦为艺术形式。

对于我每个兄弟,我都知道正确的按钮 来推动他们起来。 我知道这些话,面部表情, 甚至是会冲动他们的愤怒的微妙暗示。 更何况,我知道如何去对付他们中的一个,

如我所说,艺术形式。” 韦斯利・赫夫 所有听到最近有关Wesley Huff盗版主义的消息的人, 我认为Glen Scrivenner在这段视频中特别有帮助、坚定和同情心。 想想看最后10分钟,

Huff昨天发布了一份声明, 我们痛苦中崇高的祝福 苦难的主要结局是颂扬上帝,享受他. 我们生活的目的,是我们奋斗,损失,悲伤,疾病,丧命的时代的目的.
