title_zh: 您愿意考虑支持我的工作吗？
content: I have been blogging at Challies.com on a daily basis for over 23 years now. That long commitment has allowed me to write thousands of articles and hundreds of book reviews while also sending millions of visitors to other sites through the daily A La Carte feature. Though I’ve also written a number of books, the blog has always remained the “main thing.” Much of the blog’s content is now also translated into Spanish , French , and a number of other languages. One of my great desires has always been to freely give away as much as possible. I intend for it to always remain entirely free for all who visit . While, for obvious reasons, this can’t happen when it comes to books, I’ve made it my goal to ensure that everything else has been freely and widely distributed. While this has been possible largely because of advertisers, there is also a key role for the generosity of individuals. This is where patrons come in—patrons like you. There are a couple of different options for you to consider. The first is recurring monthly gifts. A service called Patreon provides a convenient means of linking content producers (like me) with ongoing supporters (like you). You can learn more and sign up at Patreon.com/challies . I also share monthly ministry and family updates there. The second is one-time gifts. If that is of interest to you, they can be made electronically via PayPal . If you prefer to send a one-time gift via check, you can simply mail a check (drawn on a US or Canadian bank) to this address: Tim Challies 1011 Upper Middle Road East, Box #1214 Oakville, Ontario L6H 5Z9 Canada Funds donated will be used to support my family and to help create great content or to otherwise improve, support, and enhance Challies.com. In one way or another, they will all be used to allow me to continue to do what I have been doing for these past 23+ years. Please understand that I intend for Challies.com to always remain entirely free. In fact, patrons help ensure that it always remains that way. Thank you for considering becoming a patron of Challies.com. Your support means so much to me. And this is the end of my once-yearly mention of this subject! See Also Would You Consider Becoming a Patron? Would You Consider Becoming a Patron? Would You Consider Supporting My Work As a Patron?
content_zh:
我在Challies. 这一长期的承诺使我能够撰写数千篇文章和数百篇书评,同时通过每日的A La Carte专辑将数百万游客送到其他网站。

虽然我也写了很多书, 博客的许多内容现在也被翻译成西班牙语、法语和其他一些语言。 我最大的愿望之一是尽可能地自由奉献 我打算让它永远保持 完全自由的所有访问者。

我的目标是确保所有东西都能自由而广泛地分发。 虽然这在很大程度上是由于广告商造成的,但是个人的慷慨也可以发挥关键作用。 这里就是赞助人来的地方 像你这样的保镖 你们有几种不同的选择

title: A La Carte (November 19)
summary: The hardest day you may ever face / For the ones like me / Praying to the God who rules history / Dear Gen Alpha, Claude wants to turn you into a toad / Old dogs and new tricks / Getting a handle on our emotions / Kindle deals and more See Also A La Carte (April 24) A La Carte (November 27) A La Carte (November 22)
summary_zh: 您可能面临的最艰难的一天/对于像我这样的人/向主宰历史的神祈祷/亲爱的α世代，Claude想把你们变成癞蛤蟆/老狗学新把戏/掌控我们的情绪/Kindle优惠等另请参阅A La Carte（4月24日）A La Carte（11月27日）A La Carte（11月22日）
title_zh: 单点菜肴（11月19日）
content: Thanks for reading A La Carte! I’ve got a good collection of articles, sales, deals, and other material for you this morning. I hope you enjoy it! Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a new edition of John Piper’s Desiring God , two reader-friendly studies in Romans from Tim Keller, The Gospel After Christendom , and my own From the Rising of the Sun (which, to remind you, includes the full documentary for free). Westminster Books is featuring my three Goers books for kids, each of which features a well-known Christian figure. They are nicely discounted. Logos users will want to check out Bible Study Week where you’ll find lots of deals, highlighted by the Tyndale OT & NT Commentaries at $4.99 each. Recommended Reading The Hardest Day You May Ever Face. This is a beautifully tragic piece of writing from Kimberly Wagner as she recounts an extremely hard day. “Daylight was just breaking over the ridge beyond the hills when I slipped into Mom’s bedroom and climbed into the bed beside her, the same bed that as a child I’d run to in the middle of the night to find safety and comfort. On this date, many years ago, we laid my dad’s body in the grave. But, Momma no longer remembers dates, or only guesses to know what season of the year we’re in. She won’t know the significance of today’s date, but she does have a foggy awareness that, to her today represents something terrible on her horizon.” For the Ones Like Me. Zachary Conover writes for those who are like him in that they were raised as good church kids. “What does it mean that we were dead in our trespasses and sins? How were we enemies of God? How were our hearts in rebellion against His Word? For students who have grown up attending church, reading the Bible, and learning about Jesus, these descriptions can be difficult to reconcile with their own experience. I understand that difficulty because I was one of those kids.” Praying to the God Who Rules History. Casey McCall reminds us that when we pray, we pray to the God who rules history. “If your doctrine of God leads you to pray less, you need to reevaluate your understanding of God. If your system of theology leads you to underemphasize the practical power of petitionary prayer in your life, you need to modify your system.” Dear Gen Alpha, Claude Wants to Turn You Into a Toad. Please, for the Love of All Things Human, Don’t Let It. Christina Bieber Lake warns members of Gen Alpha about what an all-out and unthoughtful commitment to Claude and other AI apps is likely to do to them. “In simple terms, we are moving from AI (Artificial Intelligence), which is about getting help processing information, to AGI (Artificial General Intelligence), which is about telling a machine what to do and letting it do it while you sit back and file your fingernails. Experts are saying that AGI will produce ten times the impact of the industrial revolution at ten times the speed.” Old Dogs and New Tricks. “I’m not opposed to the idea of people retiring after many decades of work. They have worked hard, so why not enjoy the fruit of their labor? But what I’ve found disquieting is the static nature that characterizes some retirements. I’ve seen some light, however, at the end of the tunnel and from where I stand, it doesn’t look like a train!” J.V. Fesko explains why he isn’t eager to retire, even if he does eventually withdraw from the front lines of work. Getting a Handle on Our Emotions. Writing for the Biblical Counseling Coalition, Esther St. John offers counsel on getting a handle on emotions, or, perhaps better said, stewarding them faithfully. A Great Error Respecting Duty I have often pointed out that Christians used to speak of duty far more often than we do today, since it was important to express and fulfill the duties God had given his people. You can read what William Plumer believed about duty in this brief quote from one of his works, A Word to the Weary . God’s people sometimes fall into a great error respecting their duty.
content_zh:
谢谢你读了《La Carte》! 今天早上我给你们收集了大量的文章、销售、交易和其他材料。 我希望你喜欢它!

销售和交易今日的Kindle交易包括新版的约翰·皮珀的"渴望上帝"(John Piper's Design God),蒂姆·凯勒的两本对罗马人的读者友好的研究(The Glass After Christendom),以及我自己的"太阳升起"(为了提醒各位,这本书包括免费的完整纪录片). Westminster Books)以我的三本高尔书为主角,为孩子们著书,每本书中都有一位著名的基督教人物.

他们被很好的折扣。 Logos 用户会想查看《圣经学习周》, 推荐阅读最难的一天 你永远希望面。 这是来自Kimberly Wagner的一部非常悲惨的作品,

" 日光刚从山上的山脊上冲过去,我滑进妈妈的卧室,爬到她旁边的床上,那张床就是小时候我半夜跑去寻找安全和舒适的床。 许多年前的这一天,我们把我父亲的尸体埋在坟墓里。 但妈妈不再记得日期,

她不会知道今天这个日子的意义, 但是她确实很困惑, Zachary Conover为那些像他一样的人写道, 他们被培养为教会的好孩子。 “我们因犯法和罪恶而死,这是什么意思? 我们是上帝的敌人吗?

我们的心如何违抗他的话? 对于在教堂里长大,阅读圣经,了解耶稣的学生来说,这些描述可能很难与自己的经历相协调. 我理解这种困难,因为我是那些孩子之一。” 向统治历史的上帝祈祷.

凯西·麦科尔提醒我们,当我们祈祷时,我们向统治历史的上帝祈祷. “如果你的神学引导你少祈祷,你就必须重新评价你对上帝的理解。 如果你的神学系统导致你低估了自己生活中请愿祈祷的实际力量,你需要修改你的系统。” 亲爱的阿尔法将军 克劳德想把你变成一只青蛙

克里斯蒂娜·比伯·莱克警告阿尔法将军(Gen Alpha ) , 对克劳德(Claude)和其他AI应用软件的全心全意和不思议的承诺可能对他们造成什么影响。

“简言之,我们正在从AI(人工智能)转向AGI(人工智能),它涉及的是帮助处理信息,它涉及告诉机器该怎么做,让它做,而你却坐视不理,提交你的指甲。

专家说,AGI将以十倍的速度产生工业革命的十倍影响。” 老狗和新诡计。 “我不反对人们在工作几十年后退休。 他们辛勤工作,为什么不享受他们的劳动成果呢? 但我发现令人不安的是一些退休人士所特有的静态性。

但我看到隧道尽头有些灯光, J.V. Fesko解释为何他不急于退休, 得到一个处理 我们的情感。 为圣经咨询联盟撰稿 Esther St.

约翰为掌握情绪提供了建议 或者说 最好能忠实地管理情绪 我经常指出,基督教徒比我们今天更经常谈论义务,因为必须表达和履行上帝赋予他人民的职责。

你可以读到威廉·普鲁默所相信的 关于职责的简短引文 他的作品之一,《对疲劳者的言语》 真主的宗族有时在遵守自己的义务方面陷入大错。

title: What Takes 20 Years to Build Takes 5 Minutes to Destroy
summary: I think we’ve all heard many variations of the adage, “It takes 20 years to build a reputation, but only five minutes to destroy it.” A good name that has been established through many years of honor, success, or skilled leadership can be ruined in a moment when an act of immorality comes to light. See Also A La Carte (2/13) The Sinner’s Opinion of Himself The True Character of Unbelief
summary_zh: 我想我们都听过这句话的各种版本：“建立声誉需要20年，但毁掉它只需要5分钟。” 经过多年荣誉、成功或出色领导而建立起来的好名声，在不道德行为曝光的那一刻就会毁于一旦。另见零散文章（2月13日）《罪人对自己的看法》《不信的真正本质》
title_zh: 花20年时间建造的东西，5分钟就能摧毁
content: I think we’ve all heard many variations of the adage, “It takes 20 years to build a reputation, but only five minutes to destroy it.” A good name that has been established through many years of honor, success, or skilled leadership can be ruined in a moment when an act of immorality comes to light. Until a couple of weeks ago, Jensen Huang seemed to be on top of the world. While Nvidia, the company he co-founded, had long been a Silicon Valley success story, the rise of AI had driven it to new heights of success and its CEO to new heights of prosperity. Nvidia became the most valuable company in the world, its market capitalization of nearly $6 trillion surpassing even Apple’s. Huang’s net worth soared to over $200 billion, making him one of the wealthiest men in the world and one of the richest men in history. His two children have advanced positions within the company and his wife of more than 40 years distributes vast sums of money through their charitable foundation. Huang carefully curated his reputation and, as is so often the case in Silicon Valley, his image, with his slick black leather jackets becoming his trademark. Today, of course, Huang is no longer CEO of Nvidia or anything else. He was forced to resign after it came to light that he had engaged in extramarital affairs with multiple women, one of whom is allegedly a Chinese spy and another of whom is reportedly a subordinate within Nvidia. His image was shattered in a moment, and his reputation is now in tatters. The company lost over half a trillion dollars of value in the aftermath—value that was subtracted from Huang’s wealth, of course, but also from that of everyday investors whose wealth is far more modest. Pictures of his wife and children were splashed all over the news, and stories about his exploits were printed in every major media outlet in the world. The harm to his reputation is beyond repair, yet must pale in comparison to the harm and shame he has brought to his family. I hope that as Huang ponders what has become of his life, he has the wisdom to ask this: was it worth it? I hope each one of us asks the same, for Huang is not the first person to be tempted to grave sin , nor the first to succumb to temptation. In different ways and to different degrees, that is a battle we all fight every day. I have no experience of committing adultery, but I understand that it is exhilarating, and that doing what is forbidden delivers a great rush. And I suppose it must be exhilarating, for why else would a person risk so much to pursue it? Why else would a person do something that so defies common sense? Why else would a person gamble everything for the sake of illicit, fleeting pleasures? News reports describe him, in his final days at the company, calling himself “a piece of [expletive].” And while I wouldn’t phrase it that way, he’s not wrong that this situation has exposed him as what he truly is, and it’s actually far worse than the way he describes it. I might choose the word “wretch” to describe him, and not just him, but all of us. We are all wretches, for we are all wretched, people who trade short-term pleasure for long-term pain and fleeting joys for enduring sorrows. Sin makes us act like madmen, for sin is madness. And it leaves us wretched—desperately unhappy and in the sorriest of states. There has never been a sin that was more wise than foolish. There has never been a sin that delivered more gratification than the satisfaction of obedience. There has never been a sin that was worth more than the honor of a good name and an upstanding reputation. Thankfully, there has never been a sin that is beyond Jesus’s capacity to forgive. Though time and again we, like Huang, succumb to temptation, time and again Jesus forgives those who humble themselves before him to confess their sin and ask his forgiveness. May we all have the wisdom to see ourselves in Huang and to see in him a vivid example of the reality that sin promises joy while delivering sorr
content_zh:
我认为我们都听过许多不同的说法, “要建立名声需要20年, 一个通过多年的荣誉,成功,或熟练的领导而建立的良好名声,在不道德行为被揭发的一瞬间,可能会被破坏. 直到几周前,黄詹森似乎已经登上世界之巅.

虽然他共同创办的公司Nvidia长期是硅谷的成功故事,但是AI的崛起却将它推向了新的成功高地,其CEO也推向了新的繁荣高地. Nvidia成为了世界上最有价值的公司,其近6万亿美元的市场资本化甚至超过了苹果公司。

黄克诚的入股净值飙升至2000多亿美元,使他成为了世界上最富有的人之一,也是历史上最富有的人之一. 他的两个孩子在公司中担任高级职务,40多来年的妻子通过他们的慈善基金会发放一大笔钱.

黄克诚仔细地整理了自己的名声,并像硅谷经常出现的情况一样,他的形象被他浮出水面的黑色皮夹克也变成了他的商标. 今天,当然,黄已经不是恩维迪亚的首席执行官了

在得知他与多位妇女有婚外情后,他被迫辞职,其中一人据称是中国间谍,另一人据报是恩维迪亚的下属。 他的形象在一瞬间被打碎了,他的名声现在已经破灭了.

当然,该公司在事后损失了超过5万亿美元的价值 -- -- 当然,这一价值已经从黄家的财富中减去,同时也从日常投资者的财富中减去。 他妻子和孩子的相片被溅遍新闻,关于他剥削的故事被印入了世界上每一个主要的媒体渠道.

对他名誉的伤害是无法修复的,然而与他给家人带来的伤害和耻辱相比,必须苍白. 我希望,当黄帝思考他人生的结局时,他有智慧去问:这值得吗? 我希望我们每个人都问同样的问题 因为黄先生不是第一个 被严重罪孽诱惑的人 也不是第一个屈服于诱惑的人

以不同的方式和不同程度地,这是我们每天都要战斗的战斗。 我没有通奸的经验,但我明白,这是令人兴奋的,而做被禁止的事会带来极大的冲动。 我想这一定令人振奋 否则为什么一个人会冒险去追求呢? 否则一个人为什么要做 违背常识的事?

否则为什么一个人会赌取一切 为了非法的,短暂的快活? 新闻报导描述他在公司的最后几天自称是“一片[赞 ”。 虽然我并不会这样说, 但他并没有错误地认为这种情况暴露了他的真实面目,

我可能选择“错误”一词来形容他,而不仅仅是他,而是我们大家。 我们都是弱者,因为我们都是可怜人,他们以短期快活换取长期痛苦,以短暂的快活换取持久的悲伤。 罪恶让我们像疯子一样 因为罪恶就是疯狂 它使我们悲惨地 -- -- 极不幸福地 -- -- 在最烦恼的州里。

从未有过比愚蠢更明智的罪恶. 从来没有过罪过能带来比服从满足更多的满足. 从来没有一个罪过比一个好名声的荣誉和崇高的名声更值钱. 值得庆幸的是,从未有过耶稣无法宽恕的罪恶.

虽然我们像黄帝一样,一次又一次地屈从于诱惑,但耶稣一次又一次地原谅那些在他面前谦卑自卑的人,以忏悔他们的罪过并请求他的宽恕. 愿我们都有智慧去见自己在黄道上,在黄道上看到一个生动活泼的事例,说明罪恶许诺欢快,同时施以哀伤

content: Audio Transcript Welcome back to the podcast on this Thanksgiving week. Yesterday, we read about Jesus washing the feet of his disciples in John 13. Jesus worked his basin of water from disciple to disciple on the floor. When he reached Peter, Peter instinctively pulled his feet back and said, “You shall never wash my feet.” Then “Jesus answered him, ‘If I do not wash you, you have no share with me.’ Simon Peter said to him, ‘Lord, not my feet only but also my hands and my head!’” Dump the basin on my head. Give me a shower! And then “Jesus said to him, ‘The one who has bathed does not need to wash, except for his feet, but is completely clean. And you are clean’” (John 13:8–10). Peter is clean. He was chosen, and he was redeemed. Christ’s future work has already applied to him. Now he only needs his feet washed. Confessing sin is a part of daily cleansing (1 John 1:9), and that practice is never inconsistent with being “completely clean.” Peter is a living metaphor for justification and sanctification. And it tells me we can miss what Christ has done for us because we have dirt on our feet. We fixate on washing off the dust every day. We obsess over daily sanctification and forget that Christ washed us clean. Today on Ask Pastor John: how to beat scrupulosity. Today’s question is from a middle-aged man named Dave. “Pastor John, thank you for taking my question. I have struggled for many years with scrupulosity. That’s the word I learned last week while watching YouTube videos. When I looked up that word, scrupulosity, I wept for joy. My obsessive fears have destroyed my peace for many years. And I think I have discovered the root of most of my spiritual challenges and struggle with anxiety. So, now I want to ask you, Pastor John, what advice would you give to a man who has for years been paralyzed by scrupulosity?” There is a similarity between ordinary spiritual attacks that every believer endures, on the one hand, and more sustained obsessions that some believers endure, on the other hand. There’s a similarity. There’s an overlap. In other words, I don’t think we should overstate or understate the peculiar seriousness of what it is to deal with scrupulosity, or what is sometimes called obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Let me try to illustrate what I mean by the overlap between (1) the normal threat of a thought or an image or a behavior becoming an obsession that all of us experience and (2) the more persistent thoughts or images or behaviors that keep returning and returning, and won’t let a person have any rest, like a tick that bites you on the leg and sinks into your skin, and you try to pull it off, but it just grabs on deeper and harder. All of us deal with this danger. I’ve dealt with it personally and written about it, mostly in relation to sexual threats. For example, you inadvertently see some sexually riveting situation — say, a couple having sex on the ground behind your garage. Immediately, that image lodges itself in your consciousness with tremendous force. It threatens to take over. It wants to stay there and be developed in living color by your imagination. You can adapt this situation, this sexual temptation, to whatever your temptation is, whatever the threat of repetition is. You know the kind of thing I’m talking about. What do you do? Here’s my strategy. I’ll just sum it up quickly and then show how it might apply to this issue of scrupulosity. ANTHEM is my technique for handling a situation of threatening preoccupation with thoughts that ought not to be in my head. A: Avoid what triggers the thought or the image. If it’s inadvertent, don’t look back. If you can avoid the trigger in the first place, avoid it. N: Say no out loud to Satan, to your own mind. No — a strong, decisive no. “You will not have dominion over me (Romans 6:14)!” No to that thought, image, or memory. T: Turn your mind to another compelling reality. It might be the bloody body of Jesus hanging on the cross to make you pure. It m

当他到达彼得时,彼得本能地拉回他的脚,说:“你永远不能洗我的脚。” 耶穌回答说:如果我不洗涤你们,那末,你们与我毫无关系。 西门·彼得对他说:我的主啊!我的脚不只是我的,我的手和头也一样。 把盆子扔到我头上 给我洗澡!

然后,耶稣对他说:洗过澡的人,除脚部外,不必洗,但洗得干净。 而你是清白的”(John 13:8-10)。 彼佛清净. 他被选中,被赎回。 基督的未来工作已经适用于他。 现在他只需要洗脚

当我抬头看那句话,粗心,我为欢乐而哭泣。 我执着的恐惧毁了我多年的和平 我想我已经发现了我大部分精神挑战的根源,与焦虑作斗争.

所以,现在我想问你,约翰牧师,你会给一个多年来因粗心而瘫痪的人什么建议?” 每个信仰者所忍受的普通精神攻击与某些信仰者所忍受的更持久的痴迷之间有相似之处。 也有相似之处。 也有重叠之处。

换句话说,我认为我们不应该夸大或低估处理心烦意乱或有时被称为强迫症(OCD)的特殊严肃性。

让我来解释一下,我所说的重叠是:(1) 一个想法、一个形象或一个行为 成为我们所有人所经历的痴迷的正常威胁;(2) 持续回归和回归的更顽固的思想或图像或行为, 并且不会让一个人得到任何休息, 就像一只咬住你的腿和沉入你的皮肤的虱子,

只是抓住更深,更难。 我们所有人都面对这种危险。 我亲自处理此事, 例如,你无意中看到一些性刺激的情况——比如,一对夫妇在你的车库后面的地面上发生性关系. 即刻,这种形象会以巨大的力量在你的意识中产生。 它威胁要接管。

它想停留在那里,被你的想象所发展成活的颜色. 你可以适应这种情况, 这种性诱惑, 不管你的诱惑是什么, 无论重复的威胁是什么。 你知道我在说什么。 你们做什么的? 以下是我的策略。 我将很快总结一下,

ANTHEM是我的技巧 处理一个威胁 关注的状态 与不应该在我的脑海中的想法。 答:避免引发思想或图像的东西. 如果这是无意的, 若能先避触发者,避之. N:对撒旦大声地说不,对你自己的心灵说不. 不,一个强烈,决定性的不。

title_zh: 您就不能做点新东西吗？
content: How often does church-leadership content online reveal a lightly veiled obsession with new ? The experts today might not come out and say it, but the assumption often seems to be: Surely after two thousand years and all of our light-year advances in technology, the church needs a serious upgrade. Capturing this sentiment, one article insists, “Church leaders face two options. Either battle the marketplace currents and strive to convince enough people to pay for sermon-centric Sunday gatherings, or rethink that model to better fit the realities of making disciples in the twenty-first century.” Someone recently shared a clip with me that illustrates one such updated model. The video features a popular preacher who begins his Sunday sermon by driving a Rolls-Royce onto a stage. Twenty-two screens surround him, and hundreds of light bulbs hang overhead. The “preacher” steps out of the half-a-million-dollar car and takes critics like me head-on: There are some of you who are saying, “Oh man, I can’t believe you drove a Rolls-Royce into church. Man, that’s gimmicky.” No, it’s not; it’s godly. “Oh, that’s trite. That’s flippant.” No, it’s from Christ’s playbook. If you ever go to church and you find yourself bored, blame the communicator, the pastor. Don’t blame God. Yeah, for some reason we go to church and expect boredom. Just the opposite should be true. We are — and this is going to mess you up — we are in the entertainment business. I agree that no one should be bored in church — and I certainly agree that God is not to blame for any boredom in the pews. This preacher’s gimmick implies, however, that the same old formula for church — prayer, singing, fellowship, preaching — can’t possibly keep the attention of modern people like you. Mere sermons won’t cut it. God needs us to spice things up. God is not surprised by our state-of-the-art technology or shriveling attention spans, and he has told us, from the beginning, what captures souls when we gather for worship. He’s told us how to do church, and his counsel hasn’t expired. A Church Anyone Would Want Do you want to hear about a church that was emphatically not bored? They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers. And awe came upon every soul , and many wonders and signs were being done through the apostles. And all who believed were together and had all things in common. And they were selling their possessions and belongings and distributing the proceeds to all, as any had need. And day by day, attending the temple together and breaking bread in their homes, they received their food with glad and generous hearts, praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved. (Acts 2:42–47) Don’t you want to be a part of a church like that? Don’t you want your local church to taste the camaraderie, sacrifice, growth, and joy these people experienced when they gathered? The God-authored recipe is remarkably simple and durable: “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.” What did this church do when it grew so wildly and unexpectedly? They gathered. They ate. They gave. They prayed. They preached. And because they devoted themselves to God’s inspired Sunday-service plan, they rejoiced and their numbers multiplied. It’s dumbfounding that we see this kind of church thrive for literally millennia and still conclude it’s time to shake things up. “Sunday sermons got us this far,” we say, “but we’ll take it from here.” What if God knew everything we know — artificial intelligence, fiber-optic internet, driverless cars, those new robot vacuums that can clean stairs — and deliberately told churches to pray, sing, eat, drink, and preach the word anyway? Preaching to Itching Ears God knew exactly what changes and pressures our churches would face in the twenty-first century, and so he warned us t
content_zh:

要么与市场相抗衡,并努力说服足够的人为以布道为中心的星期日集会付出代价,要么重新考虑这一模式,以更好地适应二十一世纪的门徒现实。” 最近有人和我分享了一段片段 展示了这样一个更新的模型

影片的主角是一位受欢迎的传教士, 22个屏幕包围着他 数百个灯泡挂在上方 “掠夺者”走出50万美元的汽车, 你们中有些人说,“哦,我不敢相信你们把劳斯莱斯开进教堂。

这真是令人头痛。 不,它不是;它是上帝的。 “哦,这太老套了。 这简直是一团糟。 不,这是基督的剧本。 如果你去教堂觉得无聊, 责备通讯员,牧师。 别怪上帝。 是啊,出于某种原因,我们去教堂 期待无聊。 正好相反。 我们是在娱乐圈里,这会让你很不爽。

我同意,任何人都不应在教堂感到无聊——我当然也同意,上帝不应为在教堂里发生的任何无聊而责备. 但是,这个传教士的花言巧语意味着,同样的教会老式——祷告、唱歌、研究金、传道——不可能保持像你这样的现代人的注意力。 仅仅布道是不会减少的。 上帝需要我们调味料

content: It’s feasting season. Thanksgiving. Advent. New Year’s. But for Americans in particular, is there such a thing as a non -feasting season? Our society has a bizarre love-hate relationship with food, pulling the plate toward us with one hand while pushing it away with the other. On the one hand, about 40 percent of adults are clinically obese; on the other, more than one in eight adults rely on GLP-1 to suppress their appetite. We want food and we want to want food less. We struggle to break free from the clutches of Big Food, so we look to Big Pharma for help. Happy Thanksgiving? What’s the remedy for this gastronomic schizophrenia? As counterintuitive as it sounds, godly feasting provides an antidote to foolish gluttony. Feasting vs. Feeding The Bible has a lot to say about food, not just in isolated verses but in plot points central to the arc of Scripture. Many of the most egregious sins centered on food. For instance, the first sin involved rebellious eating, looking to something forbidden in search of goodness (Genesis 3:6). After the exodus, Israel grumbled about their desire for Pharaoh’s pots of meat (Exodus 16:3). Then, when the Lord provided manna in the wilderness, Israel reenacted the sin of Eve when they gathered food on the Sabbath against God’s command (Exodus 16:27–30). But the Bible also commends feasting, both spiritual and physical. Jesus offers himself as the bread of life, given for the nourishment of the saints in exile (John 6:35). And the church looks forward to a meal at the consummation of history, the marriage feast of the Lamb (Revelation 19:9). Between the resurrection and return of the Lamb, we weekly feast on his body and blood, anchoring our minds on what Christ has done and what Christ will do (1 Corinthians 11:23–26). Godly feasting leans into our place in between the times by remembering with gratitude what was and anticipating with joy what will be. All the blessed feasts in the Scriptures are communal celebrations . Something extraordinary has happened; raise a glass to the King! We shouldn’t eat what we regularly eat today; instead, “bring the fattened calf and kill it, and let us eat and celebrate. For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found!” (Luke 15:23–24). We break from feeding ourselves (simply giving our body what it needs) in order to feast (eating and drinking more than we need) as a blessed means of joyously celebrating the work of God in history. But most Christians rarely, if ever, truly feast with mindful gratitude. We just overeat. Spiritual Malnutrition “A companion of gluttons shames his father” (Proverbs 28:7). The glutton does not feast; his god is his belly. He looks for deliverance in his next snack, his next meal, his next drink. He does not fully grasp that man does not live by bread alone. He is not marked by gratitude. The emptiness in his soul, the purposelessness of his life, and the joylessness of his ease have taken root as a spiritual disease. “A glutton is one who raids the icebox for a cure for spiritual malnutrition,” Frederick Buechner observed ( Wishful Thinking , 35). Americans, overall, remain locked in a permanent state of pseudo-feasting. Our culture combines industrial-grade, highly addictive food products and dopamine-seeking, nihilistic joylessness. We mindlessly munch. Often, we hardly even taste or enjoy our food. (A 2026 JAMA study revealed 69 percent of kids and 78 percent of adults use screens while eating.) This is an often-undiscussed problem within the church. I don’t know any Christians who intend to be gluttonous. But I know many, myself included, who have at times felt buried by the shame that follows an episode or season marked by a lack of self-control. We know we cannot make peace with sin, but we aren’t sure what this specific path of repentance looks like. So, when believers recognize the shameful pattern, we try to restrict our calories or go on a diet, which doesn’t stick. We purge and we binge — godless,

content: “Hold the lettuce.” The simple sentence, perhaps stated more frequently than we might hope, captures a crucial hallmark that predominates in the thinking of many. At a recent lunch with a friend, I saw this firsthand. For my friend, it wasn’t just the lettuce. The instructions he gave restrained the cook from adding anything remotely vegetable-like to the hamburger. Notwithstanding my jibe, my friend held fast to his decision. He was the one ordering. And he expected (rightly so!) to be served what he desired. After all, the customer is king. This cluster of expectations animates the modern marketplace. We want products tailored to our specific needs. We seek out services that let us pay only for what we want. We get frustrated when we take the car to a mechanic who not only fixes the problem we knew about but also takes the liberty of repairing other problems (and charging liberally for them). In short, we want (and expect) to be served according to our preferences and felt needs. Innocuous enough when it comes to the morsels on our plates, the reign of personal preferences involves more serious implications when it extends over the rest of life. And in the life of faith, the consequences are serious indeed. For preference-driven faith will, in the end, produce a Christless Christianity. Have It Your Way What do we hope for when we join the church for worship? Parsing motives presents no easy project, especially if there are children in tow or responsibilities for some aspect of the service or fellowship. Few of us have the personal or cognitive space to search out the depths of our hearts en route to the Sunday morning service. But the way home often presents opportunities to interrogate those hidden recesses. The questions we pose shed light on what is in our hearts: “How did you like the sermon this morning?” “Didn’t the worship team nail it today?” We tend to ask not about a confrontation with gospel truth but about measures of personal satisfaction. If our questions begin illuminating this tendency, the answers we give put our motives on clear display: “I thought the pastor did a great job! I really liked . . .” or “Ya know, I just wasn’t feeling it this morning; the sermon didn’t really speak to me.” “Yes, the worship was great!” or “I thought the team was a bit off. Did you hear them mess up on that one song?” So often, whether at the sandwich shop or on the way home from church, preference-driven language bubbles out of our mouths like boiling water from an unwatched pot. For many, our post-service concerns center far too frequently on how well certain aspects of the service met our felt needs. What did I gain from the sermon? Did I enjoy the music? Service to the ascendant self predominates. We reflect on the worship gathering in a manner unsettlingly similar to how we might reflect on a hamburger: It was decent, but I’ve had better elsewhere. I think they overdid the mayonnaise, and I would have preferred sesame rather than a brioche bun. Whether we want to admit it or not, our expectations of being served as we please spill into our perceived relationship to the church’s gathered worship. Those same expectations shape how we approach our Lord. We tend naturally, in our sin, to want merely an affirming savior. We like to hear that Jesus loves sinners so much that he died to win them, for hearing this affirms that our need for forgiveness has been met. We like to hear that his love for his sheep never falters, for hearing this quells the fear that perhaps our snide words or dubious choices or the train wreck of our inner thoughts might put our hope in jeopardy. We like to hear how our Lord railed against the hypocrisy and legalism of the Pharisees, for hearing this makes us smile inwardly, pleased that we are not so pretentious and uptight. Messages such as these leave us content, unruffled, ready to carry on with life as normal, affirmed in our preferred way of life by a (truncated) gospel that accomplishes little b
content_zh:
“抓住生菜。” 这个简单的句子,也许比我们所希望的更频繁地说,抓住了在许多人的思想中占主导地位的关键标志。 最近和一个朋友共进午餐时 我亲眼看到的 对我的朋友来说, 他给厨师的指示 禁止在汉堡里添加任何类似蔬菜的东西

我的朋友坚持他的决定 是他订的 他希望自己所欲达到的, 毕竟客为王. 这一组期望激发出现代市场。 我们需要适合我们具体需要的产品。 我们寻求服务,让我们只为所欲为。

我们感到沮丧的是,我们把车送到一个技工那里,他不仅解决了我们所知道的问题,而且还自由地修复了其他问题(并且对这些问题收取宽松的费用)。 简言之,我们希望(并期望)根据我们的喜好和感受到的需要得到服务。

谈到我们盘子里的泥潭时,个人偏好的统治,如果延续到余生,就会产生更严重的影响。 在信仰的生活中,后果确实很严重。 因为受偏好驱使的信仰,最终会产生出一种没有基督的基督教. 我们加入教堂做礼拜时希望什么?

分析动机并非易事,特别是如果有儿童被拖走或承担某些方面的服务或研究金责任。 我们当中很少有人拥有个人或认知空间,在前往周日早间礼拜的路上去探寻内心深处. 但回家的方式往往为审讯那些隐蔽的休庭提供了机会。

我们提出的问题揭示了我们心中的心事,“你今天早上喜欢讲道吗?” 我们往往不问与福音真相的对抗,而是问个人满意的措施。 如果我们的问题开始说明这一趋势,我们给出的答案清楚地显示了我们的动机:“我认为牧师做了一件伟大的工作!

我真的很喜欢. . . . . . . . . “是的,崇拜是伟大的!”或“我认为队伍有点偏差。 你听到他们把那首歌弄乱了吗?” 所以,无论是在三明治店,还是在从教堂回家的路上,偏好驱动的语言泡从我们嘴里喷出,就像从一个无人观察的锅中取出沸水来.

对许多人来说,我们的服务后关切过于频繁地集中在服务的某些方面在多大程度上满足了我们的需要。 我从布道中得到什么? 我很喜欢音乐吗? 服务于上层的自我占主导地位。 我们以令人不安的方式思考礼拜聚会, 但我在别处生活得更好。

我觉得他们做了蛋黄酱, 我更喜欢芝麻,而不是布洛克包。 无论我们是否愿意承认这一点,我们期望得到服务,因为我们希望与教会所聚集的礼拜的感同身受。 同样的期望决定了我们如何接近我们的主。 我们的罪孽中,自然而然地只想要一个坚定的救世主。

我们喜欢听到耶稣如此地爱罪人,以至于他为了赢得他们的胜利而去死,因为听到这个消息,肯定了我们对宽恕的需要已经得到满足了. 我们想听到,他对他的羊的爱从未动摇,因为听到这种平息的恐惧,也许我们的暗语或可疑的选择,或者我们内心思想的火车残骸会使我们的希望陷入危险.

我们想听听我们的主如何反对法利赛人的虚伪和法西斯主义,因为听到这使我们对内微笑,很高兴我们没有这么自大和紧张。 这样的讯息给我们留下了内容,没有磨损,准备继续正常生活,在我们所偏爱的生活方式中,用一个(经磨练的)福音来证实,这些福音成就不大。

title_zh: 对南亚的IMB事工合作伙伴来说，这“只是一个开始”
content: IMB missionary Derrick Waters spent many days in areas like this market, learning his mission field. He made a breakthrough when he met Siraj, who now confidently shares the gospel. IMB Photo The conversation began on a dusty road in rural South Asia. Siraj, a Christian, told Derrick Waters about his desire to share the gospel with Muslims. How could he begin discussions about Christ with his neighbors? After months of training and encouragement, Siraj said, “I will soon share the gospel with 100 Muslims. I know that at least a few will believe.” Waters and his wife, Rosemary, are International Mission Board missionaries who serve in South Asia. His connection with Siraj is a breakthrough in sharing the gospel in this strongly Muslim region. When he first arrived on the mission field, Waters spent his early days getting acclimated to his new community by riding on the back of a motorcycle with a national partner, traveling around and making contacts. “My partner was trying to convince me not to buy a helmet because he said he was a safe driver,” Waters said, though he chose to wear the headgear. “It’s a good thing I wore the helmet because he drove into the back of a truck with a metal bar hanging out that smacked my head.” Surviving the motorcycle ride led to the relational network that eventually allowed Waters to meet Siraj. After they connected, Siraj introduced Waters to Muslim friends and watched him share the gospel. “At first, that’s how it was with Siraj,” Waters said. “But what I really wanted was for him to get involved in the work himself.” A few months later, Waters and local ministry partners traveled to Siraj’s village to lead evangelism training. They discussed God’s love for all people, learned key vocabulary and practiced a straightforward way to share personal testimonies and the story of Jesus. Then came the hard part. Waters began asking Siraj to lead conversations. Siraj stumbled through explanations and searched for the right words. He sprinkled in newly learned terms and nervously worked through the gospel message. Slowly, confidence replaced fear. After another season of ministry together, Siraj told Waters something he would never forget. “Before you came, I didn’t know how to share the gospel with Muslims,” Siraj said. “I wanted to, but I didn’t know how. Now I feel like I can do it.” The transformation became visible during a gathering arranged by a local teacher. Dozens of parents assembled to listen. Siraj stood before them, visibly nervous. His first few sentences faltered. He started, stopped and restarted. Then, something changed. Finding his rhythm, he shared what he had learned, speaking clearly and naturally. He used the vocabulary he had practiced and explained the message of Jesus with growing confidence. By the end of the meeting, the listeners invited the believers to pray for sick family members. They served snacks and chai, thanked them for coming and invited them back. For Waters, it was a glimpse of what God could do through one willing believer. Today, Siraj continues learning and sharing. He studies from a Bible in the local language that helps him engage more effectively with Muslim friends. He distributes Bibles, shares the gospel with coworkers and regularly speaks with people in the villages. This house is part of the village where Siraj lives with his wife, three daughters and his mother. He supports them on the equivalent of US$4 a day, while also farming his land and studying to earn his Ph.D. IMB Photo His enthusiasm is especially remarkable considering his circumstances. Siraj supports his wife, three daughters and his mother on the equivalent of US$4 a day. He farms a small plot of land and studies for exams in hopes of pursuing a Ph.D.  Despite these responsibilities, he continues making time to tell others about Christ. Currently, Siraj is excited about pursuing his goal of sharing the gospel with 100 Muslims. Whether the number is reached quickly or slowly is not the p
content_zh:
IMB的传教士德里克·沃特斯(Derrick Waters)在这样的市场中度过了许多天,学习了他的任务领域. 他在遇到现在充满信心地分享福音的西拉杰时取得了突破. IMB 图片 对话开始于南亚农村的一条尘埃漫漫的道路. 基督教徒西拉杰告诉德里克·沃特斯,他渴望与穆斯林分享福音.

他怎么能开始和邻居讨论基督? 在经过几个月的培训和鼓励之后,Siraj说:“我很快将与100名穆斯林分享福音。 我知道至少少数人会相信。” 沃特斯和他的妻子罗斯玛丽是国际传教委员会传教士,在南亚服务.

他与Siraj的联系是在这个强烈的穆斯林地区分享福音的一个突破。 当他第一次到达任务领域时,沃特斯花了早期时间,通过骑着一辆摩托车背着国家伙伴,四处旅行和进行接触,来适应他的新社区.

“我的搭档试图说服我不要买头盔,因为他说他是安全的司机,”沃特斯说,尽管他选择戴头盔。 “幸好我戴着头盔, 幸存的摩托车骑行导致关系网最终允许沃特斯与Siraj会面.

在他们建立联系后,西拉杰将沃特斯介绍给穆斯林朋友,看着他分享福音. " 沃特斯说, “但我真正想要的是他自己参与这项工作。” 几个月后,Waters和地方部委合作伙伴前往Siraj村,领导福音派培训。

他们讨论了上帝对所有人的爱,学习了关键词汇,并实践了一种直截了当的方法来分享个人证词和耶稣的故事. 然后是困难的部分。 沃特斯开始要求Siraj领导对话. Siraj偶然通过解释,寻找正确的词句。 他用新学的词汇撒水 紧张地工作 通过福音的信息。

慢慢地,信心取代了恐惧。 经过另一季的部会合作,西拉杰告诉沃特斯一些他永远不会忘记的事情. Siraj说:“在你来之前,我不知道如何与穆斯林分享福音。 “我想, 现在,我觉得我可以做到这一点。” 在当地教师安排的一次集会上,转变变得明显。 数十个家长聚集起来听.

Siraj站在他们面前,明显紧张。 他的最初几句话动摇了。 他开始,停止和重启。 然后,事情变了。 在寻找他的节奏时,他分享了他学到的,清晰而自然地说话. 他使用他所练习的词汇,并以越来越大的信心来解释耶稣的旨意.

会议结束前,听众邀请信徒为生病的家属祈祷. 他们为小吃和小柴服务,感谢他们前来邀请他们回来. 对沃特斯来说,这是上帝通过一个愿意的信徒所能做的一瞥。 今天,Siraj继续学习和分享。

他学习当地语言的圣经,帮助他更有效地与穆斯林朋友接触。 他分发圣经,与同事分享福音,并经常与村里的人交谈. 这所房子是Siraj与妻子,三个女儿和母亲住在一起的村庄的一部分.

他支持他们,相当于每天4美元,同时他还耕种自己的土地,并研究获得博士学位的IMB照片。 考虑到他的情况,他的热情特别引人注目。 Siraj每天以相当于4美元的金额支持他的妻子、三个女儿和母亲。 他种了一小块土地 和学习考试 希望追求博士学位。

尽管承担了这些责任,他继续腾出时间告诉别人基督. 目前,Siraj对追求与100名穆斯林分享福音的目标感到兴奋。 数字是快速还是缓慢的不是p

title_zh: 值得铭记的波兰感恩节
content: In 2018, God provided food for more than 70 people, double the expected number, at a Thanksgiving celebration Cal and Erin Hiebsch helped to host in order to share the gospel by telling the story of God’s provision for the Pilgrims on the first Thanksgiving. IMB Photo For Cal and Erin Hiebsch and their family, Thanksgiving is more than a cherished American holiday. Living and serving in Poland as International Mission Board missionaries, it has become one of their most effective opportunities to build relationships, share their culture and ultimately point people to Christ. While Poland celebrates Christmas and Easter on a grand scale, Thanksgiving is uniquely American. Many Poles are familiar with the holiday and curious about its traditions. Over the years, the Hiebsch family has learned to use that curiosity as a bridge for ministry. “Thanksgiving is probably one of our bigger entrées into American culture,” Cal explained. Each year, they invite friends, neighbors and participants from their English conversation clubs to experience a traditional Thanksgiving meal. For many guests, this is their first encounter with foods such as stuffing, green bean casserole, sweet potato casserole and roasted turkey. Even finding a whole turkey in Poland can be a challenge, since stores more commonly sell turkey breasts and other cuts rather than the whole bird. One Thanksgiving, in particular, is especially memorable for the family. With the help of volunteers, Erin and the culinary crew carefully planned a special celebration. “We had people in four or five different kitchens across the city cooking,” she said. A generous spread of traditional American dishes filled the tables, and invitations had been extended throughout their community. Based on past events, they expected 20 to 30 people to attend. Erin said they planned for “double batches” of each dish with the intention of everybody trying a little of everything that was served. Servers fill up plates as IMB missionaries Cal and Erin Hiebsch and their friends host a Thanksgiving meal in Poland. They planned for 20 or 30 people to show up, but nearly 70 people filled the house. Thankfully, everyone had a full meal and heard the gospel message. IMB Photo As the evening began, guests kept arriving. More came through the doors. Then more. Soon the room was packed. Instead of the anticipated crowd of a few dozen, nearly 70 people showed up. The gathering became standing-room only. “I quietly asked a couple of the volunteer ladies to be praying that there would be enough for everyone,” Erin recalled. Cal was serving as emcee for the event, welcoming guests and sharing the Thanksgiving story. Meanwhile, others were distributing plate after plate of food. Every time someone entered the room, the challenge seemed to grow. How could the food possibly stretch far enough? Yet somehow, it did. People continued to receive full plates. Everyone ate. Conversations flourished around the tables. “The pumpkin pie was especially popular,” Erin said. Guests learned about the history of Thanksgiving and heard how God had provided for the Pilgrims during difficult circumstances. Most importantly, they heard the gospel woven naturally into the evening’s program. When the event finally concluded, the team compared notes and realized an astonishing experience occurred. “We doubled our crowd and had enough food for everyone to have a good Thanksgiving feast,” Cal recalled. To this day, Cal and Erin still talk about that evening. The experience remains difficult to explain, outside of God’s provision. They prepared for one number of guests and served more than twice as many. Whether miraculous or simply an extraordinary provision, the outcome was undeniable. More people than expected were welcomed, fed and exposed to the hope of Christ. An American holiday became a platform for meaningful conversations and gospel witness in a place far from home. content_zh:
2018年,上帝在感恩节庆祝活动Cal和Erin Hiebsch为70多人提供食物,是预期人数的两倍,他们通过讲述上帝在第一个感恩节上为朝圣者提供食物的故事,帮助分享福音. IMB Photo for Cal and Erin Hiebsch and their family, 感恩节不仅仅是一个珍视的美国节日.

在波兰生活和担任国际传教委员会传教士,已经成为他们建立关系、分享其文化并最终指向基督的最有效机会之一。 虽然波兰在大尺度上庆祝圣诞节和复活节,但感恩节是独特的美国人. 许多波兰人对节日很熟悉,对其传统很好奇.

多年来,Hiebsch家族学会了利用这种好奇心作为部委的桥梁。 Cal解释道, “感恩大概是我们美国文化中一个更大的参与者。 每年,他们都会邀请他们英语对话俱乐部的朋友,邻居和参与者体验传统的感恩节餐.

对于许多嘉宾来说,这是他们第一次遇到填料,绿豆砂锅,甜薯砂锅和烤火鸡等食物. 即使是在波兰找到整只火鸡也可能是一个挑战,因为商店更常出售火鸡乳房和其他切口,而不是整只鸟. 特别是感恩节对家庭来说特别值得纪念。

在志愿者的帮助下,艾琳和烹饪船员精心策划了一场特别的庆祝活动. 她说:「我们有四五个不同的厨房, 美国传统菜肴的慷慨推广为餐桌填满了餐桌,在他们的社区内发出了邀请。 根据过去的事件,他们预计有20至30人参加。

Erin说,他们计划将每道菜“分两批”使用,目的是让每个人都尝试一下所服务的东西。 服务器在IMB传教士卡尔和艾琳·希布希及其朋友在波兰举办感恩节晚宴时填满了盘子. 他们计划有20到30人出现,但将近70人填满了房子.

谢天谢地,每个人都吃过一顿饭,听到了福音的信息. IMB 图片 随着夜晚的开始, 客人不断到达。 更多人从门进来了 再来 很快房间就收拾好了. 而不是预期的几十人的人群,近70人出现了. 聚会变成了只有站着的房间。

Erin回忆道, “我悄悄地要求几位女志愿者祈祷, 卡尔当时担任了该活动的代表,欢迎嘉宾并分享感恩节的故事. 与此同时,其他人在分发盘子后再分发食物。 每次有人进入房间,挑战似乎越来越大。 食物怎么够长?

然而,不知何故,它确实如此。 人们继续收到满板。 每个人都吃了。 围绕桌子的议论蓬勃发展. 艾琳说,“南瓜派特别受欢迎。” 嘉宾们了解感恩节的历史,并听说上帝在艰难的情况下为朝圣者提供了什么. 最重要的是,他们听到了晚间节目中自然编织的福音。

当活动最终结束时,团队比较了笔记,意识到发生了惊人的经历. Cal回忆道, “我们的人口增加了一倍, 直到今天,卡尔和艾琳仍在谈论那个晚上. 除了上帝的规定之外,这些经历仍然难以解释。

他们为1位客人做准备,服务人数为2倍以上. 无论是神奇的还是简单的特别的规定,结果都是不可否认的。 更多的人受到基督的欢迎、食物和希望。 一个美国节日成为了在远离家的地方进行有意义的交谈和福音见证的平台.

summary_zh:
我丈夫和我20多岁时 从田纳西州的家搬到南亚 上帝召我们通过国际使命委员会为海外服务,我们激动地与那些还没有机会听的人分享福音。 随着我们开始将生活植根于世界另一边的一个城市,我们很快意识到我们面前的任务是巨大的.

我们被数百万人包围着,其中绝大多数是精神上的损失,并走上了一条通往人类的轨道。
title_zh: 第一人称：我们为什么请您祷告
content: April Bunn, IMB director of global prayer strategies, shows messengers at an SBC annual meeting the latest Loving the Lost prayer resource. IMB Photo April Bunn directs global prayer strategies for the IMB. IMB Photo My husband and I moved from our home in Tennessee to South Asia when we were in our 20s. God called us to serve overseas through the International Mission Board, and we were excited to share the gospel with those who had not yet had an opportunity to hear it. As we began to plant our lives in a city on the other side of the world, we quickly realized the task before us was massive. We were surrounded by millions of people, the vast majority of whom were spiritually lost and on a trajectory to an eternity separated from Christ. We were grappling with a new language, a different culture, unfamiliar foods, homesickness and the list went on. We were overwhelmed. The reality of the lostness around us felt too much to carry. As we turned to God for help, He reminded us that we were not meant to carry this task alone. We had been sent as laborers to the nations, but the Great Commission was given to the whole Church. The Church was our partner in this work. As we began intentionally inviting brothers and sisters in the U.S. to walk with us regularly in prayer, we saw God move in unmistakable ways. They carried the burden of lostness with us, and they also rejoiced with us as we saw God work. We had been sent as laborers to the nations, but the Great Commission was given to the whole Church. The Church was our partner in this work. Today, after two decades in South Asia, I have the privilege of encouraging and equipping believers to pray for people and places around the world through my work with the IMB. In doing so, I’m continually reminded that God’s mission is His work, and we are utterly dependent on Him to accomplish it. Missionaries can faithfully go, learn languages, share the gospel and disciple believers, but they cannot change hearts. God can. That is why we ask you to pray. Prayer is strategic to the Great Commission, and e very believer can take part in it. As the Church, we are living between the giving of the Great Commission and its culmination in the great multitude we see in Revelation 7:9, where people from every nation, tribe, people and language will stand before the throne worshiping God together. Until that day, we go to take the good news to a world in need. And we pray, asking God to do what only He can do. Through prayer, every believer, regardless of age or location, can intercede for places we may never be able to go ourselves. No country or people group is closed to the work of the Spirit through the prayers of God’s people. We may not see every answer to those prayers in our lifetime; some will only become visible when we stand before the throne and see the faces of those God drew to Himself. Until then, we keep praying. April Bunn, IMB director of global prayer strategies, shows messengers at an SBC annual meeting the latest Loving the Lost prayer resource. The new Loving the Lost is available for free from the IMB. IMB Photo Paul tells us in Colossians 4:2 to “continue steadfastly in prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving.” To be watchful means we are paying attention and expecting God to work. The Mixtec people of Mexico have reminded me what that kind of watchful, steadfast prayer looks like. Beginning in 2008, IMB missionaries serving among the Mixtec began sharing prayer requests with IMB’s prayer office so they could be shared widely and more believers could join them in prayer. The requests were simple. Pray for open hearts. Pray for opportunities to share Bible stories in the Mixtec language. Pray for people to help make Scripture accessible. Pray for God to open doors. Month after month and year after year, people prayed for access to villages, for the first believers, for courage in the face of persecution. Today there is a growing fellowship of Mixtec believers. title_zh: 持续向慕拉第献金奉献，有助于为中东的失聪群体提供福音传播的机会
content: An IMB missionary among the Deaf records a Bible story in sign language. IMB Photo Every dollar you give to the Lottie Moon offering goes to support missionaries like Noah Lewis who live and serve among the lost. Will you consider giving today? Noah Lewis couldn’t help signing along with a worship song playing in the background as Deaf friends gathered in his home for dinner. The International Mission Board appoints missionaries who are both Deaf and hearing to serve among the global Deaf. Many missionaries learn sign language for the first time, while others use their American Sign Language to more quickly learn global sign languages. IMB Photo The International Mission Board missionary was sitting in the living room with his roommate and two friends while others prepared food nearby. As a young, single adult, simply opening the doors to his home in the Middle East has created some of his most fruitful opportunities for gospel conversations. That evening, Lewis was stirred to worship the Lord. “I just love worshiping in sign language because it’s a full-body experience,” Lewis said. Lewis, who is hearing, began signing the song in American Sign Language. Across the room, one of his Muslim friends watched intently. When the song ended, his friend told him it was beautiful and asked to see another. Lewis explained that Christians use songs to worship God. His friend compared what he had seen to hearing the Islamic call to prayer. The exchange opened an opportunity for Lewis to explain Christian worship and why Christians worship Jesus. When his friend asked to see more, Lewis continued signing songs from the playlist. “He was just really captivated by it,” Lewis said. “It really felt like in that moment the Spirit was working in his heart.” The conversation did not end with a profession of faith. Instead, it became another step in a friendship where Lewis has watched spiritual curiosity grow over time. During Ramadan, the same friend asked about fasting. On another night, he asked how Christians pray. Each question has allowed Lewis to explain what Christians believe and why he follows Jesus. Those conversations reflect much of Lewis’ ministry. He has served in the Middle East for nearly a year and a half, spending much of his time learning sign language and building relationships in the local Deaf community. Learning sign language, like learning any language, requires time, practice and immersion in the community that uses it. For Lewis, that process has looked different from the experience of missionaries who can spend several hours each day in a formal language school. There are no comparable sign language centers where he serves, so much of his language learning happens through relationships with Deaf friends. Although Lewis has not had a dedicated language tutor since arriving on the field, personal relationships help him develop a strong conversational understanding of the sign language used where he serves. The process has also drawn him more deeply into the Deaf community he came to reach. “I want to genuinely learn about their language,” he said. “I want to be friends with them. I want to know who they are.” As Lewis’ ability to communicate grows, relationships deepen and opportunities to share the gospel follow. Even when he doesn’t know the exact sign he needs, friends help him find ways to communicate biblical truths. Lewis has learned to faithfully use the language he has while continuing to grow in his ability to communicate the gospel clearly. An IMB worker among the Deaf records a Bible story. Generous giving to the Lottie Moon Christmas Offering supports missions among the global Deaf. IMB Photo When the plan disappeared That dependence on God came into clearer focus during a recent trip to Central Asia. Lewis currently lives and serves in the Middle East, but he arrived on the field with a long-term desire to serve in Central Asia. His recent trip allowed him to learn more about the culture, Deaf communities a
content_zh:
一名IMB在聋人中的传教士用手语记录圣经故事. IMB照片 你给洛蒂月球的每一美元 都用来支持传教士 比如诺亚·刘易斯 你会考虑今天给钱吗? 当聋人朋友聚集在家中吃饭时,

国际代表团委员会任命聋人和听力传教士在全球聋人中任职。 许多传教士首次学习手语,而其他传教士则使用他们的美国手语更快地学习全球手语.

IMB照片 国际传教委员会传教士与他的室友和两个朋友坐在客厅里,而其他人则在附近准备食物. 作为一个年轻、单身的成年人,只要打开通往他在中东的家的大门,就为他的福音对话创造了一些最富有成果的机会。 当晚,刘易斯被激起崇拜主.

「我只是喜欢手语崇拜, 正在听话的刘易斯开始用美国手语签署歌曲. 在房间里,他的一个穆斯林朋友故意观看。 歌曲结束的时候,他的朋友告诉他这很美丽,并请求见另一首. 刘易斯解释说,基督徒使用歌曲来崇拜上帝.

他的朋友比较了他所看到的听到的伊斯兰祈祷的呼声. 这次交流为刘易斯解释基督教崇拜和基督徒为何崇拜耶稣提供了机会. 当他的朋友要求看到更多时,刘易斯继续从播放列表上签名歌曲. 刘易斯说:“他只是被它迷住了。”

“在那个时刻,精神确实在他心中发挥作用。” 对话没有以信仰职业结束。 相反,它成为友谊的又一个步骤,刘易斯目睹了精神好奇心随时间推移而增长. 斋月期间,同友问斋事. 在另一个晚上,他问基督徒如何祈祷.

每个问题都让刘易斯解释基督徒相信什么,为什么他跟随耶稣. 这些谈话反映了刘易斯部的许多情况。 他在中东服务了近一年半,花了很多时间学习手语,在当地聋人社区建立关系.

学习手语,就像学习任何语言一样,需要时间,练习和沉浸在使用手语的社区中. 对刘易斯来说,这一进程与传教士的经历不同,传教士可以每天在一所正式语言学校中度过几个小时。

他所服务的手语中心并不存在类似的手语中心,所以他的许多语言学习都是通过与聋人朋友的关系发生的. 虽然刘易斯自到达球场后便没有专门的语言辅导员,但个人关系帮助他发展出对他所服务的手语的强烈的对话理解.

这一过程还使他更深入地融入了他所接触的聋人社区。 他说:“我想真正了解他们的语言。” “我想与他们成为朋友。 我想知道他们是谁。” 随着刘易斯沟通能力的增长,关系加深,分享福音的机会随之而来。

即使他不知道自己需要什么具体标志, 刘易斯学会了忠实使用他拥有的语言,同时继续增强他明确传达福音的能力. 一个IMB工人在聋人中记录了一个圣经故事. 慷慨地给洛蒂月亮圣诞节 提供全球聋人中的支持任务

IMB 图片 当计划消失时 在最近访问中亚期间,这种对上帝的依赖得到了更明确的关注。 刘易斯目前在中东生活和服役,但他远期带着在中亚服役的愿望赶到现场. 他最近的旅行使他能够更多地了解文化,聋人社区

summary_zh:

title_zh: 俄亥俄州派遣庆祝活动确认33名IMB传教士为全球服务
content: Participants at the IMB Sending Celebration on Nov. 9, 2026, celebrated God's faithfulness in sending 33 new missionaries to the nations. Held at the Sugarcreek campus of First Baptist Kettering near Dayton, Ohio, the event launched the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio annual gathering. For security reasons, some newly appointed missionaries are not publicly identified. IMB Photo God continues to call His people to carry the gospel to the ends of the earth. During a Sending Celebration Nov. 9 at the Sugarcreek Campus of First Baptist Church Kettering, near Dayton, Ohio, 33 International Mission Board missionaries stood before family, friends and supporters, affirming their obedience to that call. Trustees of the IMB appointed the fully supported missionaries who represent 10 states – including two candidates from Ohio – and many Southern Baptist churches committed to sending and sustaining those called by God to go to the mission field. Senior Pastor Chad Keck welcomed those in attendance, sharing his appreciation for the partnership with Southern Baptist churches to cooperatively send and support missionaries. The Sending Celebration is meeting in conjunction with the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio. Chad Keck, senior pastor of First Baptist Kettering near Dayton, Ohio, left, and Jeremy Westbrook, executive director-treasurer of the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio, right, welcome guests gathered for the IMB Sending Celebration, which kicked off the convention’s annual gathering. IMB Photo Among those who shared their stories include a couple who answered an unexpected call later in life, a couple who are returning to Albania and to people they could not forget; and a couple who moved from welcoming the nations in Canada to going to Fiji. All of them shared their stories before the Sending Celebration. Unexpected invitation to go On Dec. 5, 2025, what seemed like an ordinary FaceTime call became a turning point for Rob Boss. As he spoke with his daughter, Hannah, during her IMB training, Rob sensed God speaking clearly to his heart: “You can do this too.” The impression was unexpected. After decades of writing, Christian education, seminary teaching and active support of missions, overseas service had never been part of Rob and Stephanie Boss’ plans. “It wasn’t an audible voice, but it was so clear,” Rob said. “It was Him. It was so kind and so gentle and so encouraging.” The moment drove him to his knees in surrender. When Stephanie came home later that day, he told her he believed God was calling them to the nations. Her response was immediate. “Thrilled is the right answer,” she said. The next day, the couple contacted the IMB and began the application process. Though missions had long been part of their family’s story, Rob and Stephanie Boss sensed God leading them to overseas service while encouraging their daughter, Hannah, during her missionary training. Sent by Wedgwood Baptist Church in Fort Worth, Texas, they are now headed to Colombia, where they will serve through theological education. IMB Photo Looking back, the Bosses see the Lord’s hand preparing them long before they realized where He was leading. “God brought us together in the summer of 1990 at Glorieta, New Mexico, where we met and married,” Stephanie said during the Sending Celebration. What followed was years of ministry, teaching, parenting and navigating life’s unexpected turns, which taught them to hold plans loosely and trust God completely. “We did not have a clue about what life held in front of us,” Stephanie said. “We just knew we wanted to follow the Lord.” Their calling also continues a family legacy. Rob’s mother served with the IMB in Africa after retirement, helping inspire Hannah’s service in South Korea. Now, three generations of the same family have answered God’s call to the nations. Rob and Stephanie expressed deep gratitude for their sending church, Wedgwood Baptist Church in Fort Worth, whose strong commitment to missions
content_zh:
2026年11月9日的IMB送信庆典的参与者,庆祝上帝向各国派遣33名新传教士的忠诚. 该活动在俄亥俄州代顿附近的第一浸信会Kettling的Sugarcreek校园举行,在俄亥俄州发起了浸信会州议会年会。 出于安全考虑,一些新任命的传教士没有公开身份.

IMB图片神继续呼叫 他的族人将福音传到地底 11月9日,在俄亥俄州代顿附近的第一浸信会Kettling教堂的Sugarcreek校区,33名国际传教委员会传教士站在家人、朋友和支持者面前,申明他们服从这一呼吁。

IMB的受托人任命了代表10个州的全力支持的传教士 — — 包括俄亥俄州的两名候选人 — — 以及许多南方浸信会教会承诺将那些被上帝召唤去传教的传教士送去并维持下去.

高级牧师Chad Keck欢迎与会者,与他一样感谢与美南浸信会教会合作派遣和支持传教士。 送教庆典会与俄亥俄州的浸信会州会议同时举行.

俄亥俄州代顿附近第一浸信会Ketting的资深牧师查德·凯克(Chad Keck)左翼,俄亥俄州浸信会执行董事兼创始人杰里米·韦斯特布鲁克(Jeremy Westbrook)右翼欢迎前来参加IMB送信庆典的来宾,这驱散了大会的年度集会。

在分享自己故事的人中,有一对夫妇在生活后期意外地接了电话,一对夫妇正在返回阿尔巴尼亚,一对夫妇无法忘记;一对夫妇从欢迎加拿大各国搬到斐济。 他们都分享了他们的故事 在送信庆典之前。 意外邀请 Dec 上。

5, 2025, 看起来像一个普通的FaceTime电话成为Rob Boss的转折点. 当他和他的女儿汉娜在IMB训练期间交谈时,罗布感应到上帝对他说的很清楚:“你也可以这样做。” 印象出乎意料。

经过几十年的写作、基督教教育、神学院教学和对使团的积极支持,海外服务从未成为罗布和斯蒂芬妮·博斯计划的一部分。 Rob说, “这不是一个声音, “这是他。 它是如此善良和温柔,如此鼓舞人心。” 那一刻,他被迫跪在地上投降。

当斯蒂芬妮当天晚些时候回家时,他告诉她,他相信上帝在召唤他们到各国. 她立即作出反应。 她说,“令人惊叹的是正确的答案。” 次日,夫妇联系IMB,开始了申请程序.

虽然传教团早就是他们家庭故事的一部分,但罗布和史蒂芬妮·博斯感知到,在传教团训练期间,他们带领他们到海外服务,同时鼓励他们的女儿汉娜。 由德克萨斯州沃思堡的韦奇伍德浸信会(Wedgwood Baptist Church)派遣,他们现在前往哥伦比亚,通过神学教育服务.

IMB照片回想起来,老板们看到主的手 在他们意识到在哪里之前很早就准备了 他是领导。 " 1990年夏天,上帝把我们带到了新墨西哥州格洛里埃塔,我们在那里相遇并结婚。 " Stephanie在送货庆典上说。

接下来是多年的教职、教职、养育和过着意想不到的转折,教他们松动计划,完全相信上帝。 Stephanie说:“我们不知道我们面前的生活是什么。” 我们只知道我们想跟随主。 他们的召唤也延续了家庭遗产。

罗布的母亲退休后在非洲为IMB效力,帮助激励汉娜在韩国服役. 现在,同一家庭的三代人响应了上帝向各国发出的呼吁。 Rob和Stephanie深表感谢他们派来的教会Worth堡的Wedgwood浸信会教堂,他们坚定致力于使命

title: IMB missionaries in place, prepared to encourage Senegal’s churches toward Youth Olympics outreach
summary: As athletes and spectators from around the world fill the streets of Senegal for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, missionaries and local believers are praying the event will leave behind more than medals and memories. For Carson West, an International Mission Board missionary serving in Senegal, the Games represent a unique opportunity not only to engage visitors with the gospel but also to mobilize local churches to take a more active role in evangelism long after the Olympic flame is exting
summary_zh:

content: A Senegalese Christian shares the gospel with event volunteers during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo As athletes and spectators from around the world fill the streets of Senegal for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, missionaries and local believers are praying the event will leave behind more than medals and memories. For Carson West, an International Mission Board missionary serving in Senegal, the Games represent a unique opportunity not only to engage visitors with the gospel but also to mobilize local churches to take a more active role in evangelism long after the Olympic flame is extinguished. “This is the first Olympic event ever held on the continent of Africa,” West said. “For us, it was an opportunity to ask, ‘What are we going to do with this?’” The Youth Olympic Games, which began Oct. 31 and end Nov. 13, are taking place across three host cities: Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. Event organizers expect nearly 2,700 athletes, ages 14-17, to participate in 35 sports and represent more than 200 delegations. The Games have drawn a million spectators, and West reported more than 6,000 event volunteers are staffing all the venues. With so many people gathering in Senegal, West and his team concentrated on preparing Senegalese churches for evangelistic opportunities. “We could run and hide, or we could do this thing,” West said, recalling an early conversation with teammates. “We decided we were going to do this thing.” The 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, is the first Olympic event held on the continent of Africa. IMB Photo West serves as team leader for IMB work in Senegal, where ministry efforts focus on three areas: gospel engagement, church advancement and community development. The Youth Olympic outreach naturally aligns with the first two priorities. “Our approach has been to mobilize the local church,” he said. “This is their backyard.” Instead of relying on a large influx of international volunteers, though there is one volunteer team from the United States serving, the strategy has centered on equipping local believers. Senegal has four Baptist churches in the greater Dakar area. Many leaders representing the congregations, as well as other ministry partners, participated in evangelism training designed specifically for the Games. Church leaders and ministry partners in Senegal participate in an evangelism training session specifically designed to share the gospel during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo A key outreach method involves trading commemorative pins, a familiar Olympic tradition. Volunteers use the exchange as a natural conversation starter before offering gospel-centered materials. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code connected to a digital engagement platform adapted from previous Olympic and World Cup outreaches. Visitors who scan the code are directed to online resources and can connect with trained digital responders. Experienced volunteers in the U.S. are helping provide follow-up conversations. “We’re building on strategies that have been used effectively in previous Olympic Games,” West said. “It’s an easy, non-intimidating way to start gospel conversations.” Trading commemorative pins is an Olympic tradition. Volunteers use these pins to start gospel-driven conversations during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code that connects people to trained digital responders. IMB Photo The effort extends beyond Dakar. IMB teams and church partners are positioned in each of the three host cities. An IMB team, which includes three global missionary partners, is helping coordinate outreach efforts in Diamniadio, and an IMB team along with a Baptist church is organizing efforts in Saly. West believes the greatest potential impact may be felt not among international visitors but among Senegalese believers themselves. Senegal is approximately 95% Muslim and 0.2% evangelical. title: IMB seeks teachers, healthcare workers, business professionals to serve as missionaries
summary: When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. title_zh: IMB寻求教师、医护人员、商业专业人士担任传教士
content: IMB missionary Dr. Heidi Haun, left, checks on patients at Baptist Medical Centre in Nalerigu, Ghana. There are needed roles for IMB missionaries in healthcare, ministering to the needs of local populations and utilizing this time to minister to spiritual needs. IMB Photo When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. Doreen Baker, IMB director of TCK (third culture kid or missionary kid) education, sees a constant need for education professionals. Teachers are needed in international schools, which cover a variety of global educational entities, and in other settings to provide for missionary kids and their educational needs. “Teachers are significant in that not only are they providing instruction for students, but they are an integral part of the core missionary task ,” Baker said. “We also have great needs for consultants to support our families on the field with their children’s education in many ways.” Baker previously served 25 years teaching in Asia and experienced how education creates access to missions where traditional pathways may be limited. IMB missionary Ellie Bohrer teaches a 12th grade World Views class at Black Forest Academy in Germany. The IMB is seeking other educators, like Bohrer, who are willing to use their skills on the mission field. IMB Photo Scott Ray, IMB senior director of global deployment, noted that many missionary positions go unfilled simply because they fall outside traditional perceptions of missionary service. He said professional skills can provide both practical ministry support and access to countries where traditional missionary visas are difficult to obtain. Opportunities exist for finance professionals, veterinarians, medical workers, Send Relief personnel and others. Healthcare remains one of the most strategic areas in demand. Tom Hicks, IMB director of global health strategies, said many medical professionals have the wrong perception about mission work. “We do have an issue where people will select out because they don’t think that what they do is useful on the mission field,” he said. In reality, Hicks said many areas across the globe are increasingly seeking family medicine physicians, internists, pediatricians, pediatric nurse practitioners, OB providers, physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech pathologists and lactation consultants. The need is especially significant in sub-Saharan Africa, where young populations create a growing demand for pediatric care. Healthcare professionals also provide a unique advantage in countries that restrict missionary activity. “Missionaries with a vocational value, like healthcare missionaries, have opportunities to go places that others can’t go,” Hicks said. Another often-overlooked ministry is member care, which focuses on the spiritual, emotional, mental and relational health of IMB missionaries. Chris Martin is the IMB director of global member care. “Member care missionaries stand alongside those missionaries that are thought of traditionally as church planters or evangelists and support them,” Martin said. Many who serve in these roles come from counseling backgrounds and help missionaries navigate stress, conflict, grief and other challenges that can affect long-term ministry effectiveness. Martin compares their role to Aaron and Hur in Exodus 19, holding up Moses’ arms during battle, strengthening those serving on the front lines. IMB missionary Glen Garner uses his business skills and experience as the logistics director for missionaries serving globally. He lives in Lima, Peru, with his wife, Shannon

IMB正在寻找其他教育者,比如波尔,他们愿意在任务领域运用自己的技能. IMB Photo Scott Ray是IMB全球部署的高级主任,他指出,许多传教士职位由于不属于传教士服务的传统观念而无人填补. 他说,专业技能既能提供实用的部委支助,也能进入传统传教签证难以获得的国家。 金融专业人员、兽医、医务工作者、派遣救济人员和其他人都有机会。 保健仍然是需求最有战略意义的领域之一。 全球卫生战略的IMB主任汤姆·希克斯(Tom Hicks)说,许多医疗专业人员对任务工作的看法是错误的. 他表示:「我们确实有个问题, 人们会选择出局, 事实上,Hicks说,全球许多地区正在越来越多地寻找家庭医学医生、实习医生、儿科医生、儿科护士、产科医生、物理治疗师、职业治疗师、语言病理学家和哺乳期咨询师。 这种需求在撒哈拉以南非洲尤为重要,那里的青年人口对儿科护理的需求日益增加。 在限制传教活动的国家,保健专业人员也提供了独特的优势。 「有职业价值的使团, 另一个经常被忽略的部是成员护理,重点是IMB传教士的精神、情感、心理和关系健康。 克里斯·马丁是IMB全球会员关怀的总监. Martin说,“会员关心传教士与那些传统上被认为是教会植树人或福音传教士的传教士站在一起并支持他们。” 担任这些角色的许多人来自咨询背景,帮助传教士应对压力、冲突、悲痛和其他挑战,这些挑战可能影响部委的长期效力。 马丁将他们的角色比作出埃及19号的Aaron和Hur,在战斗中举起摩西的手臂,强化了在前线服役的人. IMB传教士格伦·加纳(英语:Glen Garner)利用其作为在全球服务的传教士的后勤主任的业务技能和经验. 他和妻子香农住在秘鲁利马

title_zh: IMB传教士通过新信徒和当地教会看到神在工作
content: In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo Twenty minutes had passed already. The sun was going down, and they were looking everywhere, but they only saw men in the park. Sophia, an International Mission Board missionary, joined another IMB missionary and Maryam, a South Asian Christian. They went to the park to share the gospel, but approaching a man in their Muslim-majority city was out of the question. They kept walking and watching. Even if they went home without a single conversation, Sophia knew Maryam would want to try again. This woman who had grown up with a distrust of Muslims, now searched a park for a Muslim woman to tell about Jesus. When Sophia first invited her along, Maryam never imagined a Muslim could come to know Jesus. But the more they went out sharing the gospel together, the more God softened her heart. “One day, I found she was sharing in the park by herself, without me,” Sophia said with a laugh. These days, she shares regularly — with classmates, with rickshaw drivers, with women in the park, when she can find them. God transformed Maryam’s heart. He could transform this walk through the park, too. “So we stopped,” Sophia said, “and prayed, ‘God, give us just one woman to talk to.’” Then they spotted her — a girl sitting alone on a bench. Meeting the girl on the bench She looked like other conservative Muslim women in the area, covered in black except for her face. They approached casually, not wanting to frighten her. It was Eid al-Adha – “one of the biggest Muslim holidays here,” Sophia said. They greeted her and asked about her holiday plans. Her name was Tara, and she wasn’t intimidated at all. “You may think I’m a Muslim from the way I dress,” she said, “but actually in my heart, I have left Islam.” “I was a little shocked,” Sophia said, hearing such a bold statement from a stranger. Tara told them she was a university student at a conservative Islamic school, but she had grown disillusioned and discontent with the religion. “ I don’t believe in Islam anymore,” Tara said. Without knowledge of God, she had no one to pray to, and it left her lonely. She’d been searching — Buddhism and Hinduism from friends, even a meeting with atheists, who struck her as unhappy, following only themselves. “Do you know any Christians?” Sophia asked. “Would you like to hear what we believe?” “Sure, please share.” They read about Jesus’ birth, and Tara was hungry for more. When she asked about church, Sophia described their congregation of about 40 believers, many from a Muslim background. Though she wasn’t ready to visit the church, Tara continued her interest in learning. Sophia and Maryam met with her every week in coffee shops, tea shops, Sophia’s home, wherever they could talkthat wasn’t too loud or have “too many ears and eyes” observing them. Finding her closest friend They read through the Gospel of John. One November day in a coffee shop, they reached the passage on the Samaritan woman at the well, and Sophia noticed Tara was crying. “Tara, I see you have tears,” Sophia said. “Let’s stop. Let’s talk about it .” That day, Tara prayed to receive Christ. Soon after, she wanted to visit the church, though nervous how believers would receive her in a hijab. “They will love you,” Sophia told her. “Don’t worry.” Tara went and was welcomed. That Christmas, 80 people packed Sophia’s apartment, singing and dancing in circles. Across the room, Sophia saw Tara, wearing red Christmas garland like a scarf and a smile stretched across her face. “Tara grew up very conservative – music was not even allowed in her home. But now she’s dancing, worshiping the Lord with us with music and songs.” In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo That spring, Tara was baptized.

Tara说:「我不再相信伊斯兰教了。 没有上帝的知晓,她没有任何人可以祈祷,这让她孤独. 她从朋友那里寻找佛教和印度教, 甚至和无神论者会面, “你们认识任何基督徒吗?” 索菲亚问。 你们告诉我吧! 他们读到耶稣的出生,Tara更渴望更多。 当她问起教堂时,索菲亚描述了他们大约40名信徒的聚会,其中许多来自穆斯林背景. Tara继续学习。 Sophia和Maryam每周在咖啡店、茶店、Sophia家相会, 找到她最亲近的朋友 他们通过"约翰福音"阅读. 11月一日在一家咖啡店里,他们到达了井上撒玛利亚女人的通道,索菲亚注意到塔拉正在哭泣. “塔拉,我看到你有眼泪,”索菲亚说。 " 让我们停下来吧。 让我们谈谈。 当天,塔拉祈祷接受基督. 不久后,她想参观教堂,虽然担心信徒会如何用头巾接见她. “他们会爱你,”索菲亚告诉她。 “别担心。 Tara去了,受到欢迎。 80人收拾了索菲亚的公寓, 在房间对面,索菲亚看见了塔拉,身穿红色的圣诞外衣,像围巾和微笑被伸到她脸上. " Tara长大后非常保守——她家甚至不允许音乐. 现在她正在跳舞,用音乐和歌曲与我们一起崇拜上帝。 在南亚,玛丽安和一位当地牧师为新信徒塔拉施洗. IMB的传教士与当地的信徒和教会一起工作,完成"大委员会". IMB 相片 当年春天,塔拉被洗礼.

title_zh: 神通过IMB在意大利的传教士保持忠诚
content: The eastern face of St. Peter's Basilica in the Vatican City in Rome, Italy, is famous for its central balcony from which popes give their papal addresses. Most people in Rome have at least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” IMB Photo In the city where Jason and Lizzy Davis serve, some steps have a lot of meaning. And the meaning is different for them than it is for the thousands who travel there to visit that site. “If you come to Rome, you can come to a place called the Holy Steps,” Jason said. “People go there, and they’ll crawl up on their knees and pray the rosary all the way up.” From the top of the steps, a mural depicting Jesus on the Cross looks down on those making the pilgrimage. For Jason and Lizzy, it’s a spiritual experience, a picture of a religion that asks people to earn their way to Jesus. “That’s really the opposite of what the gospel is. The gospel is Jesus saying, ‘No, you can’t do it . . . no matter how good you think you are,’” they said. Most people in Rome have at the very least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism, as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” Jason explained, “It’s where the Pope lives in the Vatican. It’s very much part of the religion and culture. It’s all intertwined here.” An ‘unavoidable’ call Jason and Lizzy are investing their lives as International Mission Board missionaries in Rome, Italy, to share the truth of the gospel. The Davises partner with national believers through a new church plant, and they’re seeking to plant more churches within the city. Lizzy said for her, the call to missions was unavoidable. “I grew up as a third culture kid, or a missionary kid. My parents were on the mission field, as were my grandparents, all with the International Mission Board.” Then her family moved to Virginia for her dad to work for IMB’s home office staff. As a middle schooler and high schooler, every time Lizzy heard about the need for the gospel to go forth, she felt a burden, a “burning” in her heart. She didn’t know what God would do with that, but she had a feeling she would see one day. Now, years later, she and Jason spend their time trying to find as many opportunities as they can to invite people into their home so they can share the hope of Jesus with them. That can mean Bible study or simply sharing a meal. ‘Completely lost’ Jason has been surprised by just how often people are willing to talk about faith. “You can get into spiritual conversations very quickly with people, especially if you’re just open and honest with them.” Lizzy shared that one of the easiest ways to do this is to be willing to let your day be interrupted. “That’s something I’ve seen Jason do firsthand in our neighborhood. He walks down the street, and everybody knows him because he stops and takes the time to ask them questions about their families, gets to know people, gets to know the newspaper stand guy and the guy at the fruit stand and the grocery store ladies.” She emphasized that caring about people is “what Christ would do.” The Davises, whose previous mission service prevents their photos from being published, live in a neighborhood of about 130,000 people. Their church of 15 people is the only evangelical congregation there. Lizzy said the area is “truly a lost, completely lost, dark neighborhood” with people who have never heard the gospel. Thousands more come to their area on a religious quest. The Davis family’s neighborhood is home to the Basilica Papale di San Paolo (the Papal Basilica of Saint Paul), one of the city’s four major basilicas. “So we get a lot of people coming on spiritual journeys, visiting our neighborhood, seeking some sort of spiritual experience. And oftentimes it’s just trying to earn their salvation,” she added. Jason described this environment as “a genuine need for people to actually hear the gospel and know that their sins can be forgiven and they can have an assurance of that.” IMB missionaries Jason and Liz
