summary_zh: 在基督徒抵抗运动开始一百年后，墨西哥主教们提议从真相、良心自由、和解与对话的角度来审视这段痛苦的历史事件。
title_zh: 墨西哥主教们在基督徒抵抗运动发起一百周年之际发表的牧函——Infovaticana博客
content: A cien años del inicio de la resistencia cristera, los obispos mexicanos proponen leer aquel doloroso episodio histórico desde la verdad, la libertad de conciencia, la reconciliación y el compromiso de una fe dispuesta a hacerse servicio A cien años del inicio de la resistencia cristera, los obispos de México han dirigido al país una carta pastoral que busca recuperar uno de los episodios más dolorosos, complejos y controvertidos de la historia nacional sin convertirlo en instrumento de revancha, polarización o legitimación de la violencia. Bajo el título ¡Viva Cristo Rey! Su fe, nuestra memoria; su testimonio, nuestra misión, el documento propone una lectura histórica, teológica, espiritual, jurídica y pastoral de aquellos acontecimientos, pero, sobre todo, formula una pregunta dirigida a los creyentes de nuestro tiempo: ¿Qué significa hoy mantener viva una fe por la que otros estuvieron dispuestos a entregar la existencia? La carta no celebra la guerra ni presenta la resistencia armada como modelo de acción cristiana para el presente. Su punto de partida es otro, recordar la fidelidad de un pueblo que, en medio de la persecución, continuó rezando en sus hogares, bautizando a sus hijos, protegiendo a sus sacerdotes, celebrando clandestinamente los sacramentos y defendiendo la libertad de conciencia frente a un Estado que pretendió administrar las convicciones religiosas como si fueran una concesión del poder. Los obispos establecen desde el comienzo una diferencia indispensable entre el conflicto bélico, con sus errores, excesos, responsabilidades y heridas, y el testimonio de quienes murieron sin renunciar a su fe. Los mártires, subraya el documento, no son recordados porque hubieran matado por Cristo, sino porque murieron por Él y, en numerosos casos, perdonaron a sus verdugos. No se trata de recuperar un grito de guerra, sino la fuerza espiritual de una conciencia que se negó a ser sometida. El episcopado propone un triple ejercicio de memoria histórica, valoración del martirio y compromiso cristiano con la vida, la dignidad humana y la paz. Al recorrer la carta aparece una convicción transversal, la memoria solo es auténticamente cristiana cuando conduce a la conversión, ayuda a sanar las heridas, impide la repetición de las injusticias y se transforma en misión. Ese propósito exige comenzar por “un breve recuento del conflicto religioso”, título del primer capítulo y punto de entrada para entender que la confrontación no surgió repentinamente en 1926. Sus antecedentes se remontan a la formación del Estado mexicano después de la Independencia, cuando comenzaron a enfrentarse dos proyectos de nación. Uno reconocía al catolicismo como fundamento del orden social; el otro pretendía limitar la influencia institucional de la Iglesia para consolidar un Estado liberal, soberano y progresivamente secular. La Constitución de 1857 y las Leyes de Reforma representaron un momento decisivo en ese proceso. Establecieron la separación entre la Iglesia y el Estado, limitaron la propiedad eclesiástica y modificaron la presencia de la institución religiosa en la educación y la vida civil. Para sus promotores fueron disposiciones indispensables para modernizar al país; para la Iglesia y numerosos católicos significaron una intervención hostil sobre espacios que consideraban esenciales para su identidad y misión. La carta reconoce, sin embargo, que la secularización no ocurrió de manera inmediata ni eliminó el profundo arraigo del catolicismo en la vida nacional. La fe continuó presente en las costumbres, las familias, la educación, las fiestas y las formas comunitarias de organización. En ese contexto cobró fuerza el catolicismo social, inspirado en buena medida por la encíclica Rerum novarum de 1891. Surgieron organizaciones obreras, asociaciones juveniles y femeninas, cajas de ahorro para campesinos, escuelas nocturnas, centros de ayuda mutua, medios de comunicación y proyectos de participación política. title: RED WEEK PER RICORDARE I CRISTIANI PERSEGUITATI
summary: Anche quest’anno, nonostante il disinteresse dei media, dal 15 al 22 novembre la Fondazione Pontificia Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre ha dato vita al Red Week per ricordare che in tutto il mondo milioni
summary_zh: 今年，尽管媒体不感兴趣，但教宗基金会“援助受苦教会”仍于11月15日至22日举办了“红色周”活动，以提醒人们在全球范围内有数百万
title_zh: 红色周，纪念受迫害的基督徒
content: Anche quest’anno, nonostante il disinteresse dei media, dal 15 al 22 novembre la Fondazione Pontificia Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre ha dato vita al Red Week per ricordare che in tutto il mondo milioni di persone sono discriminate o perseguitate per la loro fede, in particolare le tante comunità cristiane che vivono in contesti dove la loro libertà religiosa subisce gravi violazioni. Per farlo, luoghi di culto, monumenti ed edifici pubblici in questa settimana si sono illuminate di rosso in tante nazioni contemporaneamente in occasione della Red Week, Dal 2015, sono stati illuminati luoghi di culto e monumenti fra i più iconici del mondo: dalla Fontana di Trevi a Roma al monumento del Cristo Redentore di Rio de Janeiro, dalla Basilica della Sagrada Familia di Barcellona a quella del Sacro Cuore di Parigi. La libertà religiosa in pericolo. Il Rapporto sulla libertà religiosa nel mondo 2025 di Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre evidenzia come in 62 Paesi si siano verificate violazioni sistematiche della libertà religiosa: 24 Paesi rientrano nella categoria più grave, ovvero quella di “persecuzione”, e 38 in quella di “discriminazione”. Complessivamente, oltre 5,4 miliardi di persone vivono in contesti in cui la libertà di religione è seriamente compromessa. 413 milioni di cristiani vivono in Paesi in cui la libertà religiosa è gravemente violata; di questi, circa 220 milioni risiedono in nazioni in cui sono direttamente esposti a persecuzioni. Regimi autoritari, violenza jihadista, nazionalismi religiosi e criminalità organizzata rappresentano oggi le principali minacce. Voci dimenticate: due serate tra musica e testimonianza a Milano e Roma Tra gli appuntamenti centrali della Red Week 2026 si sono svolte due serate di Voci dimenticate, il 16 novembre a Milano nella Basilica di Santa Maria delle Grazie, e il 21 novembre a Roma nella Basilica di San Saba. Chi lo desidera potrà contribuire, con una donazione libera, ai progetti di Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre a beneficio dei cristiani perseguitati. A Milano il pubblico ha assistito al concerto del Coro Filarmonico G.B. Pergolesi e dell’Orchestra Filarmonica Amadeus, diretti dal Maestro Gianmario Cavallaro; in programma brani del repertorio barocco, con musiche di Vivaldi, Torelli e Händel. Nella capitale il Coro Città di Roma, diretto dal Maestro Mauro Marchetti, ha proposto invece un percorso musicale con musiche di Mozart, Bach e Pergolesi. Ospite di entrambi gli appuntamenti è stata una donna che ha vissuto personalmente il dramma della persecuzione. La giovane sarà accompagnata da Don Joseph Fidelis Bature, sacerdote della diocesi nigeriana di Maiduguri e direttore del Trauma Center. La struttura, sostenuta dai benefattori di ACS, offre assistenza psicologica, spirituale e sociale alle vittime del gruppo terroristico islamista Boko Haram, accompagnandole in un percorso di guarigione e reinserimento nella comunità. Le loro toccanti testimonianze hanno raccontato la violenza che continua a colpire migliaia di persone e le occasioni di rinascita rese possibili dalla solidarietà di numerosi benefattori, italiani e internazionali. Le donazioni raccolte durante i due eventi di Milano e Roma sosterranno in particolare un progetto finanziato da ACS nella diocesi nigeriana di Minna, nel cui territorio le comunità cristiane vivono sotto la minaccia di attacchi armati, sequestri e violenze. L’iniziativa aiuterà 200 donne, uomini e bambini sopravvissuti alla violenza a ricostruire la propria vita attraverso il sostegno psicologico, il rafforzamento dei legami con la comunità e, per gli adulti, il recupero dell’autonomia economica. Il progetto prevede inoltre la formazione di circa 60 figure di riferimento delle comunità locali, tra cui sacerdoti e autorità, affinché sappiano riconoscere i bisogni delle persone più vulnerabili e offrire loro un sostegno adeguato. summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——对于正在成长的安迪·吉布森（Andy Gibson）来说，面对生活中种种挑战，度过每一天都特别艰难。当他的父母分居，他的姐姐又在车祸中丧生时，情况尤其如此。他甚至祈祷并问上帝为什么会发生这些事情，但没有得到回应……这篇文章《父母离异和妹妹去世使他远离上帝，阿尔法课程带来了改变》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 父母的分居和姐姐的去世使他远离了上帝，而“认识基督教”课程为他带来了改变
content: By Charles Gardner — Andy Gibson (photo: Gardner) Getting through life with all its many challenges was particularly tough for Andy Gibson as he was growing up. This was especially the case when his parents separated, and his sister was killed in a car crash. He even prayed and asked God why these things were happening, but heard no answers – until much more recently, when a growing relationship with Jesus transformed his life. Now 33, the Doncaster-based railway operations planner has his journey firmly back on track. Having attended a Church of England primary school and subsequently made only occasional visits to church, following Jesus is now the focus of his days. Looking back, he recalls: “I was lost and, moving into my teens, was full of anger, ego and arrogance. I got heavily involved with underage drinking around town and yet, strangely, I’d always pray before going out. “Time moved on and I found myself coasting through life in my twenties – meeting Beth, now my wife, working, saving for a house and having our first child Arlo. “Then in 2019, as the Covid pandemic approached, I was listening to odd things relating to Christianity on YouTube, as a result of which I went to a local church and completed an Alpha course (an introduction to the Christian faith). “In all honesty, it didn’t really interest me. But I gave it a bit of time, feeling that I still wanted to know about Jesus, God and the Bible as a whole. So I went on Google and found BEC (Bessacarr Evangelical Church) which was not far from where we lived. “I remember saying to Beth, ‘I’m going to go there!’ So I went one Sunday evening and was just blown away. The preaching was different to anything I had experienced, and I was finally understanding the Bible. “I couldn’t wait for the following Sunday to find out more. It was like waiting for another episode of a Netflix documentary to come out because we’d be following a specific section of the Bible, studying each chapter in depth as part of a series over several weeks. So I’d be looking forward to an explanation of the next verses the following week. And in due course I publicly declared my faith in Jesus by getting baptised. “Until I started going to church, learning more about the Bible and developing a relationship with Jesus, I never felt fulfilment and love. I never felt I fitted in anywhere until I found Jesus. “I didn’t have answers in my youth. But now I realise it’s not something you can work out all on your own. I can just turn to God’s Word and, through prayer, have a relationship with Jesus. “I can honestly say it’s completely changed every aspect of my life, and I am so grateful that I can’t even put it into words.” Andy and Beth now have a second child, named Red, and are members at BEC, a growing church in a Doncaster suburb. If you want to know more about a personal relationship with God, go here The post Parents’ separation and sisters death turned him from God, Alpha course brought change first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
由查尔斯·加德纳(英语:Charles Gardner)——安迪·吉布森(英语:Andy Gibson)(摄影:Gardner)执导. 在安迪·吉布森长大的时候 面对众多挑战 生活特别艰难 父母分居,妹妹在车祸中丧生时尤其如此.

他甚至祈祷并问上帝为什么发生这些事情,但是没有听到答案——直到最近,与耶稣的日益密切的关系改变了他的生活. 现在33号 以唐卡斯特为基地的铁路运营规划师 他的旅程已牢牢地回到轨道上

曾就读于一所英格兰教会小学,后来只偶尔访问教堂,跟随耶稣成为他时代的焦点. 回顾过去,他回顾道:“我迷失了,进入十几岁时,充满了愤怒、自我和傲慢。 但奇怪的是,我总是在外出前祈祷。

“时光在流逝,我发现自己在20多岁时踏上了生命的旅程,结识了现在的妻子贝丝(Beth),在工作、为房子储蓄和生下第一个孩子阿罗。 “随后,在2019年,随着科维德大流行的临近,我在YouTube上听到一些与基督教有关的怪事,结果我去了当地的教堂,完成了阿尔法课程(基督教信仰介绍).

“老实说, 但我给了它一点时间,感觉我仍然想知道耶稣,上帝和整个圣经. 于是我继续谷歌,找到了BEC(Bessacarr福音教会),它离我们住的地方不远. " 我记得对贝丝说:‘我要去那里! 所以我去了一个星期天晚上 被吹走。

传教与我经历过的一切不同,我终于明白圣经. 我迫不及待地等待下一个星期日再了解更多情况。 这就像等待Netflix纪录片的另一集出来, 因为我们将遵循圣经的特定部分,

因此,我期待着下周对下一首诗进行解释。 在适当的时候,我通过接受洗礼公开宣布我对耶稣的信仰. “直到我开始去教堂,更多地了解圣经,发展与耶稣的关系,我从未感到满足和爱。 在找到耶稣之前,我从未感觉到自己身处任何地方 我年轻时没有答案。

但现在我意识到这不是你能自己解决的事情。 我可以转而引用上帝的话,并通过祈祷与耶稣建立关系。 “我可以坦率地说,这完全改变了我生活的方方面面,我非常感激,我甚至不能用言语表达。 安迪和贝丝现在有一个第二个孩子,名叫瑞德(Red),是BEC的成员,BEC是顿卡斯特郊区正在成长的教堂.

Nixon is perhaps best known for his academic work at Veritas International University, his books, and his journalism for God Reports, ASSIST News Service, and other media […]  The post  From Post-Punk to German Techno—A Musical Journey  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh:
由马克·埃利斯(Mark Ellis)出名于他的奖学金,新闻,和声,布莱恩·C·尼克松(Brian C.

尼克松在维里塔斯国际大学的学术工作,他的著作,以及他为"上帝报道","ASSIST新闻服务"(ASSIST News Service),以及其他媒体[.]而出名的也许是他. 从后朋克到德意志科技-音乐之旅的文章首次出现在"上帝报告"上.
title_zh: 从后朋克到德国 техно——一段音乐之旅
content: By Mark Ellis — Known for his scholarship, journalism, and voice, Brian C. Nixon has another creative life—one that spans more than three decades of songwriting, recording, and musical exploration. Brian Nixon Nixon is perhaps best known for his academic work at Veritas International University , his books, and his journalism for God Reports , ASSIST News Service , and other media outlets. His voice has also reached listeners across the country through his former involvement with the radio program To Every Man an Answer (later known as Pastors’ Perspective ) and, more recently, Paratus , a program devoted to developing a biblical worldview. What may surprise those familiar with Nixon’s academic and journalistic work is that he is also an accomplished musician and songwriter whose musical journey spans more than 30 years. In his forthcoming book, A Beautiful Defense: How Aesthetics Points to God , co-written with Dr. Patrick Zukeran and scheduled for release in 2027 , Nixon explores the relationship between beauty, faith, and the creative process. In anticipation of the book’s release, I spoke with Nixon about his musical beginnings, his creative influences, and his unexpected venture into German electronic music. Tell me about your early musical journey. I grew up in a musical family. Music was part of my everyday life. During high school, I formed a band with some friends that eventually signed with an independent record label in the San Francisco Bay Area. We released only one record, but several of the other members went on to successful careers in the music industry. One became involved in founding Stones Throw Records, an influential independent label known for its underground hip-hop and experimental music. It was an exciting time. We were young, creative, and discovering what music could be. What did you do after the band broke up? I continued my college education, eventually transferring to California State University, Stanislaus. There, I met another group of musicians, and we formed a band called Canterbury. We ended up winning a Bay Area battle-of-the-bands competition, which was exciting. But rather than continuing in that direction, we decided to pursue something with a more intentional ministry focus. That led to the formation of Widow’s Mite . Widow’s Mite eventually signed with Rick Wakeman, the legendary keyboardist of Yes. Interestingly, that connection also introduced me to journalist Dan Wooding, who wrote Wakeman’s first biography. That relationship eventually opened the door for me to write for ASSIST News Service . So, in a rather unexpected way, my musical career helped launch my journalism career. Widow’s Mite After college, did you continue writing music? Absolutely. I still write music today. My compositions range from jazz and pop to what I call tone poems —short instrumental works that emphasize mood, atmosphere, and musical expression. Some are experimental, while others are much more accessible. I’ve always enjoyed exploring different musical forms rather than staying within a single genre. Interestingly, some of my recent compositions have been selected for rotation by a German online radio station. And here’s the surprising part: they’re German electronic and techno-influenced songs. I’ve been experimenting with AI-assisted production, including using a synthesized female vocalist to interpret my compositions. Did you say German techno? (Laughs.) I know. It sounds funny, doesn’t it? But there’s a story behind it. Recently, I took a deep dive into the music of Kraftwerk, the pioneering German electronic band. I was familiar with their work during high school in the early 1980s because they had influenced so many of the post-punk bands I was listening to at the time. I decided to revisit their entire catalog, and I was blown away all over again. They were years ahead of their time. Their approach to rhythm, synthesizers, repetition, and technology helped shape entire genres of contemporary music.
content_zh:
由马克·埃利斯(Mark Ellis)——以他的奖学金,新闻学,和声著称,布莱恩·C·尼克松(Brian C. Brian Nixon Nixon或许以他在Veritas国际大学的学术工作、他的书籍、他为《上帝报告》所做的新闻工作、ASSIST新闻服务以及其他媒体而闻名。

他的声音也通过他以前参与的电台节目“每个男人一个答案”(后来被称为“牧师的观点”)以及最近参与的Paratus,

可能令那些熟悉尼克松的学术和新闻工作的人惊讶的是,他还是一位成就卓著的音乐家和作曲家,他的音乐旅程长达30多年. 在他的即将出版的书《美丽的防御:美学如何指向上帝》中,

Patrick Zukeran)并计划于2027年发行,尼克松探讨了美,信仰,以及创作过程之间的关系. 为了期待这本书的发行,我和尼克松谈到了他的音乐开始,他的创作影响,以及他对德国电子音乐的意外冒险. 跟我说说你早期的音乐旅程 我成长在一个音乐家庭。

音乐是我日常生活的一部分。 在高中期间,我与一些朋友组成了一个乐队,最终在旧金山湾区与一个独立的唱片标签签约. 我们只发行了一张唱片,但其他几位成员继续进入音乐行业的成功职业生涯.

1开始参与创办Stones Throw Records,这个有影响力的独立标签以其地下嘻哈和实验音乐而闻名. 这是一个令人兴奋的时代。 我们年轻 富有创造力 并发现了什么是音乐。 乐队解散后你做了什么? 我继续我的大学教育, 最终转到加州州立大学斯坦尼斯劳斯。

在那里,我遇到了另一组音乐家,我们组成了一个乐队,叫坎特伯雷. 我们最终赢得了湾区战役的冠军 令人兴奋 但是,我们不是继续朝这个方向前进,而是决定以更有意的部级重点来追求某些目标。 这导致了寡妇之谜的形成。

寡妇的Mite最终与传说中的Yes键盘手Rick Wakeman签约. 有趣的是,这种联系也让我认识了记者丹·伍德(Dan Wooding),他写了Wakeman的第一份传记。 这段关系最终为我打开了为ASSIST新闻服务撰稿的大门. 因此,以相当出乎意料的方式,我的音乐生涯帮助启动了我的新闻事业.

你继续写音乐吗? 当然 我今天还写音乐 我的构思从爵士乐和流行到我所谓的调子诗——强调情绪、气氛和音乐表现的短器作品。 有些是实验性的,而另一些则更容易获得。

我总是喜欢探索不同的音乐形式, 有趣的是,我最近的一些构件已经被一个德国在线电台选为轮换. 这是令人惊讶的部分:它们是德国的电子和科技影响歌曲。

包括使用合成女性配音师来解释我的配音。 你说德国科技吗? (笑声) 我知道,我记得 这听起来很有趣, 但背后有一个故事。 最近,我深入了德国电子乐队Kraftwerk的音乐。

1980年代初高中期间我熟悉他们的工作,因为他们影响了我当时听的很多后朋克乐队. 我决定重新审视他们的全部目录,我再次被吹走. 他们比以前早好几年 他们对节奏,合成器,重复,技术的方法帮助塑造了整个当代音乐流派.

summary_zh: 作者：查尔斯·加德纳 (Charles Gardner) — 我的妻子琳达 (Linda) 并不了解 20 世纪 70 年代和 80 年代她的雇主的犹太背景。她只知道自己喜欢为他们工作，只是为了听从上帝的呼召，与孩子们一起工作。因此，我们前往伦敦参加鲑鱼展览，并且 [...] 发现犹太根源，回应反犹太主义的帖子首次出现在《上帝报告》上。
title_zh: 探索犹太血统，应对反犹太主义
content: By Charles Gardner — Charles and Linda on their wedding day My wife Linda had no idea of the Jewish background of her employers during the 1970s and 80s. She just knew that she loved working for them and only left to follow God’s call to work with children. So we travelled down to London for an exhibition of the Salmon and Gluckstein dynasty, and the story of how these resilient Jewish families fled violent persecution in Eastern Europe to build what became the largest catering company in the world known as J Lyons & Co. Linda worked there as a home economist from 1977-1984 but it was only much later that she learnt of the Jewish nature of the firm that once literally fed Britain with its teashops and corner houses on every high street, and its products in every home, Linda playing her part through her cooking and marketing skills. A few years later, after graduating from Bible College in Bournemouth, she worked at a prayer and reconciliation centre in Northern Ireland where she was introduced to the importance of the Christian faith’s Jewish roots, as a result of which she took a study tour of Israel to learn more. And on a second trip to the Holy Land ten years later, she got more than she bargained for. At Cana in Galilee, where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding, Linda was given a vision of her own wedding. And we met on a blind date six months later! Though having Jewish ancestry myself, I grew up knowing nothing about it. But I learnt more later, especially after becoming a Christian in my early twenties, as Linda had done. It helped that I had a Jewish believer as my early mentor, and I became increasingly aware of the significance of our Jewish heritage, about which I now write prolifically. Meanwhile Linda, who has been teaching Christianity in Doncaster area schools for over 30 years, also now teaches about Judaism as it forms the context into which Christ came to us, fulfilling all the laws and promises of the Old Testament. So in both our cases, we were kept in the dark about very important aspects of our lives – until the Lord shone his light on the truth. Which brings me to the Christian Church as a whole, especially in the UK. We have known very little, if anything, of our faith’s Jewish roots or of God’s ongoing purposes for Israel. This needs to change – and fast! For we are surely hurtling towards the Messiah’s Second Coming like a high-speed train, in danger of coming off the rails with the rest of humanity if we fail to get to grips with how we Christians fit into the unfolding picture of global opposition to tiny Israel. What is our role as we watch antisemitism spread across the globe like wildfire? Do we just sit and watch, or write it off as having nothing to do with us, and remain silent? Or do we stand up to be counted as those who refuse to salute the new Nazism that portrays itself as anti-Zionism – a Confessing Church walking the way of the cross for God’s chosen people? My questions come as renewed calls are made for an independent inquiry into antisemitism at the BBC following news that Oscar-winning producer Lucie Kon has won £400,000 in compensation from the broadcaster. Lucie’s career is said to have unravelled after she raised concerns about antisemitism within the BBC, though the latter have not admitted to any fault. This is highly significant as millions of UK Christians are (where Israel is concerned) probably more influenced by what they hear from our national broadcaster than what they read in the Bible. The Apostle Paul writes that the gospel should be proclaimed “to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile”. (Romans 1:16) Yes, we must share t
content_zh:
由查尔斯·加德纳(Charles Gardner)——查尔斯和琳达在他们的婚礼当天 我的妻子琳达对1970年代和80年代雇主的犹太背景一无所知. 她只知道她喜欢为他们工作,只好听从上帝的号召,与孩子们一起工作。

于是我们来到伦敦,为沙门王朝和格勒克斯泰因王朝举办展览, 讲述了这些坚韧的犹太家庭是如何逃离东欧的暴力迫害, 来建造一个被称为J Lyons & Co的世界最大的餐饮公司的故事。

琳达从1977年到1984年作为家庭经济学家在那里工作,但直到很晚,她才得知这家公司的犹太性质,曾经真正地向英国提供每条高街上的茶店和角楼,以及每家每户家中的产品,琳达通过她的烹饪和营销技巧扮演了她的角色.

几年后,她从伯恩茅斯的圣经学院毕业后,在北爱尔兰的一个祈祷与和解中心工作,在那里向她介绍了基督教信仰犹太教根源的重要性,因此她前往以色列学习更多知识. 在十年后的第二次圣地之行中,她得到了比她讨价还价的更多.

在加利利的卡纳,耶稣在婚礼上把水变成了葡萄酒,琳达得到了自己婚礼的愿景. 我们六个月后相识了! 虽然自己有犹太血统,但长大后却一无所知. 但我后来学到更多, 特别是在我20多岁时成为基督徒之后, 就像琳达所做的那样。

这有助于我有一个犹太教信徒作为我的早期导师,我越来越意识到我们的犹太遗产的重要性,我现在以正文写道。

与此同时,琳达在顿卡斯特地区学校教授基督教30多年,现在还教授犹太教,因为它构成了基督来到我们面前的背景,履行了《旧约》的所有法律和承诺。 因此,在我们这两种情况中,我们被蒙在鼓里,谈论着我们生活中非常重要的方面,直到上帝照亮真理。

这让我来到整个基督教会 特别是在英国 我们几乎不知道我们的信仰的犹太根源,或上帝对以色列的持续目的。 这需要改变,

因为如果我们不能把握基督徒如何融入全球反对小以色列的景象, 我们肯定会像高速列车一样, 与人类其他部分一同下火车。 当我们看到像野火一样在全球蔓延的反分裂主义时,我们的作用是什么?

我们只是坐视不理,还是把它写成与我们无关,保持沉默? 或者我们被算作拒绝向将自己描绘成反犹太复国主义的新纳粹主义致敬的人,

我的问题是,在奥斯卡获奖制片人Lucie Kon从广播公司获得40万英镑的赔偿后,英国广播公司再次呼吁独立调查反犹太主义。 Lucie的职业生涯据说在BBC内提出反分裂主义的担忧后破裂,

由于数百万英国基督徒(就以色列而言)受到我们国家广播机构广播的影响,

而今天的查尔斯和琳达(Charles and Linda),上帝的言语告诉我们“安抚”他的古老人民(以赛亚40:1), 有关以色列正在发生的事情的报道经常被传到造成整个国家遭受创伤的恐怖分子身上,

使徒保罗写道,福音应当被宣布为“首先对犹太人,然后对异教徒”。 (罗姆人1:16) 是的,我们必须分享T

title: New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran
summary: By Howard Cooper — Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democrat who became the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, says he plans to take his oath of office on a Quran when the new Congress convenes in January. El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers on November 3, becoming the first Muslim American elected to the […]  The post  New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh: 霍华德·库珀 (Howard Cooper) 撰文：密歇根州民主党人阿卜杜勒·赛义德 (Abdul El-Sayed) 成为第一位当选美国参议院的穆斯林，他表示，他计划在一月份新一届国会召开时，在《古兰经》的基础上宣誓就职。 42 岁的埃尔-赛义德于 11 月 3 日击败了共和党人迈克·罗杰斯，成为第一位当选为 […] 的穆斯林美国人。来自密歇根州的新参议员表示，他将在《古兰经》中宣誓。
title_zh: 密歇根州新任参议员表示他将以古兰经宣誓就职
content: By Howard Cooper — Abdul Al-Sayed (wikipedia commons) Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democrat who became the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, says he plans to take his oath of office on a Quran when the new Congress convenes in January. El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers on November 3, becoming the first Muslim American elected to the Senate and the first epidemiologist to serve in the chamber, according to WION News. In an interview with NPR’s Leila Fadel, he said, “I will likely swear on a Quran. Which Quran, we’re not sure.” He pointed to a copy once owned by Thomas Jefferson, which Keith Ellison used when he was sworn in to Congress, and to an old Quran at the University of Michigan that he described as the first in the state. The US Constitution does not require a Bible or any religious text. In practice, senators usually take the formal oath together on the Senate floor, and a Bible comes into play in individual ceremonial swearings-in. El-Sayed hasn’t said whether he’ll use the Quran in the formal proceedings, the ceremony, or both, and that his choice would not alter the wording of the oath. He has also stressed that his oath will be to the U.S. Constitution,  according to IBTimes. He will be sworn in by Vice President JD Vance, a fact El-Sayed has noted with humor. The Blaze reported he called it a “delicious irony” that Vance is constitutionally required to do so. Not everyone is comfortable with the news. The Daily Signal reported that former White House press secretary Sean Spicer said this week that given El-Sayed’s connections and statements, he should undergo a formal background check before receiving classified information. Presumably, Spicer was referring to Al-Sayed’s family connections to the Muslim Brotherhood. For many Christians, the moment raises questions about the role of faith in public life, the long American tradition of religious liberty, and the Judeo-Christian roots of the United States. El-Sayed and his colleagues are scheduled to be sworn in at noon on January 3, 2027. The post New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
由霍华德·库珀(英语:Howard Cooper)——阿卜杜勒·赛义德(英语:Abdul Al-Sayed (wikipedia communes)),密歇根州民主党人阿卜杜勒·艾尔·赛义德(英语:Abdul El-Sayed)成为美国参议院首位当选的穆斯林议员,他说他计划在1月份新国会召开时,在《古兰经》上宣誓就职.

42岁的赛义德在11月3日击败共和党人迈克·罗杰斯,成为首位当选参议院议员的美国穆斯林,也是首位在议院任职的流行病学家,据WION News报道. 在NPR的Leila Fadel的采访中,他说:“我很可能在《古兰经》上发誓。

这本《古兰经》, 他指曾由托马斯·杰斐逊拥有的一本副本,基思·埃里森在向国会宣誓就职时曾使用过这份副本,指密歇根大学的一本旧《古兰经》,他称之为该州的第一本。 美国宪法并不要求圣经或任何宗教文本.

在实践中,参议员通常在参议院的地板上共同进行正式宣誓,在个别的仪式宣誓中,圣经开始发挥作用. El-Sayed并未表示他是否会在正式诉讼、典礼或两者中使用《古兰经》, 他还强调,根据IBTimes的说法,他将向美国宪法宣誓。

副总统万斯将宣誓就职, 纵火报称万斯是宪法要求的, 不是每个人都对新闻很满意

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位勇敢的也门记者讲述了他在访问以色列后，对以色列的看法发生了翻天覆地的变化，这一说法令联合国感到震惊。他得出的结论是，他被教导要相信的关于犹太人的所有事情都是谎言。鲁艾·艾哈迈德应邀 […]  这篇文章《也门记者访问以色列，观点发生巨大转变》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 也门记者访问以色列，观点发生戏剧性变化
content: By Charles Gardner — Luai Ahmed speaking at UN (screenshot YouTube) A brave Yemeni journalist has stunned the United Nations with an account of how his view of Israel has dramatically changed following a visit there. And he was led to the conclusion that everything he has been taught to believe about the Jews is a lie. Luai Ahmed was invited to address the assembly by UN Watch, a non-governmental organisation monitoring the international body’s performance, as the UN Human Rights Council gathered to debate racism. He said: “I grew up in Yemen, where the word that we used for black people is ‘abeed’, which quite literally means ‘slaves’. Racism towards black people in my country is horrifying, but it’s not even the most toxic hatred that I was taught. “The first time I ever heard the word ‘Jew’ was in my local mosque when I was nine years old. At the end of Friday prayers, the Imam said: ‘May Allah kill the Jews and the Zionists’. And I responded alongside thousands of Muslims praying beside me: ‘Ameen’.” Luai then continued: “I was taught that Zionism meant killing Arabs, stealing our land, and destroying Islam. Then October 7th came. Hamas terrorists ‘freed Palestine’ by slaughtering 1,200 Israelis and kidnapping more than 200 people, including a one-year-old child. “Almost everyone in my Arab-Muslim circle celebrated. I didn’t. Instead, as a journalist, I decided to visit the so-called Zionist entity, and I was completely shocked to the core by the lack of apartheid and racism that I experienced. “One day, I got an eye infection. At the hospital, the nurses in reception were Jewish. The doctor treating me was Arab. Is there racism in Israel? Of course. There’s racism everywhere. “But Arabs in Israel aren’t called ‘slaves’. They are doctors, engineers, and party leaders. My experience helped me realise that Zionism really just means the Jewish people’s right to a tiny country. Everything I was taught was a lie.” Quite apart from tipping over the tables of woke left-wing ideology spreading its poisonous antisemitic tentacles across the globe, Luai’s testimony also knocks holes into the escalating pressure on the UK to make reparations for the slave trade, which saw plenty of collaborators in the host countries of those who suffered. And of course, the truth that dare not speak its name – that it was Christians like William Wilberforce who put an end to it! Luai is a great inspiration to fellow journalists like me who long for more of our colleagues to stand up and be counted. Thanks also to David Soakell of Christian Friends of Israel’s Watching Over Zion newsletter, November 5, 2026. The post Yemeni journalist visits Israel, dramatically changes views first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
一位勇敢的也门记者在联合国(YouTube)讲话时, 而他由此得出了这样的结论:他所学的关于犹太人的一切信仰都是谎言.

Luai Ahmed被联合国观察组织邀请在大会上讲话,该组织是监测国际机构业绩的非政府组织,在联合国人权理事会聚集一堂讨论种族主义问题。 他说:“我成长于也门, 我们用来形容黑人的字眼是“有病”的,

对我国黑人的种族主义令人恐惧, “当我九岁时,我第一次听到`犹太人'这个词是在我的地方清真寺。 星期五祷告结束时,教母说:愿真主杀害犹太教徒和犹太复国主义者。

我与数千名穆斯林一同祈祷: 卢艾接着说:“我被告知犹太复国主义意味着杀害阿拉伯人、偷窃我们的土地并摧毁伊斯兰教。 后于十月七日来. 哈马斯恐怖分子屠杀了1 200名以色列人并绑架了200多人,包括一名一岁儿童,从而“解放了巴勒斯坦”。 “我的阿拉伯-穆斯林圈子里几乎每个人都庆祝。

我没有。 相反,作为一名记者,我决定访问所谓的犹太复国主义实体,我对缺乏种族隔离和种族主义感到完全震惊。 “有一天,我眼睛受到感染。 在医院接待的护士是犹太人. 治疗我的医生是阿拉伯人。 以色列是否存在种族主义? 当然 到处都有种族主义。

“但以色列的阿拉伯人并不被称为奴隶。 他们是医生、工程师和党领袖。 我的经验帮助我意识到犹太复国主义只是意味着犹太人民对一个小国的权利。

我所学的一切都是谎言。” 卢艾的证言不仅在醒目的左翼意识形态席上倾出,在全球散布出有毒的反酋长触角,还打入了英国为奴隶贸易提供赔偿的不断升级的压力的洞口,在那些受苦受难者所在的东道国中,有许多合作者。

当然,那个不敢说出自己名字的真理——是威廉·威尔伯福斯这样的基督徒终结了它! 吕艾对像我这样的记者同事来说是一个巨大的灵感,他们渴望有更多的同事站起起来被统计. 也感谢以色列基督教之友的David Soakell,

title_zh: 蝠鲼带领海洋科学家找到失去的鳍
content: By Mark Ellis — Amber Sparks (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, especially with the Rigs-to-Reefs program, when oil drilling platforms are decommissioned. “We work with the oil companies to repurpose certain parts of the platform, retrofit it so that it can remain in place and continue to function as an artificial reef,” she told God Reports. Amber’s work has taken her around the world, with many dive experiences and encounters in the ocean with marine life. But there is one story she will never forget. It happened in the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Amber graduated from Scripps Institute and was invited on a research industry cruise with oil company representatives, scientists, and regulators on a liveaboard vessel. At the Flower Garden National Banks, a marine protected area 200 miles offshore, Amber was excited about her first dive, but slightly nervous. “You don’t know what you’re going to see or what this experience is going to be like,” she recalls. Dropping in (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook) Each diver had to jump off the vessel to get in the water. “We’re all geared up with our snorkel, our buoyancy control device, our wetsuit, and fins are the last thing you put on. So, I put on my fins and I jumped off the side of the boat.” “The second that I hit the water, one of my fins fell off, and I looked down and watched as it slowly descended to the bottom.” Amber glanced over at her dive buddy, and said, “I’m gonna go down. I’m going down.” Normally she would wait for her dive partner and they would go down together, but in this case, she thought, “I can’t (wait). I gotta go get my fin.” So Amber slowly began to descend to the bottom, about 60 feet below the ocean surface. “I felt completely lost. I was in a completely new area. I never dove before, and now I only had one fin.” She realized there were major currents that could have moved her fin in any direction. “I realized I can’t really swim with just one fin. So now not only am I at depth, but I’m handicapped with just one fin, and I started to feel pretty nervous.” It would probably take her 10 minutes to get back the surface, with safety stops. At the moment before panic set in, she looked upward and saw an amazing sight. It was a giant manta ray, with wings extending at least 10 feet. “Its wingspan was double mine. Its arms were out, and it was coming up over the side of a reef. “I’ve never seen a manta ray like this before. It totally took my breath away, it was so magnificent.” Another manta ray (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) She noted that manta rays are known in the ocean community to be “majestic, God-connected creatures with an understanding maybe beyond what humans can fully comprehend. They see the world and feel it in another way,” she notes. Mantas have the largest known brain of any fish. Their brains are large in absolute terms and relative to body size, which is also true of elephants, dolphins, and people. Their brains have enlarged areas associated with intelligence, vision, and motor coordination, and some of their brain cells are more like those in birds and mammals than in other fish.(1) As the manta ray drew close to Amber, she had an unusual communication experience. “I felt this sense where it said, ‘I want you to follow me. I’m going to help you find your fin.’ Amber Sparks Amber’s diving partner had just descended next to her, and they both began to swim after the manta. “I was barely making it, following this manta ray across the reef. At this point, I was so excited to see a manta ray. I kind of forgot about being handicapped, and I was just trying to go as fast as I can to keep up with it. Then Amber got the sur

summary: While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence […]  The post  Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success  first appeared on  God Reports .

title_zh: 拉尼尔第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利系列讲座：圆满成功
content: John Warwick Montgomery While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence with C. S. Lewis and his barrister gowns to the thousands of books that comprise his remarkable personal collection, Lanier has provided the Christian world with a marvelous tribute to one of the great Christian intellectuals of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Born in 1931, John Warwick Montgomery (d. 2024) was a distinguished Christian apologist, theologian, attorney, and scholar whose extraordinary career spanned several disciplines. Holding numerous academic degrees, including doctorates in theology, philosophy, and law, Montgomery became internationally recognized for his defense of Christianity through historical evidence, legal reasoning, and philosophical argumentation. His influential books, including History and Christianity , Faith Founded on Fact , and The Shape of the Past , helped establish a rigorous approach to Christian apologetics. Whether lecturing in universities, debating skeptics, or practicing law, Montgomery maintained that Christianity was not merely a matter of subjective belief but a faith grounded in historical reality and rational inquiry. Yet to stop at the library would be to understate Lanier’s remarkable work. The sixth annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series was a tour de force of distinguished thinkers, passionate Christians, and intellectually engaging presentations. More than a commemoration of Montgomery’s life, the gathering represented a continuation of his intellectual legacy: the conviction that Christianity can withstand serious scrutiny and offer compelling answers to life’s most profound questions. Mark Lanier, Nancy Pearcey, Paul Gould, Adam Francisco, and Michael Horton From the opening panel discussion hosted by attorney and philanthropist Mark Lanier to Dr. Paul Gould’s thoughtful presentation on worldviews, followed by attorney Craig Parton’s lecture on jurisprudential apologetics, one theme emerged with unmistakable clarity: Christianity is a reasonable faith. The presentations reflected Montgomery’s own interdisciplinary approach to apologetics: the Christian faith and intellectual inquiry need not be adversaries. Indeed, the Christian tradition has long insisted that faith and reason are complementary avenues in the pursuit of truth. The following day continued this rich intellectual exploration. Professor Nancy Pearcey addressed questions surrounding truth, dismantling various modern ideologies, while Dr. Adam Francisco offered an informative overview of Islamic history and belief, helping participants better understand one of world’s biggest religions. The keynote address by Dr. Michael Horton examined the challenge of reaching those who identify as “spiritual but not religious,” a growing segment of contemporary society. Horton’s presentation underscored the importance of communicating historic Christian truth in a culture increasingly suspicious of religious institutions yet often deeply interested in spiritual meaning. Dr. Michael Horton On Sunday morning, Lanier founder, Mark Lanier, hosted many participants during his Biblical literacy class, where he continued the dialogue with Michael Horton. Taken together, the lectures, discussions, and interviews demonstrated the breadth of Christian scholarship and the continuing relevance of thoughtful apologetics in an age of skepticism, religious pluralism, and cultural uncertainty. As I reflected on the weekend, I was reminded of the Festschrift Christianity for the Tough-Minded , a collection of scholarly essays honoring Montgomery’s life and ministry. Like that volume, the Lanier lecture series brought together diverse intellec

约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利 在德克萨斯州休斯敦拉尼尔图书馆和研究中心的约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利研究中心等待开会时,我找图书管理员沙龙·科夫兰和执行主任戴维·弗莱明博士说:“约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利将非常高兴拉尼尔代表他取得的成就。” 蒙哥马利与C.S.的书信

刘易斯和他的大律师礼服为他杰出的个人收藏的数千本书,为基督教世界向20世纪和21世纪伟大的基督教知识分子之一致敬。 1931年出生于约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利(d.

2024年)是一位杰出的基督教道歉学家,神学家,律师和学者,其非凡的事业跨越多个学科. 蒙哥马利拥有众多学术学位,包括神学,哲学和法学的博士学位,他通过历史证据,法律推理,哲学论证,为基督教辩护而获得国际承认.

他的有影响力的著作,包括历史和基督教、基于事实的信仰、以及过去的造型,帮助确立了对基督教学的严格态度。 无论是在大学里讲课,辩论怀疑论,还是执业法律,蒙哥马利都坚持认为基督教不仅仅是主观信仰的问题,而是建立在历史现实和理性调查基础上的信仰.

然而, 停留在图书馆将会低估拉尼尔的出色工作。 第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利讲座系列是由杰出的思想家,充满热情的基督徒,以及智力参与的演讲组成的巡回演出.

这场集会不仅仅是纪念蒙哥马利的一生,它代表着他思想遗产的延续:相信基督教能够经受住严肃的审视,为人生最深刻的问题提供令人信服的答案.

马克·拉尼尔 南希·皮尔西 保罗·古尔德 亚当·弗朗西斯科 迈克尔·霍顿 从律师和慈善家马克·拉尼尔主持的开场小组讨论到保罗·古尔德博士关于世界观的深思熟虑的演讲,然后是克雷格·帕顿律师关于法学理论的演讲,一个主题以明确无误的方式出现: 基督教是一种合理的信仰.

这些介绍反映了蒙哥马利自己对学说采取的跨学科方法:基督教信仰和知识调查不必是对手。 事实上,基督教传统长期以来一直坚持信仰和理性是追求真理的补充途径。 次日继续进行这种丰富的知识探索.

Nancy Pearcey教授谈到了围绕真理的问题,摧毁了各种现代意识形态,而Adam Francisco博士则提供了伊斯兰历史和信仰的翔实概览,帮助与会者更好地理解世界上最大的宗教之一。 由Dr.A.先生作主旨发言。

迈克尔·霍顿研究了帮助那些认为是“精神上但并非宗教上”的当代社会日益扩大的阶层的挑战。 霍顿的演讲强调了在一种对宗教机构越来越怀疑、但往往对精神意义很感兴趣的文化中传播基督教历史真理的重要性。 医生

迈克尔·霍顿 星期天早上,拉尼尔创始人马克·拉尼尔(Mark Lanier)在他的圣经识字课期间接待了许多参与者,在那里他继续与迈克尔·霍顿进行对话.

讲座、讨论和访谈共同显示了基督教奖学金的广度,以及深思熟虑的学说在怀疑主义、宗教多元化和文化不确定性的时代的持续相关性。

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——在第二次世界大战南太平洋的一场海战中，一名日本水兵所在的驱逐舰被美国人击沉，他的大多数战友都淹死了。令人惊奇的是，尽管鱼雷官新谷通晴与其他人一起被卷入波涛之下，随着战舰的沉没，但他却奇迹般地在这场1942年的灾难中幸存下来。（只有18名……）  这篇文章《二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”
content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
查尔斯·加德纳编著: 当一艘日本水手的驱逐舰在二战南太平洋战役中被美国人击沉时,大部分同伴溺毙. 令人惊奇的是,尽管随着船只的下沉,他与其他人一起被吸在海浪下,但鱼雷军官Michiharu Shinya却不知何故幸免于1942年的灾难。 (200人的船员中只有18人这样做).

但他宁愿死在那个时候,因为他的族人被灌输相信被俘虏是可耻的. 然而,他受了重伤,但被医护人员喂养。

在时间上,他被接了起来,最终被带到新西兰惠灵顿附近的费瑟斯顿(Featherston)的战俘营,在那里他将度过接下来的三年,正如唐·斯蒂芬斯在他的励志书"战争与格蕾丝"(福音出版社,10Publishing的印记)中记载的那样.

信也和同狱囚犯受到很大程度的善待(与盟军囚犯经常在日本人手中遭受的酷刑形成鲜明对比). 在圣诞节用礼物淋浴 一个他一无所知的宴会 看起来特别奇怪

然而,在一些囚犯要求精神帮助和提供日本圣经后,他决心不再接受基督教教义的 " 接纳 " 。 直到他看到一篇题为“为胜利而悲伤”的文章,作者在文章中引用了一位“赫布鲁先知”的话:“那些希望主复活的人。 他们将像鹰一样飞翔,

他们将奔驰,而不会疲倦,他们将走路,而不会晕倒。 这给他留下了深刻的印象,他下定决心要找出它来自何处. 假设它来自旧约,他开始阅读圣经,从创世纪第一章开始. 最终,在他的喜悦中,他发现深刻的文字来自先知以赛亚的经典(第40章第31节).

在搜索中略微浮出水面后,他发现自己患上了疟疾,一位朋友给他带了一本小册子,名为《原因》,解释救世之路。 难民营的牧师Hessell Troughton牧师曾是日本的传教士, 信也加入了其他人的圣经研究,来到了了解和热爱耶稣作为他的救世主.

这种“完全自由”现在统治了他的生活,监狱变成了他所称的“地球上独一无二的天堂”。 他从此之后再也没有回头看,并且确信他的战后召唤将会为他的主服务. 当他最终回家时,家人震惊地看到他活着,因为他被报道为阵亡.

他还给抓捕者取了一个假名,因为被假定是落入敌人手中的耻辱。 在东京和美国多年的神学研究之后,信也后来成为一名牧师和多产作家和翻译。 他逐渐相信,《旧约》表明了罪恶是“人类的最终问题”,并明确指出基督是答案。

在试图理解为什么如此少的日本人成为基督徒时,他感到部分是由于他们的自豪感,因为他们相信他们是优越的种族。

至于他在新西兰度过的三个圣诞节,作者Don Stephens写道:"在他收到的所有礼物中,他最珍视的一件是`上帝在耶稣基督中无限和深厚的恩惠与和平 ' 。 日本战俘在营地发现「自由」,

title_zh: 在西部明星的阴影下：格罗弗·刘易斯、拉里·麦克默特里和文字的胜利
content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. content_zh:
与《格罗弗·刘易斯读者:短草中的辉煌与西部之星》,拉里·麦克默特里的最新传记, 手持,我装载我的卡车并前往德克萨斯州阿彻城, 由我的妻子梅兰妮和我们的朋友埃利奥特陪同。 阿彻城当然是麦克默特里国家,一个通过美国最著名的小说家之一的文学想象而成名的德克萨斯小镇.

在之前访问Archer城后, 我对McMurtry的信仰(或缺乏信仰)有一番兴趣, 这一次,我转而关注有天赋的记者、评论家和诗人格罗弗·刘易斯,他在大学时代的生活与麦克默特里的生活交织在一起。

然而,刘易斯的故事并非从文学成就开始,而是从几乎难以想象的悲剧开始. 他从小就经历了父母的惨痛损失,当时他的父亲谋杀了他的母亲,随后被他即将死亡的妻子或在场的其他人用同一把枪射杀。 刘易斯才八岁 很难想象一个更可怕的开端。

然而,刘易斯最终没有让这场悲剧成为他的全部故事,而是通过文学找到了声音. 也许他命中注定的卡片 给他写了很多东西 或写作成为他理解世界的方式, 这个世界已经揭示了它的残酷性,还为时过早。

刘易斯在自传诗“Hillbilly Song”中写道 : “ 你曾经问过我,Ann/Over咖啡随着谈话而变得冷淡,在你妈妈的雨滴/住所里,他们是谁,他们在无气息的年代/在野外时如何。 ” 对刘易斯来说,那些早年的确很狂野. 但它们也是他的文学想象最终会成长的土壤.

1934年出生于德克萨斯州的"言语生活"(A Life in Words Born in Texas),格罗弗·刘易斯(Grover Lewis)成为美国新闻业中一个有特色的代言人,特别是通过他对1960年代和1970年代迅速变化的地貌的文化批评和报道.

他以尖锐的观察,文学的才华,以及能够捕捉美国文化的个性和矛盾而闻名,即使他偶尔在讲述中伸张真理. 他的作品出现在包括滚石公司在内的著名出版物中,他的报道帮助他树立了自己作为有见地,有时剪切流行文化观察者的声誉.

然而,刘易斯不只是一名记者。 他是一位诗人和文学家,一个懂得文字可以比传递信息更有用的人. 它们可以揭示人类的状况,暴露其矛盾,甚至可能提供某种治疗方法。

Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) 继续“Hillbilly Song,” 刘易斯思考道:“最后,无气息和干燥的嘴唇/在蓝色的暗处私欲下,我们都躺在一起——/我的母亲、父亲、他们的死亡/梦想,我这个未出生的囚犯儿子......” 这些台词有些困扰。 死者仍然在场。 过去拒绝消失。

而诗人,即使作为一个成年人,似乎也与塑造他进入世界的环境相搏. 然而,写作本身就暗示了另一种情况:拒绝保持沉默。 两德克萨斯州立大学,两条文学道路刘易斯州立大学和拉里·麦克默特里(英语:Larry McMurtry)在1950年代作为北德克萨斯州立学院,即现在的北德克萨斯大学的学生跨过道路.

两人都是年轻的德克萨斯人,被吸引到文学和写字的可能性. 他们的友谊是在共同的知识环境中发展起来的,这种环境鼓励阅读,对话,追求文学野心.

尽管他们的职业生涯最终走的是不同的道路——小说、剧本和文学名人、刘易斯新闻、诗歌和文化批评——但他们对美国生活的复杂性有着共同的兴趣。 麦克默特里和刘易斯在大学期间(ChatGPT)都拥有超越德克萨斯州和美国西部神话的能力,认识到孤独,凝视

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位犹太籍陆军外科医生对一名年轻士兵的勇气感到惊叹，这名士兵在美国内战（1861-65）的葛底斯堡战役中身受重伤。为了挽救这个男孩的生命，马克斯·罗斯瓦利（Max Rossvally）博士不得不截肢，截掉了他的一条腿和一条胳膊。但这改变了他自己……  这篇题为《犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归向耶稣》的文章  最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归信耶稣
content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online. The post Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
牧师彼得·科隆在他的故事电影"查尔斯·加德纳"(By Charles Gardner)中描绘了罗斯瓦利少校——一位犹太军队外科医生对美国内战期间格底斯堡战役(1861-65)中一名年轻士兵严重受伤的勇气感到惊讶. Max Rossvally医生被迫截肢, 但这改变了他自己的生活。

对于17岁的Drummer Boy — — 年龄太小,无法承担前线任务 — — 拒绝氯仿或白兰地来消磨疼痛。 查理·科尔森选择了信任耶稣,他的主和救世主.

这位医生是一名陆军少校和正统犹太人,对男孩的勇敢以及他大胆地宣布对基督的信仰,恳求军官(他知道是犹太人)相信耶稣是可以理解的,因为他也是犹太弥赛亚。 然而,马克思被动摇僵硬,陷入了巨大的困境,因为他一直被教导要憎恨耶稣.

他的宗族曾否认他是一个 " 骗子 " 和假的弥赛亚。 Charlie在几天后就去世了,显然更关心医生的永恒命运,而不是他自己痛苦地离开这一生。 10年后,马克思发现自己在纽约的理发师座椅上再次被敦促信任耶稣.

在解释了福音之后,理发师答应为他祈祷,并说每当他与一个犹太人接触时,他觉得有义务将他介绍给前来寻找“迷失的以色列羊”的人(Matthew 10:6)。

外科医生随后登上火车在华盛顿举行商务会议,报纸的广告将他引向 " 复活 " 服务,传教士重复了他从理发师和男孩士兵那里听到的信息,使他流泪。

他在家里苦苦地祈祷了一段时间,他首先想到,如果他接受基督,他将反对他所知道的所有建议和教导,更不用说整个犹太社区了。 但他最终确信耶稣确实是"旧约预言"的实现(特别是创世纪49:10,米迦5:2和以赛亚7:14).

他就祈祷说:易卜拉欣、易司哈格、叶尔孤白的主啊! 你知道我对这件事很真诚 如果耶稣基督是上帝之子,那么今晚把他告诉我,我将接受他为我的弥赛亚。” 一场漫长的战斗随之而来,但他的疑虑最终被欢乐和幸福所取代,因为他称赞上帝找到了真正的希洛,以色列统治者和埃马纽埃尔.

但他要付出高昂的代价,跟随基督的所有人一样。 他的妻子抛弃了他;他的父母抛弃了他。 但是,他从未放弃过希望,因为他不断祈祷和联系家人。 在54天后,他的妻子作为耶稣的门徒加入了他,在时间上,他的女儿也成为了信徒.

但他的儿子与他断绝关系多年,直到他最终与他的大地父和天父都和解. 在他来到基督的大约18个月之后的一段非凡续集中,马克思在战场上遇见了那些年前他死去的年轻病人的母亲科尔森夫人.

他怀着极大的喜悦,得以分享她儿子如何使他踏上基督辉煌未来的道路,这就是触摸世界各地的生活,包括我的家乡英格兰约克郡. 事实上,他来到利兹居住,向那里的犹太社区伸出援手,并被埋在城内的草坪林墓地.

我的一个爱尔兰朋友科林·内文参观了这个坟墓,其中包括医生颂歌"I am Coming Soon"的节录,并且能够把马克思的故事复制给看守人,因此在1892年去世后一个多世纪的福音派传承下来,享年64岁.

一部54分钟的电影 — — Rossvally: 从Synagogue到救世主 — 已经在DVD上制作,显然可以在网上订购. 在目睹病人的勇气首次出现在上帝的报告之后,

title: Two truck tires and a white dove taught me to trust God
summary: By Mike Shreve — Evangelism has been my focus for 55 years, ministering throughout the United States and in 14 other nations. God mercifully saved me during the Jesus Revolution (1970), out of a hippie lifestyle and a passionate, though misguided pursuit of truth through far eastern religious practices (yoga and meditation). Shortly after encountering […]  The post  Two truck tires and a white dove taught me to trust God  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh:
由迈克·史瑞夫(Mike Shreve)——福音主义一直是我55年来的焦点,在全美国和其他14个国家担任部长. 上帝在耶稣革命期间(1970年)从嬉皮的生活方式和热情中怜悯地拯救了我,尽管通过远东宗教实践(瑜伽和冥想)错误地追求真理.

碰面后不久... 两辆卡车轮胎和一只白鸽教我相信上帝,
title_zh: 两只卡车轮胎和一只白鸽教会了我信靠上帝
content: By Mike Shreve — Tent meeting in the 80s Evangelism has been my focus for 55 years, ministering throughout the United States and in 14 other nations. God mercifully saved me during the Jesus Revolution (1970), out of a hippie lifestyle and a passionate, though misguided pursuit of truth through far eastern religious practices (yoga and meditation). Shortly after encountering Jesus and being delivered, along with another brother in the Lord, I began hitchhiking around the country, preaching the Gospel on street corners and college campuses. That developed through the years into ministry in churches, auditoriums, conferences, and tent crusades. Supernatural provision and divine intervention has always carried me, through every phase of this five-and-a-half-decade-long adventure. However, the following story is a classic. For about 25 years I carried big Gospel tents around the country. At the time of this “miracle,” I was transporting a 60’ x 90’ tent from one city to the next in an old, dilapidated bus that kept introducing new challenges to our amateur mechanic skills (putting it mildly). One day, on our way to Tampa, Florida—unfortunately—we hit a large pothole in the road that put a serious dent in the rear left rim on which a large truck tire was mounted. From that point, the inner tube would not retain air, making it necessary to stop every thirty miles or so to fill it up again . . . and again . . . and again . . . making the trip painfully slow. Adding to the problem, the other rear tire was bald, and we had no spare (couldn’t afford one). So, a flat would have brought us to a complete standstill. Sometimes, I think back on those days (when our zeal for the Kingdom outran any wisdom we might have possessed), and I marvel at the many times God took care of us anyway (like the loving heavenly Father that He is). Thousands of pounds of equipment were packed into that groaning, creaking, rusty, decrepit bus — heavy canvas tent sections, metal poles, stakes, platform, and 300 chairs—and only a few days allowed in between cities for transit and setup. No, we really could not afford any setbacks. And yes, a lot of “faith prayers” were uttered during every trip (or were they “presumptive proclamations”—not sure—maybe a mix of the two). An old split rim tire mounted on an old bus Once we got to Tampa, attempting to be frugal, I visited the junkyards hoping to find a used replacement rim. As if they had conspired to dissuade me, every junkyard owner/manager shot down my hopes with a similar assessment, “Fella, you won’t find one of them old split-rims anywhere. They’re dangerous. When you try to mount a tire on one, they can snap open and injure somebody real bad, cutting off a hand, even killing a person. We melted ‘em all down as scrap metal.” (Go ahead, look them up online—they were even called “widow-makers.”) It was the same story everywhere I went. Nobody could help. Then three weeks passed and we had to pack the bus and head to our next location—Bessemer City, North Carolina. It was a college-level, biblically-sound course on developing long-suffering and patience: stopping every thirty miles or so to air up that unpredictable tire, pleading with God to somehow supernaturally assist us in our journey by making sure none of the tires blew. Somehow, we made it—around 600 miles—stopping about 25 times. Then an incredible miracle happened! God did it and I still feel awestruck, just writing about it. As we turned into the fairgrounds area, right in the middle of the entrance were two brand new, neatly-stacked truck tires (unclaimed), exactly the size we used on the bus—mounted (you guessed it!) on the very same split rims our bus required. Talk about worshiping God—we launched into a praise session right then and there! What were the odds? We all knew it had to be God. Jehovah-Jireh (the Lord our provider) had fulfilled His amazing promise to do “exceedingly, abundantly above all” we could ask or think (Ephesians 3:20). Then li
content_zh:
麦克史瑞夫 80年代的帐篷会议是我55年来的焦点,在美国和14个其他国家担任部长。 上帝在耶稣革命期间(1970年)从嬉皮的生活方式和热情中怜悯地拯救了我,尽管通过远东宗教实践(瑜伽和冥想)错误地追求真理.

在遇到耶稣和被送走后不久,我与上帝的另一个兄弟一起,开始搭便车到全国各地,在街角和大学校园传福音. 多年来,这在教堂、礼堂、会议和帐篷十字军中发展成部。

超自然的供给和神的干预 总是让我在五年半的历险历程中 然而,以下的故事是一个经典的故事. 大约25年来,我在全国各地搭载着大型福音帐篷。

在这个“奇迹”发生时,我正用一辆老旧、破旧的公交车将60×90的帐篷从一个城市运送到另一个城市,这辆公交车不断给我们的业余技工技能带来新的挑战(轻轻地推开)。 有一天,在前往佛罗里达州坦帕的路上——不幸地——我们撞上了路边的一个大坑洞,在后左侧竖起一个大型卡车轮胎,后侧有严重的凹痕。

从此,内管不会保留空气,使得每30英里左右必须停一次才能再次填充. . . 再加上问题, 另一台后轮胎是秃头, 因此,一个公寓会 使我们完全停顿。

有时,我想起那些时候(那时我们对王国的热情超越了我们可能拥有的任何智慧),我惊讶地看到,无论怎样,上帝总是照顾我们(就像他那慈爱的天父)。

数千磅的设备被装进那辆呻吟、颤抖、生锈、破烂的巴士——重型帆布帐篷路段、金属杆、木桩、平台和300张椅子——而且只有几天时间允许在城市之间过境和布置。 不,我们真的无法承受任何挫折。

在每次旅行中都发表了许多“信仰祷告”(或它们是否“假定的宣告”——不确定——可能是两者的混合)。 一辆旧公共汽车上挂着一个旧的分叉轮圈轮胎 一旦我们到了坦帕, 试图节俭, 我参观了垃圾场 希望找到一个旧的替代轮圈。

就像他们密谋劝阻我一样, 每个垃圾场老板/经理都用类似的评估来击落我的希望, “伙计, 他们很危险。 当你试图安装一个轮胎, 他们可以撕开和伤害一个人 真正的坏,切断一只手,甚至杀死一个人。

我们把它们都融化成废金属。” 他们甚至被称为“寡妇制造者”。 我去过的地方都一样 没人能帮上忙 然后三个星期过去了,我们不得不收拾公交车 并前往下一个地点——北卡罗莱纳州的贝瑟默市。

这是一个关于发展长期痛苦和耐心的大学级、圣经般的教程:每隔30英里左右就停下来吹吹那个不可预测的轮胎,恳求上帝以某种超自然的方式协助我们的旅程,确保没有轮胎爆炸。 不知何故,我们大约在600英里的距离里,停了25次。 奇迹发生了!

上帝做到了,我仍然感觉 西车,只是写它。 当我们变成广场时, 就在入口的中间, 两个全新的, 整洁的卡车轮胎(无人认领), 说到崇拜上帝——我们发起了一次赞美会议,

什么机会? 我们都知道那是真主。耶和华已满足了。 他令人惊奇地承诺“超越一切, 然后说
author: Mark Ellis

title: Aku Simon dari Kirene
summary_zh: 我是来自古利内的西门。 我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。
title_zh: 我是古利奈人西门。
content: Aku Simon dari Kirene. Namaku menunjukkan bahwa aku tinggal di benua Afrika. Meski demikian, kulitku tidak hitam dan bibirku pun tidak tebal. Dan meskipun sudah selama beberapa generasi keluargaku berdiam di Kirene, ibu kota Kireneika -- sebuah kota Yunani di Afrika Utara yang terkenal karena kemakmuran dan para ahli filsafatnya -- kulitku tidaklah putih. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku orang Yahudi asli sampai ke jantung hati. Sejak kecil, kutaati semua hukum agama tanpa kecuali, walaupun aku tidak lagi fasih berbahasa Aram akibat dibesarkan dalam masyarakat yang berbahasa Yunani. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku tidak ingin berkisah tentang diri sendiri. Juga tidak tentang semua pengalaman hidupku. Aku cuma ingin bercerita tentang pengalamanku yang satu itu. Pengalaman yang kemudian mengubah seluruh jalan hidupku. Dan seluruh jalan hidup Anda, sekiranya Anda juga mengalaminya. Hari itu adalah hari Jumat. Aku baru saja tiba di Yerusalem pagi itu. Tujuanku melakukan perjalanan yang jauh itu adalah untuk merayakan hari raya Paskah. Setiap tahun aku melakukannya. Tidak sedikit pun aku heran melihat orang-orang penuh sesak memadati kota. Walaupun letih, segera setelah menaruh barang-barangku di hotel dan membersihkan badan, aku keluar berjalan-jalan untuk menikmati keriuhan kota yang sedang larut dalam semarak pesta. Lengking jeritan anak-anak yang berlari ria kian kemari, teriakan membujuk bahkan kadang-kadang memaksa para pedagang yang menjajakan barang-barangnya, dan bau asap dupa atau suara syahdu orang-orang yang menyanyikan kidung-kidung pujaan -- semua itu membuat aku lupa akan keletihanku. Suasana yang agak liar ini memang berbeda benar dengan suasana Kirene yang sopan dan tertib. Namun, lebih hidup. Tiba-tiba ada kegaduhan yang tak biasa. Para serdadu Roma menyeruak massa. "Ah, lagi-lagi pawai laskar-laskar Romawi untuk mengingatkan siapa yang berkuasa di negeri ini," pikirku. Akan tetapi tidak. Di baris paling depan, ada seorang serdadu yang memegang panji bertulis: "Yesus, orang Nazaret, raja orang Yahudi." Aku memang belum pernah berjumpa dengan-Nya. Akan tetapi, nama "Yesus", siapa yang tidak mengenal-Nya? Dia adalah tokoh paling kontroversial. Yang tidak dapat kumengerti, mengapa serdadu Romawi mengarak panji seperti itu. Karena itu, aku mendekat untuk melihat lebih dekat. Di tengah pagar betis laskar-laskar Roma itu, tiga orang melangkah pelan memanggul salib. "Penjahat-penjahat besar," pikirku. Namun, apa hubungannya dengan panji itu? Kemudian aku semakin mengerti. Riuh rendah massa rakyat menyebut-nyebut nama Yesus sambil mencemooh-Nya. Tidak kurang pula yang meludahi-Nya. Akan tetapi, yang manakah Yesus di antara ketiga orang itu? Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku semakin mendekat. Lalu aku tahu dengan pasti yang mana Yesus. Dia paling kecil, hampir tidak berotot. Rambut panjang-Nya terurai, lekat di sana-sini oleh darah kering yang berasal dari duri-duri yang teranyam di kepala-Nya. Sekujur tubuh-Nya biru lebam. Langkah-Nya tertatih-tatih. Amat letih. Akan tetapi mata-Nya -- meski merah sebab kurang tidur -- namun tetap tajam menusuk setiap kali menatap. Anehnya, juga begitu lembut menyejukkan. Aku tak dapat lepas memandang mata-Nya itu. Penuh wibawa, tetapi juga begitu menenangkan dan kebapakan. Lalu Dia roboh. Tubuh-Nya yang kecil dan nyaris hancur itu tidak kuat lagi menahan bobot salib di pundak-Nya. Massa berteriak kesenangan bagai binatang liar yang haus darah. Cemeti melayang menyayat punggung-Nya. Darah menyembur. Dan Dia pun bangkit lagi pelan-pelan. Keletihan. Tetapi mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Lalu Dia berjalan beberapa langkah. Namun, roboh lagi. Arak-arakan berhenti. Massa semakin buas. Cemeti melayang berulang-ulang. Darah menyembur. Namun, Dia tak mampu bangun kembali. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Entah mengapa, aku tidak terkesan benar oleh semua itu. Kecuali oleh tatapan mata-Nya. Mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. content_zh:
我是来自古利内的西门。我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。尽管如此，我的皮肤并不黑，嘴唇也不厚。尽管我的家族已经在昔兰尼生活了几代人，昔兰尼是昔兰尼加的首府，这是一座位于北非的希腊城市，以其繁荣和哲学家而闻名，但我的肤色并不白。我是古利奈的西门。

我从心底里是一个地道的犹太人。从小到大，我毫无例外地遵守所有宗教律法，尽管由于在讲希腊语的社区长大，我已经不再精通阿拉姆语。我是古利奈人西门。我不想谈论我自己。也不想讲述我所有的生活经历。我只想讲述我那一次的经历。

这段经历后来改变了我的人生轨迹。如果您也经历过，那么也会改变您的人生轨迹。那天是星期五。那天早上我刚抵达耶路撒冷。我长途跋涉的目的就是为了庆祝逾越节。我每年都这样做。看到熙熙攘攘的人群挤满了这座城市，我一点也不感到惊讶。

尽管很累，但在酒店放下行李并洗漱完毕后，我还是出门散步，享受这座沉浸在节日气氛中的城市的喧嚣。

到处跑来跑去的孩子们尖叫声，叫卖的小贩们劝诱甚至有时强迫的吆喝声，还有熏香的味道或人们吟唱赞美诗的悠扬声音——这一切都让我忘记了疲惫。这种略显喧闹的氛围与古利奈文雅有序的氛围截然不同，但却更有活力。

突然间，出现了一阵不寻常的喧哗。罗马士兵挤过人群。“唉，又是罗马士兵的游行，用来提醒人们谁才是这个国家的统治者。”我想。但是不是。在最前面一排，有一名士兵拿着一面旗帜，上面写着：“拿撒勒人耶稣，犹太人的王。” 我确实从未见过祂。

但是，“耶稣”这个名字，谁不认识他呢？他是最具争议的人物。我不明白的是，为什么罗马士兵要举着这样的旗帜游行。因此，我走近仔细观察。在罗马士兵的方阵中间，有三个人背着十字架缓缓前行。“大坏蛋，”我想。不过，这和那面旗帜有什么关系？

然后我渐渐明白了。人群喧嚣着，一边喊着耶稣的名字，一边嘲笑祂。还有不少人向祂吐唾沫。但是，这三个人当中哪一个是耶稣呢？我是古利奈人西门。我走得越来越近。然后我确切地知道谁是耶稣。他是三人中个子最小的，几乎没有肌肉。

祂的长发散乱，这里那里都沾满了干涸的血迹，这些血迹来自祂头上戴着的荆棘冠。祂的全身都瘀青了。祂的步伐蹒跚。祂非常疲惫。但是祂的眼睛——尽管因为睡眠不足而发红——但每次注视时仍然锐利如刀。奇怪的是，他的眼神也如此温柔、令人舒心。我无法移开视线，不去看祂的眼睛。

充满威严，但也非常平和和慈父般。然后祂倒下了。祂瘦小而几乎破碎的身体再也承受不住肩上十字架的重量。人群像嗜血的野兽一样欢呼雀跃。鞭子抽打着祂的背。鲜血喷涌而出。祂又慢慢地站了起来。祂疲惫不堪。但是祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

然后他走了几步。然而，祂又倒下了。游行队伍停了下来。人群变得越来越凶狠。鞭子一次又一次地挥舞着。鲜血喷涌而出。然而，祂再也无法站起来了。我是古利奈人西门。不知为何，这一切并没有真正触动我。除了祂的眼神。祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

因此，当一名士兵突然拉我时，我好像失去了知觉。然后把十字架放在我身上。

title: Kasih Tuhan Tiada Taranya
summary_zh: p style="margin-bottom:1em; ">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。
title_zh: 上帝的爱是无与伦比的
content: p style="margin-bottom:1em;">Oleh: Romauli br Marpaung Shalom, Nama saya Romauli br Marpaung. Saat ini, saya berusia 23 tahun. Saya berasal dari keluarga Kristen. Saya anak pertama dari lima bersaudara. Keluarga saya, dahulunya, bukan keluarga yang harmonis. Orang tua saya sering bertengkar. Namun, saat kelas IV SD, bapak saya bertobat sungguh-sungguh dan menyerahkan dirinya untuk diperlengkapi di Sekolah Alkitab Purbasari Pematang Siantar. Setelah selesai sekolah, beliau akhirnya diangkat menjadi seorang Pendeta, dan saya mulai pelayanan sejak kelas V SD di Gereja Kemuliaan Sion sebagai pemain musik tunggal. Pada 2013, saat saya lulus SMA, saya berharap bisa kuliah di Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Medan. Namun, saat mengikuti SBMPTN, saya gagal karena tidak lulus seleksi. Akhirnya, bapak saya mengusulkan supaya saya kuliah di Solo karena dia punya rekan pendeta yang anaknya kuliah di Solo juga. Saya mengikuti keinginan bapak saya karena beliau rindu saya bisa menjadi seorang hamba Tuhan. Akhirnya, saya kuliah di STT Berita Hidup, Solo, dan mengikuti semua kegiatan, aturan yang ada di kampus tersebut. Saya dibaptis saat duduk di bangku SMA kelas XI. Awalnya, saya kuliah di Berita Hidup karena orang tua dan pelarian, tetapi pada akhirnya saya bertobat dan percaya sungguh-sungguh kepada Tuhan Yesus saat kuliah semester 2. Pelayanan-pelayanan yang Tuhan percayakan kepada saya itu tidak mudah. Ada banyak masalah yang saya hadapi, baik itu dari asrama, tempat pelayanan, maupun kampus. Kalau bukan karena kekuatan Tuhan, mungkin saya tidak mampu. Namun, Tuhan Yesus baik, Dia memberi pertolongan saat saya benar-benar tidak mampu menjalaninya. Saya pelayanan di Gereja Bethel Tabernakel, Karanganyar. Saya mulai melayani di sana sejak Agustus 2014 sampai saat ini. Saya dipercaya untuk melayani di beberapa bagian, seperti melayani anak-anak sekolah minggu, pemuda/remaja, jemaat dewasa, maupun yang sudah lanjut usia. Selain itu, saya juga ambil bagian dalam musik, yaitu melatih anak-anak sekolah minggu belajar musik. Selain itu, saya juga diberi kesempatan oleh pendeta saya untuk membuka Bimbingan Belajar di Bibis Luhur Solo. Sewaktu kuliah, saya ditempatkan praktik tahunan di Gereja Kristus Rahmani Indonesia (GKRI), Jimbaran Bali. Tantangan yang saya hadapi adalah saya melayani orang-orang Kristen yang sudah berkeluarga, tetapi belum terikat dalam pernikahan. Saya juga membantu mengajar di PAUD Shinam, Jimbaran, milik gereja tersebut. Saya bersyukur untuk semua pelayanan yang telah dipercayakan gereja kepada saya. Saya bisa menjalani semua ini dengan pertolongan Tuhan. Yang saya rindukan dalam pelayanan adalah saya bisa memberikan yang terbaik untuk Tuhan dan gereja, menjadi berkat bagi banyak orang, dan tetap setia terhadap panggilan Tuhan. Saya juga rindu suatu saat saya bisa membuka pelayanan sendiri. Saya tahu itu tidak mudah, tetapi saya percaya kuasa pertolongan Tuhan nyata bagi saya. Kiranya kesaksian ini bisa menjadi berkat bagi semua orang, dan saya rindu kita tetap percaya bahwa segala sesuatu yang kita lakukan untuk Tuhan tidak akan kembali dengan sia-sia, melainkan Dia akan memberkati kita senantiasa (Kolose 3:23). Mulailah mengatakan bahwa pelayanan itu adalah sebuah kehormatan, bukan beban. Tuhan Yesus memberkati. "Dan, Maria berkata, "Sesungguhnya, aku ini hamba Tuhan. Terjadilah padaku seperti yang engkau katakan itu." Kemudian, malaikat itu pergi meninggalkannya."(Lukas 1:38, AYT)

p style="margin-bottom:1em;">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。我今年 23 岁。我来自一个基督徒家庭。我是五个兄弟姐妹中的老大。我的家庭以前并不和谐。我的父母经常吵架。

然而，当我上小学四年级时，我父亲真心悔改，并前往位于Pematang Siantar的Purbasari圣经学校接受装备。毕业后，他最终被任命为牧师，而我从小学五年级开始就在锡安荣耀教会担任独奏乐手。

2013 年，当我高中毕业时，我希望能在棉兰的北苏门答腊大学 (USU) 上大学。然而，在参加全国统一高考（SBMPTN）时，我因为没有通过选拔而落榜了。最后，我父亲建议我去梭罗上大学，因为他有一位牧师朋友，他的孩子也在梭罗上大学。我听从了父亲的意愿，因为他希望我能成为神的仆人。

最后，我在梭罗的生命福音神学院（STT Berita Hidup）上学，并参加了该校的所有活动，遵守了该校的所有规定。我在读高一的时候受洗。起初，我因为父母和逃避现实的原因而就读于生命信息神学院，但最终我在第二学期时悔改并真心信靠主耶稣。

神托付给我的服侍并不容易。我面临着很多问题，无论是来自宿舍、事工场所还是校园。如果不是因为上帝的力量，我可能无法做到。然而，主耶稣是良善的，当我已经实在无法承受时，祂会伸出援手。我在卡朗亚尔的伯特利会幕教会（Gereja Bethel Tabernakel）服侍。

我从 2014 年 8 月开始在那里服侍，至今仍在继续。我受托在几个部门服侍，例如服侍主日学儿童、青年/青少年、成年会众以及老年人。此外，我还参与音乐方面的工作，即指导主日学儿童学习音乐。

此外，我的牧师还给了我机会，在梭罗的Bibis Luhur开设学习辅导班。在大学期间，我被安排在巴厘岛金巴兰的印度尼西亚基督慈悲教会（GKRI）进行年度实习。我面临的挑战是我要服侍那些已经有家庭但尚未缔结婚姻的基督徒。

我还协助在属于该教会的金巴兰 Shinam 幼儿教育中心（PAUD Shinam）进行教学。我感谢教会将所有这些事工托付给我。在神的帮助下，我能够做到这一切。我在侍奉中渴望的是，我能够为上帝和教会尽我所能，成为许多人的祝福，并始终忠于上帝的呼召。

我也希望有一天我能自己开办一间教会。我知道这并不容易，但我相信上帝的帮助对我来说是真实的。愿这个见证能成为所有人的祝福，我希望我们能继续相信，我们为神所做的一切都不会徒劳无功，祂必会永远赐福于我们（歌罗西书 3:23）。

开始说服自己，服侍是一种荣誉，而不是一种负担。愿主耶稣赐福。 “马利亚说：‘我是主的使女。愿照你的话成就在我身上。” 天使就离开她去了。”（路加福音 1:38，AYT）

content: Santo Toribio y León XIV: los caminos de la palabra y la acción de fe Chimbote en Línea.- La elección de León XIV trajo la mirada de la Iglesia universal hacia el Perú. No solo porque Robert Francis Prevost desarrolló gran parte de su ministerio sacerdotal y episcopal en nuestro país, sino porque su estilo pastoral parece inscribirse en una tradición que hunde sus raíces en una de las figuras más extraordinarias de la historia de América: Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo. Cuatro siglos después de su muerte, el legado del gran arzobispo de Lima continúa ofreciendo claves para comprender una forma de ejercer el liderazgo eclesial basada en la cercanía, el diálogo, la evangelización, la comunicación activa y el respeto por la dignidad de todos los pueblos. En la historia de la Iglesia abundan teólogos, intelectuales y administradores brillantes. Son menos frecuentes los hombres capaces de transformar instituciones recorriendo caminos. Santo Toribio perteneció a esta última categoría. Nombrado arzobispo de Lima en 1579 por el papa Gregorio XIII, llegó a una jurisdicción inmensa que comprendía buena parte de Sudamérica. Su desafío era monumental. El territorio presentaba enormes dificultades geográficas, poblaciones dispersas y profundas diferencias culturales. Frente a esa realidad, Toribio tomó una decisión que marcaría para siempre su ministerio: salir al encuentro de las personas. Los estudios de los historiadores de la Iglesia, Rubén Vargas Ugarte S.J. y José Antonio Benito, así como la documentación conservada por el Arzobispado de Lima y el Dicasterio para las Causas de los Santos, coinciden en señalar que desarrolló extensas visitas pastorales por la costa, los Andes y regiones apartadas del entonces Virreinato del Perú. Aquellas jornadas, realizadas a pie, a caballo o en precarias condiciones, no fueron simples inspecciones administrativas. Constituyeron un método pastoral basado en la escucha y en el conocimiento directo de la realidad. Toribio comprendió algo que conserva plena vigencia en el siglo XXI: la autoridad moral nace del contacto con las personas y no de la distancia respecto de ellas. Ese principio permite entender por qué su figura resulta tan significativa para interpretar la trayectoria de León XIV. Antes de convertirse en pontífice, Robert Prevost desarrolló una intensa labor misionera y pastoral en el Perú. Su trabajo como religioso agustino, posteriormente como obispo de Chiclayo y más adelante como prefecto de la Santa Sede, estuvo caracterizado por una constante cercanía a las comunidades y por una especial atención a las periferias humanas y sociales. Muchos observadores han destacado que su experiencia latinoamericana no fue circunstancial ni académica. Se trató de una inmersión prolongada en la realidad de una región marcada por desafíos sociales y sanitarios complejos (no olvidemos el COVID 19), grandes expresiones de religiosidad popular y una marcada diversidad cultural. Esa experiencia pastoral, forjada en contacto directo con la población, guarda evidentes resonancias con el modelo evangelizador representado por Santo Toribio. La conexión adquiere una dimensión particular en Lambayeque, región que ocupa un lugar singular en la historia de ambos personajes. Fue precisamente en el antiguo pueblo de Zaña donde Santo Toribio falleció el 23 de marzo de 1606 durante una de sus visitas pastorales. El hecho posee una enorme carga simbólica. El arzobispo murió en pleno ejercicio de su misión, lejos de cualquier comodidad y dedicado a la atención espiritual de sus fieles. Sus restos reposaron inicialmente en Zaña antes de ser trasladados a Lima. Aquella primera sepultura constituye uno de los lugares más significativos de la memoria católica peruana. En ella permanece representada una idea fundamental: la santidad entendida como servicio. No deja de resultar significativo que siglos después esa misma región fuera escenario de buena parte de la labor episcopal de quien llegaría a convertirse en León XIV. Lambay

content: Cuando el 8 de mayo de 2025, el cardenal estadounidense Robert Prevost salió al balcón central de la Basílica de San Pedro convertido en el Papa León XIV era un desconocido para el gran público, incluso para muchos en Perú, donde pasó buena parte de su vida sacerdotal. Ese día, el periodista peruano Santiago Roncagliolo, quien admitió que hasta ese momento no tenía "ni la más remota idea" de quien era el nuevo jefe de la Iglesia católica, recibió el encargo de escribir un libro sobre él. "Lo único que sabía es que había sido misionero", confesó. No obstante, asumió la encomienda porque "consideraba que podía aportar algo diferente que un corresponsal en el Vaticano". "Si había una historia, yo podía contarla, por lo menos podría contar una parte que no están contando los grandes medios", agregó. El resultado es El pastor y los lobos, un libro fruto de más de un año de investigación. Para escribirlo, Roncagliolo recorrió las zonas de Perú donde Prevost desarrolló su labor pastoral y entrevistó a decenas de personas que lo conocieron. La obra se asemeja más a un thriller policial que a la biografía de un religioso, y está entrelazada con la propia infancia y juventud del autor. El escritor de El accidente, Y líbranos del mal y La pena máxima habló con BBC Mundo antes de su participación en el Hay Festival de Arequipa, que se celebró del 5 al 8 de noviembre, y a pocos días de que León XIV visite Perú desde este miércoles y hasta el 16 de noviembre. —Este libro contiene dos biografías al mismo tiempo, no solo la del Papa, sino también la suya. ¿Por qué decidió enfocar este trabajo así? —Bueno, tenía que explicar por qué el Papa existe. ¿Por qué es importante? ¿Por qué 1.400 millones de personas escuchan a alguien que no les cobra impuestos, que no tiene un ejército, que no tiene una autoridad directa? Y la única manera de explicarlo era acudiendo a mi propia experiencia, cuando yo era un niño con educación católica que sufría violencia dentro de su familia, que sufría violencia en el país y cómo esa fe se convirtió en un escudo contra el miedo, contra el dolor y en una fuente de sentido para un adolescente completamente perdido, como lo fui. La oferta de un padre, que es lo que ofrece la Iglesia católica, es muy atractiva para las personas que tuvimos relaciones violentas, difíciles con nuestros modelos paternos. —¿Por qué este Papa en particular? ¿Fue simplemente porque había sido misionero en Perú y luego obispo de Chiclayo? —En este caso me llamaba la atención que este Papa que se forma en Perú, en la teología de la liberación, tiene una aproximación al cristianismo como con la que yo había crecido. Una teoría que resalta que Dios, que Cristo no era un emperador ni un rico, sino que era el hijo de un carpintero, que fue perseguido por un imperio, que fue refugiado, fue torturado y finalmente asesinado. Más parecido a los guerrilleros que a los papas. En ese sentido, esta historia tenía que ver con lo que yo mismo había aprendido que era Dios y me parecía que había una historia, porque en países como España, donde vivo, mucha gente asocia a la Iglesia con el franquismo y yo más bien crecí con curas que eran bastante subversivos. Contar eso me parecía bastante interesante. —El pastor y los lobos deja una doble imagen de León XIV. Por un lado, la de un religioso que busca acercar la Iglesia a los fieles y que se preocupa por sus condiciones materiales. Por otro, la de una suerte de agente especial del Vaticano enviado para depurar la Iglesia de sacerdotes implicados en abusos, corrupción e incluso vínculos con sicarios. ¿Se esperaba esas dos facetas de este hombre? —No, mi principal preocupación era que podía no haber ninguna historia. Podía encontrarme con un sacerdote que se pasó todos los domingos dando homilías y que a lo mejor no había hecho nada en su vida y llegó a ser Papa por cuestiones burocráticas.
